college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Investigation of issues in the design of modern microprocessors, with an in-depth treatment of current research topics in the field.  The course is driven by the discussion of seminal papers in the fields.

title: Advanced Computer Networks
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Graduate level course on computer networking. The course will consist of a taught component, as well as a term project component. The taught component of the course will focus on advanced networking topics by studying a combination of classic research papers as well as current and emerging topics in computer networking. Term projects will be expected to address a significant networking problem and to form the basis for a possible conference/workshop paper or poster submission. Project will be chosen from a wide range of networking related optics and can include analysis, measurement, simulation or implementation. As such the course is suitable for Masters and PhD students wishing to explore or engage in networking related research.

title: Advanced Computer-Aided Construction
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: This course offers an in-depth exploration of various state-of-the-art software packages and emerging technologies in the area of construction engineering and management. Students will engage with advanced methods to manage, monitor and coordinate various steps of construction projects. Key topics include using photogrammetry and LiDAR technologies for modeling and analysis of built environment, advanced topics in Building Information Modeling, proper use of emerging technologies to navigate through and coordinate construction projects and applications of Augmented Reality and Virtual Reality (AR and VR) in construction. While the theoretical knowledge in those areas will be briefly discussed, the course is more focused on practical applications of commercially available technologies and software packages.

title: Advanced Computer-Aided Manufacturing
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Advanced topics in computer-aided manufacturing. Applications of computers to planning and control of manufacturing systems.

title: Advanced Computer-Aided Structural Analysis
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Special topics in the analysis and design of structural systems using computers. Procedures for determining dynamic response, structural buckling, and P-Delta effects. Three dimensional and solid geometric modeling on the computer.

title: Advanced Concepts in Pathophysiology
description: An advanced course in pathophysiology that explores the mechanisms underlying disease or altered body functioning. Emphasis is placed on multiple health problems with attention to underlying genetic, immune, and inflammatory mechanisms. Epidemiology and clinical manifestations are integrated throughout. In addition to core content, specialty tracks include critical care, pediatrics, and gerontology foci. For RN-BSN students only.

title: Advanced Conditioning and Research
description: An advanced study of current cross-training methods for dancers concentrating on strength building and stretching. Student will be responsible for research and introduction of materials in class.

title: Advanced Conduction Heat Transfer
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Fourier's law of conduction, heat diffusion equations, analytical and numerical solutions of multiple-dimensional, steady- and unsteady-conduction heat transfer, and approximate solutions of heat conduction problems.

title: Advanced Construction Materials
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Advanced material characterization using theories of elasticity, visco-elasticity, and fracture mechanics. Study of particulate, non-homogenous, and composite materials including aggregates, Portland cement concrete, and asphalt concrete with application to construction. Include evaluation of testing procedures and modeling.

title: Advanced Construction Project Management
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: This advanced construction project management course focuses on management-driven approaches to large-scale construction projects, emphasizing the ability to navigate and simplify overwhelming complexities, including task, social, cultural, operational, and cognitive challenges. Unlike process-driven frameworks, the course applies a descriptive management model to analyze the impact of engineering tasks, management functions, and cultural dimensions. Students will develop strategies for effective leadership and project execution in complex construction environments.

title: Advanced Consumer Behavior II
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: Ph.D. students only. Applied course in interpretive consumer research. Interpretation of primary and secondary tests, including field notes, literature, film, and video sources. Interpretive research project in either micro or macro consumer behavior.

title: Advanced Contemporary Art and Architecture
description: Graduate-level study of contemporary developments in the visual arts and architecture with emphasis on the various possible interpretations of installations, inter-media works, sit-specific sculpture, responses to the environment and electronic imaging. Culturally-diverse artistic expressions and work by contemporary women artists will be examined.

title: Advanced Content area Literacy Instruction
description: The purpose of this graduate-level course is to develop an in-depth understanding of the research findings, issues, principles, and practices related to exemplary, research-based literacy teaching in the content areas. The course will prepare teachers to provide every student with meaningful and engaging opportunities to learn high-level skills through reading, writing, listening, and speaking while working with multimodal sources and multisensory strategies in the K-12 curriculum, with particular emphasis on using data to plan and deliver differentiated literacy instruction across the curriculum. Participants will also evaluate texts in various content areas to plan for cultural and linguistic diversity while creating a positive, literacy-rich learning environment in which all students can thrive

title: Advanced Convection Heat Transfer
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Analytical derivation of laws governing forced convection heat transfer. Laminar tube flows, laminar boundary layer flows, turbulent tube flows, turbulent boundary layers. Principal of superposition, and arbitrarily specified temperature and heat flux boundary conditions. Analytic integral boundary layer solutions. Numerical and analytic differential equation solutions. Natural and mixed convection. Variable properties. High-speed flows.

title: Advanced Corporate Finance
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: An advanced course on recent theoretical developments and empirical evidence pertaining to corporate finance. Topics can include: financial policy and capital structure (security design, financial distress, behavioral aspects, dynamics); payout policy (dividends, repurchases); capital raising (equity and debt markets, IPOs, SEOs, private placements, bank lending, venture capital, private equity); financial intermediation; investment policy (decision rules, internal capital markets, corporate diversification); internal corporate governance and organization design (agency, catering, executive compensation, boards and directors, managerial myopia, culture); corporate control (ownership structure, voting, takeovers and the market for corporate control, regulation ); managerial labor markets (career concerns, tournaments, learning); other external governance (product markets, rating agencies, regulators, legal rules); event study methods; behavioral corporate finance; and legal traditions, law, and finance.

title: Advanced Corporate Finance
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: The purpose of the course is to give you a framework for thinking about how a firm should make investment and financing decisions to create value for its shareholders. At the end of this course you should be able to understand corporate securities, security issuance, and major securities markets; understand important corporate decisions, such as real options, IPOs, corporate payout decisions, capital structure decisions, and M&As; understand how corporate financing decisions impact the value of the firm and the effect of financing issues on investment decisions and apply the methodologies learned in this class (e.g., research literature, do corporate event studies) to real-world problems.

title: Advanced Corporate Finance
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: Unlock the secrets to driving corporate success with our dynamic course on investment and financing decisions. By the end of this journey, you will be equipped to:1.        Master Corporate Securities: Explore the intricacies of corporate security issuance, and navigate major securities markets with confidence.2.        Strategize Corporate Decisions: Gain deep insights into crucial corporate maneuvers, including real options, IPOs, corporate payouts, capital structure strategies, and mergers & acquisitions.3.        Impact Firm Value: Understand the profound effects of corporate financing decisions on a firm’s value and learn how these choices shape investment outcomes.4.        Apply Real-World Methodologies: Put theory into practice by leveraging cutting-edge methodologies and conducting corporate event studies to solve real-world business challenges.

title: Advanced Corporate Research
college: LW - S.J. Quinney College of Law
description: Corporate Legal Research is an advanced legal research course that introduces students to specific sources and strategies for researching a variety of business law topics, including corporations, securities, and commercial bankruptcy and reorganization.  The course is designed to present students interested in transactional legal practice with the types of issues they may face in their practices, and introduces the resources available to lawyers to respond to their clients' needs.  We expect to cover key primary and secondary sources for business law research:  statutes, regulations, and other administrative materials; subject-specific secondary sources; company disclosure documents; and sources for factual company research, among others.  The course will emphasize research process, strategies, and evaluation of print and online sources in a changing information environment.

title: Advanced Corporate Taxation
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: Focus is the federal income taxation of C corporations and their shareholders. The course covers the formation of corporations, taxation of regular and stock dividends, taxation of redemptions, tax impact of liquidations on corporations and shareholders, tax-free reorganizations, etc. In addition to C corporations, a significant focus is S corporations. Topics covered in this course provide a solid foundation for the tax portion of the Regulation section of the CPA examination.

title: Advanced Counseling: Theory & Skills
description: This course will build upon the theory and skills from the course, Introduction to Counseling. In this advanced course, students will demonstrate the ability to write a psychosocial and treatment plan. It will also focus on the development of advanced skills and techniques such as screening, creating treatment plans and understanding use of self at the advanced level of practice.

title: Advanced Creative Advocacy Lab
college: LW - S.J. Quinney College of Law
description: Students who have completed one semester of Creative Advocacy Lab may enroll as advanced students in subsequent semesters. This opportunity is reserved for Creative Advocacy Lab students whose learning and advocacy goals align with a community partner’s need to design legal informational resources. The credit load for each student will be set in advance of the semester based on the scope, nature, and goals of the project each student will undertake. Enrollment is subject to an application process and faculty approval. Students may enroll for only one semester at a time. Subsequent semesters require an additional application and faculty approval.

title: Advanced Culture Studies
description: This course trains students in basic cross-cultural awareness then places students in communities with indigenous and/or agrarian families. The purpose of this course is to develop understanding of another culture as well as to highlight the student's home culture and privilege, without judgement, ultimately becoming more self-aware as a global citizen. This immersion in a locally sustainable family setting also illuminates human ecology issues and political issues relate to power. The course looks at the benefits and pitfalls of ecotourism, using a systems approach to look at sustainable tourism in international settings. The sustainability model includes the triple bottom line of ecological, economic, and social sustainability with humans as an integral part of the ecosystem.

title: Advanced Curriculum Design in Health Professions Education
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course will build off of our previous work in the Foundations of Curriculum Design and Evaluation course and apply these concepts through an advanced lens. This advanced course will focus on curricular design with attention to clinical curriculum design, mission-based programming, the changing technological environment of education, and interprofessional education.

title: Advanced Curriculum Theory
description: Focuses on exploring current thinking in the area of cultural marxist, feminist, and post-modern theories of curriculum. For each tradition we will explore the roots, assumptions, & implications in order to compare and contrast the traditions. Finally, this course should enable students to position themselves within these theoretical frameworks.

title: Advanced Cyber Pedagogy
description: This course is a 2-credit, half-semester course. It provides an opportunity to develop advanced online teaching and course design skills. This course introduces enhanced online teaching/learning tools, resources, concepts, and challenges. Students will revise and upgrade a preexisting online courses, investigate relevant online learning topics and issues, and develop strategies for assessing online courses and student learning.

title: Advanced Dance Improvisation
description: This course is designed to offer advanced experience with improvisational studies, including learning to design and lead improvisation activities. Students develop individual expression and movement creation through improvisational structures, practice, and forms.

title: Advanced Data Management
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: This course covers issues, methods and applications of large-scale database systems. Topics include administration and management of database, data warehouse and ERP systems, advanced SQL programming, distributed, multimedia and web data management as well as optimization of query processing, ETL and storage management.

title: Advanced Data Mining
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: This course covers advanced data and web mining methods and software tools for customer segmentation, recommendations, personalization, fraud detection, time series analysis, social network analysis as well as web content matching and extraction. Special attention will be given to imbalanced data mining, cost-oriented classification and privacy-preserving data mining issues and methods. Students will collect and analyze real world data using available data mining software or programming tools.

title: Advanced Database Systems
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Graduate-level course on the design and implementation of (relational) database system kernels, as well as other large-scale data management techniques. Reviews the relational data model (including relational algebra) and relational query language: SQL. Examines in depth file organization, database storage, indexing and hashing, query evaluation and optimization, transaction processing, concurrency control and recovery, database integrity and security (if schedule allows). In addition to the study of relational database kernels, this course also investigates latest development in other large-scale data management techniques, e.g., streaming algorithms, the MapReduce framework (in particular, the Hadoop system), and other IO efficient techniques (if time permits). Students will participate in a semester-long project and build a mini-database system by implementing several core modules in a relational database system. There might also be projects on other large scale data management techniques, such as sketching, MapReduce-based projects, etc., if time allows. In summary, this course is about the principles of designing and implementing database kernels, as well as other relevant large data management techniques. Please note that this is NOT a course on building database applications and introduction to database systems, i.e., we will not cover in this course how to build a database application (e.g., ER design, schema refinement, functional dependency, and database application development). Such topics will be covered in CS 5530.

title: Advanced Deductive Logic
description: Various advanced topics in deductive logic such as proof theory and model theory, set theory, modal logic, metalogic, e.g. completeness, and computability.

title: Advanced Dental Radiology
description: This will be a lecture/hands-on lab that provides an understanding of dental radiographic theory, anatomy, pathology, equipment and techniques which will enable participants to appropriately prescribe, acquire and interpret diagnostic radiographic images.  Students will learn the basic principles of CBCT and other advanced imaging modalities. They will expand their radiographic interpretation capability and develop diagnosis and treatment planning skills through experience with clinical cases. Among the CBCT applications covered will be implant planning, TMJ, paranasal sinuses, periodontal evaluation, airway studies, and endodontic challenges. Students will learn how to select the right equipment for their future offices and when to refer imaging studies for specialty consultation.

title: Advanced Desert Backpacking
description: Must have previous backpack experience and able to hike 10 mile per day. Students will explore advanced hiking techniques and back country travel strategies for the desert environment. This course will include discussions regarding resource management issues, activity skills, risk management, and environmental ethics associated with backpacking on public lands. Competency in fundamental camping skills, hiking skills, outdoor cooking, travel techniques, Leave no Trace skills are required.

title: Advanced Design
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Offered by arrangement with a professor. Complex chemical-process problems of interest to students; analysis, synthesis, and optimization.

title: Advanced Design Research Methods
description: This course delves into design research methodologies, emphasizing the study and application of techniques to investigate and understand design challenges. Students will explore various qualitative and quantitative research methods to gather insights about users, contexts, and systems. The focus will be critically developing and analyzing research findings to inform design decisions.

title: Advanced Design Studies
description: This course builds on the Design Studies Survey and explores advanced topics in design discourse and consideration of the built environment. Students engage in reading, writing, and class discussion about design and develop their own research questions regarding designed objects and material culture.

title: Advanced Design: Petroleum Engineering Project
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Capstone project in petroleum engineering with topic to be approved by student's supervisory committee.

title: Advanced Digital Photography
description: Digital Technology has affected every aspect of the photographic process. Historically, new tools have lead to new forms of expression. Using tools learned in the preceding classes, students will explore visual issues unique to digital photography. Students will develop their personal vision and explore extended possibilities of the medium through a series of projects based on questions about the nature of contemporary photography. This class also explores technologies (such as video and 3D computer modeling ) that are new to contemporary fine arts photography. This class assumes that students are well grounded in technical skills and are prepared to use digital tools to explore aesthetic issues and advanced concepts.

title: Advanced Digital Photography
description: Digital Technology has affected every aspect of the photographic process. Historically, new tools have lead to new forms of expression. Using tools learned in the preceding classes, students will explore visual issues unique to digital photography. Students will develop their personal vision and explore extended possibilities of the medium through a series of projects based on questions about the nature of contemporary photography. This class assumes that students are well grounded in technical skills and are prepared to use digital tools to explore aesthetic issues and advanced concepts.

title: Advanced Digital Product
description: Advanced methods and processes for digital product design.

title: Advanced Digital Signal Processing I
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Project-oriented class on advanced topics of current interest in signal processing. Examples of topics include image compression, nonlinear signal processing, active noise control, blind deconvolution, and equalization.

title: Advanced Digital Signal Processing I
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Project-oriented class on advanced topics of current interest in signal processing. Examples of topics include image compression, nonlinear signal processing, active noise control, blind deconvolution, and equalization.

title: Advanced Digital Signal Processing II
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Project-oriented class on advanced topics of current interest in signal processing. Examples of topics include image compression, nonlinear signal processing, active noise control, blind deconvolution, and equalization.

title: Advanced Digital Signal Processing II
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Meets with ECE 7641. Project-oriented class on advanced topics of current interest in signal processing. Examples of topics include image compression, nonlinear signal processing, active noise control, blind deconvolution, and equalization.

title: Advanced Digital VLSI Systems Design
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: This course addresses advanced issues in VLSI design, covering the following topics: design methodologies and IP design, CMOS circuit scaling, advanced logic circuit styles, noise sources and signal integrity in digital design, design techniques for dynamic and static power reduction, power supply issues, interconnect analysis, clocking and synchronization, process variation, and performance verification.  Students are expected to complete a substantial design project as part of the course, which involves extensive use of CAD tools.

title: Advanced Digital VLSI Systems Design
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: This course addresses advanced issues in VLSI design, covering the following topics: design methodologies and IP design, CMOS circuit scaling, advanced logic circuit styles, noise sources and signal integrity in digital design, design techniques for dynamic and static power reduction, power supply issues, interconnect analysis, clocking and synchronization, process variation, and performance verification.  Students are expected to complete a substantial design project as part of the course, which involves extensive use of CAD tools.

title: Advanced Direct Practice I
description: Introduces students to theories, models, and interventions used in advanced clinical practice and which are referred to in our school as the Four Forces of psychology.  Assessment at this level of direct practice becomes more comprehensive using a combined ecosystems (outer forces)/ constructivist-developmental(inner forces), bio/psycho/social/spiritual paradigm.  Application to direct work with both individuals and groups is the focus of experiential components of this course.

title: Advanced Direct Practice II: Couples and Families
description: A second-year course related to advanced clinical practice with couples and families.  Theories evolving from marital and family therapy are introduced as aids in understanding the complexity of family systems with both their strengths and dysfunctional aspects.  The developmental levels of individuals within a given client-system is considered a key element in assessment that helps the practitioner to determine effective interventions for a couple or family within its own developmental stage as a system.  Application to direct work with couples and families is the focus of experiential components of the course.

title: Advanced Directing
description: An examination of diverse directing styles both contemporary and historical including non-realistic and non-western approaches to the craft of directing.

title: Advanced Discovery
college: LW - S.J. Quinney College of Law
description: This course covers discovery strategy and best practices in litigation, including the procedural and ethical rules governing discovery in criminal and civil cases; location of electronic and other records; collection of records; preservation and spoliation; e-discovery techniques and processes; encryption; and the technologies, tools and platforms used in identifying and handling evidence.

title: Advanced Discussion of Social Aspects
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: The combination of CS 5050/5051 is appropriate for students who have a graduate-level background in issues related to the social aspects of computing (e.g., intellectual property or electronic commerce).

title: Advanced Doctoral Pro-seminar
description: This seminar will help prepare you for professional life after the dissertation.  We will explore the multiple options that are open to you and by the end of this proseminar we will hopefully have answered the long lingering question: "So, what are you going to do with that doctorate?"

title: Advanced Documentary Filmmaking
description: An advanced course in non-fiction film production that teaches professional skills necessary for each student to produce and direct a short professional documentary suitable for a thesis project, broadcast, film festivals, or job applications. Special attention is placed on individual student projects from inception, to research and development, production, and post-production. Documentary directors will also focus on ethical issues, fundraising, and distribution.

title: Advanced Dramatic Theory
description: An examination of genres and modes of theoretical analysis.

title: Advanced Dramaturgy
description: Approaches to directing verse drama. Analysis and preparation of verse scenes, and workshop productions of full length verse plays.

title: Advanced Dynamic Meteorology
description: Advanced topics in geophysical fluid dynamics: Atmospheric waves, baroclinic and frontal instability, observation and theory of the general circulation, middle atmospheric dynamics, tropical dynamics, and dynamical oceanography.

title: Advanced Dynamical Systems
description: Basic abstract dynamics; stable, unstable, center manifold theory; index theories; KAM theory; chaos; dimensions of attractors; forced oscillations; applications.

title: Advanced Dynamics of Addiction - Evaluation & Treatment Planning
description: Meet with SW 721. Core course defining the principles in comprehensive addictive and dual diagnosis. Examines psychological Development at an advanced level looking at deviations that lead to personality vulnerability to addictive behaviors. Will include treatment planning, definition of scope of practice and advanced ethics.

title: Advanced Dynamics of Structures
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: The course presents analytical methods for multiple degree of freedom dynamic structural systems; topics include inelastic design spectrum; Rayleigh's method for natural vibration frequency; Lagrange's equation of motion; static condensation method; orthogonality of vibration modes; classical dumping; modal damping matrices; displacement superposition method; modal response contributions, modal expansion of excitation vector; modal equations and responses; response spectrum analysis; time stepping methods including Newmark's method and Wilson's method; influence of period and beam-to-column stiffness ratio on modal contribution factors; allowable ductility and ductility demand; base isolated buildings; structural dynamics in the building codes; comparison of building codes; and displacement-based design using elastic and inelastic design spectra.

title: Advanced Dynamics, Vibrations, and Wave Propagation
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Lagrange methods and Euler's equations, Hamilton's principle. Free and forced vibration of single- and multi-degree of freedom systems. Free and forced vibration of strings, beams and membranes. Traveling and standing waves, reflection, and generation of waves.

title: Advanced Early Modern Philosophy
description: Intensive study of significant themes in modern or recent philosophy or of the connections, contrasts, or debates between important figures in modern or recent philosophy. For juniors and seniors.

title: Advanced Early Modern Philosophy
description: Intensive study of significant themes in modern or recent philosophy or of the connections, contrasts, or debates between important figures in modern or recent philosophy.

title: Advanced EAS Communication Skills
description: An integrated-skills course designed to improve reading, writing, speaking, and listening through note-taking, writing and revision of expository papers, and making class presentations.

title: Advanced EAS Communication Skills for Graduate Students
description: An advanced integrated-skills course designed to improve reading, writing, and listening skills through note-taking, writing short essays, and giving oral lectures and presentations in class.

title: Advanced Ecology
description: Advanced treatment in central topics in modern ecology; population growth and regulation, competition, predation, herbivory, mutualisms, stability, and diversity of communities.

title: Advanced Ecology Lab
description: Field and classroom laboratory demonstrating ecological principles such as populations growth and regulation, competition, predation, herbivory, mutualisms, stability, and diversity of communities.

title: Advanced Economic Theory
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: Drawing on the concepts from the first year microeconomics and game theory courses, the advanced theory course will apply the tools of choice under uncertainty, equilibrium analysis, contract theory and mechanism design to topics of interest in Economics and Business disciplines. Beyond exploring important applications, and links to the data, students will begin to develop sensitivity to behavioral assumptions and robustness of results to informational assumptions. Students will be expected to work through theory papers close to the frontier of economics and business and tackle deeper analytic exercises.

title: Advanced Education Law
description: Examination of legal principles and laws affecting the administration and management of schools with emphasis upon system level concerns, and an analysis of current legal issues.

title: Advanced Educational Policy Analysis
description: Students in our PhD program need an advanced educational policy course to further theiracademic knowledge in educational policy analysis and enable them to conduct complexanalysis of P-20 educational policy for their dissertation work.

title: Advanced Electricity and Magnetism
description: This is a formal-theoretical development of classical electrodynamics. It will build on material mastered in previous core courses (e.g., PHYS 4010 - Electromagnetism and Quantum Mechanics). The course will go deeper into curvilinear coordinates, electric and magnetic fields in matter, Maxwell's equations in matter, electromagnetic waves, Green's function method of electromagnetic waves, guided waves, antennae, potential formulation, retarded potential, Lagrangian formalism of special relativity and relativistic electrodynamics.

title: Advanced Electro-Acoustic Music Composition I
description: Special fee required. Fundamentals of electronic music composition.

title: Advanced Electro-Acoustic Music Composition II
description: Special fee required. Fundamentals of electronic music composition.

title: Advanced Electromagnetic Fields
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Review of Maxwell's macroscopic equations in integral and differential forms including boundary conditions, power and energy computations, and time-harmonic formulations. Macroscopic-electrical properties of matter. Oblique incidence planewave propagation and polarization in multi-layered media. Separation of variable solutions of the wave equation in rectangular, cylindrical, and spherical coordinates. Vector potential theory and the construction of solutions using Green's theorem. Electromagnetic theorems of duality, uniqueness, reciprocity, reaction, and source equivalence. Waveguide, cavity, antenna, and scattering applications in rectangular, cylindrical, and spherical geometries.

title: Advanced Electromagnetic Fields
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Review of Maxwell's macroscopic equations in integral and differential forms including boundary conditions, power and energy computations, and time-harmonic formulations. Macroscopic-electrical properties of matter. Oblique incidence planewave propagation and polarization in multi-layered media. Separation of variable solutions of the wave equation in rectangular, cylindrical and spherical coordinates. Vector potential theory and the construction of solutions using Green's theorem. Electromagnetic theorems of duality, uniqueness, reciprocity, reaction, and source equivalence. Waveguide, cavity, antenna, and scattering applications in rectangular, cylindrical, and spherical geometries.

title: Advanced Electron Microscopy for Semiconductors
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: This course covers both the theory and practical use of modern electron microscopy for semiconductor materials and devices. It assumes basic knowledge of semiconductors, but much of the necessary material will be covered. The course begins with the principle of electron microscopy, proceed to the description of conventional and advanced modern technique, and evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of each method. Metrologies for semiconductors devices are then introduced, including energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), electron beam induced current (EBIC), and cathodoluminescence (CL), to study active defects, junction interfaces, and excess carrier dynamics of the devices. About 30 % of the class time will be held in labs for demos and system operation sessions. Extra work (e.g., simulations) is required of those who registered in the 6000 level.

title: Advanced Electrophysiology
description: Anatomical and physiologic components of the peripheral and central auditory pathways as related to generation of evoked potentials; current electrophysiologic systems, administration and interpretation of electrophysiologic tests; assessment of electrophysiologic function of the auditory system across the age span of infants, children and adults.

title: Advanced Embedded Software
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: This is a follow up course in embedded systems, focusing on real-time requirements and reliable systems. The course will cover practical implementation of real-time systems using Real Time Operating Systems (RTOS). Topics covered include: timing requirements, low power modes and energy efficiency, concurrency, distributed communication using CAN bus, system testing and verification.

title: Advanced Embedded Systems
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: This is a follow up course in embedded systems, focusing on real-time requirements and reliable systems. The course will cover practical implementation of real-time systems using Real Time Operating Systems (RTOS). Topics covered include: timing requirements, low power modes and energy efficiency, concurrency, distributed communication using CAN bus, system testing and verification.

title: Advanced Empirical Asset Pricing
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: This is an advanced class on empirical asset pricing. The class will cover recent influential papers in asset pricing and market microstructure.

title: Advanced EMT
description: Expands the EMT-Basic's skills to include advance management of hypoprofusion, airways, and drugs/medications. Utah state certification is possible after successful completion of this class; however, students may take this course for knowledge and experience and not certify.

title: Advanced Energy Systems
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Introduction to advanced energy systems utilizing chemical and nuclear fuels and solar based energy. Assessment of thermodynamic, chemical, and physical factors.

title: Advanced Energy Systems and Grid Modernization
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: This course explores grid modernization with hands-on software development for hardware-in-the-loop projects. Students develop models for grid subsystems, focusing on practical applications and realistic data. Key protocols covered include OCPP 1.6.1/2.0.1 (with improved security in 2.0.1) and OCPI. The course also introduces OpenADR for energy management, emphasizing grid-to-site control. Projects involve charger intelligent load control, basic on-off and curtailment commands, and creating functional EMS using CAISO's real-time price signals. Additionally, it covers smaller building-scale EMS with AI components, including Q-learning, reinforcement learning, and Transformer models to predict energy demands, solar generation, battery degradation, and price signals.

title: Advanced Energy Systems II
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Recent developments in advanced energy systems with emphasis in fuel resources, environmental impacts, risk assessments, regulatory aspects, and economic issues.

title: Advanced Engineering Analysis
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Unified treatment of the equations describing momentum, energy, mass, and population balances. Emphasis is on thinking analytically about solving new problems rather than on finding specific solutions. Problem synthesis and analysis are covered. Specific topics include (1) how to solve classic prototype problems that shed light on the relationship between a physical problem and a mathematical equation; (2) how to use scaling analysis to identify controlling phenomena, and (3) how to make radical approximations to render intractable problems tractable.

title: Advanced Engineering Pysch/Human Factors
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Provides students with an opportunity to apply the knowledge acquired in Psych 3171 or 3172 to real world situations. First half of the class will deepen theoretical knowledge of engineering psychology. Second half uses a combination of service learning and collaborative learning to develop solutions for real world problems at local businesses.

title: Advanced Entrepreneurial Law
college: LW - S.J. Quinney College of Law
description: This course builds on the material covered in Entrepreneurial Law. Students in this course will continue to explore the business and legal components required to successfully transition technology from early conception to out-licensing for commercial development, including the formation of a venture capital-funded entity. Drafting exercises include confidentiality agreements, material transfer agreements, valuations, term sheets, and employment contracts. Topics include leveraged buyouts, private equity, and technology licenses. Counts toward the experiential education requirement. PRE-REQUISITE: Entrepreneurial Law.

title: Advanced Environment and Behavior
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Graduate students should enroll in PSY 6400 or FCS 6620 and they will be held to a higher standard or do additional work. Some sections taught with service learning emphasis; see Bennion Center for details. Study of selected environmental settings and environment and behavior processes.

title: Advanced Environment and Behavior
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Meets with PSY 6400. Graduate students should enroll in a 6000-level section and they will be held to a higher standard or do additional work. Some sections taught with service learning emphasis; see Bennion Center for details. Study of selected environmental settings and environment- and behavior-processes.

title: Advanced Environment and Behavior
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Meets with FCS 5620, FCS 6620, PSYCH 5400, and PSYCH 6400. Graduate students should enroll in a 6000-level section, and they will be held to a higher standard or do additional work.  Some sections taught with service-learning emphasis; see Bennion Center for details.  Study of selected environmental settings and environment and behavior processes.

title: Advanced Environment and Behavior

description: Meets with FCS 5620, FCS 6620, PSYCH 5400, and PSYCH 6400. Graduate students should enroll in a 6000 level section and they will be held to a higher standard or do additional work. Some sections taught with service learning emphasis; see Bennion Center for details. Study of selected environmental settings and environment and behavior processes.

title: Advanced Environmental Economics
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: This is the proposed second course in a new two graduate field, Environmental Economics. This course will introduce students to applying economics to environmental issues.

title: Advanced Environmental Justice Clinic
college: LW - S.J. Quinney College of Law
description: Students who have completed one semester of the Environmental Justice Clinic may enroll as advanced students in subsequent semesters. The credit load for each student will be set in advance of the semester based on the scope, nature, and goals of the project each student will undertake. Enrollment is subject to an application process and faculty approval. Students may enroll for only one semester at a time. Subsequent semesters require an additional application and faculty approval.

title: Advanced Ergonomics: Occupational Biomechanics
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Application of engineering statics and dynamics in determining biomechanical stresses on humans in the work environment; anthropometric measurement methodologies; determination of physiological stresses during work.

title: Advanced Ergonomics: Occupational Biomechanics Laboratory
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Empirical evaluation of biomechanical and physiological stresses on humans in the work environment. Recommended Prerequisite: ME EN 1300 AND ME EN 2080 AND ME EN 6100.

title: Advanced ESL Communication Skills for Graduate Students in Finance
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: An advanced integrated-skills course designed to improve reading, writing, speaking and listening skills through note-taking, writing short essays, and giving oral lectures and presentations in class. Assumptions and interaction practices of the American classroom are emphasized.

title: Advanced Eukaryotic Genetics
description: This course builds upon BIOL 2030, and is designed to give students a deeper understanding of the experimental basis of modern eukaryotic genetics. Topics to be covered include: chromosome recombination and segregation; DNA mutation and repair: gene expression and gene disruption; finding and characterizing mutants; analyzing gene function in time and space; gene interactions and pathways.

title: Advanced Evidence
college: LW - S.J. Quinney College of Law

title: Advanced Evidence Based Practice
description: The purpose of this course is to further develop evidence-based practice skills specific to the role of the advanced practice nurse in clinical decision-making, specifically as they relate to risk/harm assessment, prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment, prognosis, and intervention.

title: Advanced Evidence-Based Practice
description: This course will apply evidence-based practice principles in clinical practice settings. Critical analysis of the levels of evidence supporting various special tests and clinical evaluation skills will be a major component of this course. Throughout this course, students will explore a variety of methods for gathering and generating evidence relevant to clinical practice.

title: Advanced Evidence-Based Practice and Research
description: Required for nursing Master of Science and Doctor of Nursing Practice students to lead the translation of the best available scientific evidence into clinical practice. Students will apply evidence-based competencies to independently search for, appraise, and synthesize research and be prepared to recommend practice changes at the individual and system level based on the strength of the evidence.

title: Advanced Excel and Access Techniques
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: This course explores the more advanced tools in Microsoft Excel and Access that are applicable to the Accounting and Auditing professions. The first ten weeks will cover Excel including, Financial Modeling, Pivot Tables, Advanced Functions, recording Macros and Databases. The last five weeks of the semester will focus on Microsoft Access. In the Access section, students will automate a complete business process including building tables, queries, forms and reports.

title: Advanced EXCEL and Technologies for Accountants
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: This course explores the more advanced tools in Microsoft Excel and other current technologies that are applicable to the accounting profession.

title: Advanced Excel for Finance
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: This course explores the more advanced tools in Microsoft Excel that are applicable to the Finance profession. The course will cover shortcut keys, financial modeling, pivot tables, financial ratios, advanced functions, recording macros and databases. Students will develop advanced Excel skills through a combination of participation in demonstrations of Excel tools and applying the skills they learn by using them to solve real world finance problems using Excel.

title: Advanced Exercise Physiology I
description: Presents fundamentals of the acute human response to physical exercise and activity with respect to bioenergetics and the neuromuscular system. The course focuses on the metabolic substrates and pathways involved in sustaining physical work and the integrated neural and muscular responses necessary for human activity.

title: Advanced Exercise Physiology I
description: Presents fundamentals of the acute human response to physical exercise and activity with respect to bioenergetics and the neuromuscular system. The course focuses on the metabolic substrates and pathways involved in sustaining physical work and the integrated neural and muscular responses necessary for human activity. Practical laboratory experiences will accompany the lectures.

title: Advanced Exercise Physiology I
description: This course will focus on considering how we have come to the current point of understanding of metabolism and muscle physiology.

title: Advanced Exercise Physiology II
description: The demands of exercise present an excellent opportunity to explore the capacity of the cardiovascular and endocrine systems to meet the biologic needs of the body. This class will examine heart, lung, vessel and fluid changes in addition to the various hormonal adjustments that occur to support the increased level of metabolism during various types of muscular work. Concepts addressed in lecture will be reinforced by practical laboratory experiences.

title: Advanced Exercise Physiology II
description: The demands of exercise present an excellent opportunity to explore the capacity of the cardiovascular and endocrine systems to meet the biologic needs of the body. This class will examine heart, lung, vessel and fluid changes in addition to the various hormonal adjustments that occur to support the increased level of metabolism during various types of musuclar work. Concepts addressed in lecture will be reinforced by practical laboratory experiences.

title: Advanced Exercise Physiology II
description: This course is intended to develop an understanding of selected physiological mechanisms underlying the acute responses to dynamic and static exercise. Special emphasis is given to cardiovascular, respiratory, and thermoregulatory functions.

title: Advanced Exercise Physiology II-Lab
description: This laboratory experience is the companion course to ESS 7310. Upon completion of this laboratory the student will have a variety of skills necessary for assessing pulmonary, cardiovascular, and thermoregulatory function during rest and exercise.

title: Advanced Exercise Physiology Laboratory I
description: In this course you will develop skills for utilizing the scientific method.  Dependent variables for experiments in this course require developing laboratory skills related to indirect calorimetry, metabolic measures of exercise efficiency and recovery, carbohydrate, lactate, and lipid metabolism, body composition appraisal, muscle-power tests, and bone health.  You will explore ways to research a topic, perhaps not always familiar to you, and write a partial manuscript citing relevant literature for each experiment.

title: Advanced Exercise Physiology Laboratory I
description: In this course you will develop skills for utilizing the scientific method. Dependent variables for experiments in this course require developing laboratory skills related to indirect calorimetry, metabolic measures of exercise efficiency and recovery, carbohydrate, lactate, and lipid metabolism, body composition appraisal, muscle-power tests, and bone health. You will explore ways to research a topic, perhaps not always familiar to you, and write a partial manuscript citing relevant literature for each experiment.

title: Advanced Exercise Physiology Laboratory II
description: In this course you will further develop skills for utilizing the scientific method. Dependent variables for experiments in this course require developing skills related to blood flow, blood pressure, metabolism, lung function, respiration and work capacity. You will continue to work on the scientific writing skills developed in ESS 6301/7301.

title: Advanced Expository Writing (for EAS Speakers)
description: Emphasis is on writing 7-8 page expository papers with citations.

title: Advanced Familiality Methods
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Introduction to more advanced hypothesis testing of familiality.  Advanced Familiality Methods is taught in the Spring semester provided sufficient demand and at the discretion of the instructor.  For more information, contact Dr. Lisa Cannon-Albright.

title: Advanced Federal Tax Issues
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: This course focuses on tax laws, issues, problems, and planning opportunities facing companies in our current tax environment. Such topics are incorporated in a survey of ASC 740 (Accounting for Income Taxes). A strong, foundational, knowledge of ASC 740 is critical for both tax and audit professionals.

title: Advanced Feminist Theories: Critical Theories and Post-structuralism
college: CT - Sch for Cultural & Social Tran
description: Cross-listed as ENGL 5760 (Criticism) when this topic specified. One of three options to fulfill the required theory core course for Gender studies majors. Feminism no longer signifies (if it ever did) a single theory or methodology. Disagreements about what counts as feminist theory rage within the rapidly shifting borders of feminist discourse even as feminists continue to insist that gender be considered a fundamental category of analysis. Readings focus on theoretical texts that articulate feminism(s) with and against other methodologies and critical issues.

title: Advanced Field Ornithology
description: 14 day intensive field course. Students will study morphological, ecological and behavioral diversity and adaptations of birds across a variety of habitats in the Western U.S. Written exercises will be accomplished during the 2 week period.

title: Advanced Field Practicum I A
description: Application of advanced roles, models, and theories of social work to agency practice; using the generalist perspective.

title: Advanced Field Practicum I B
description: Application of advanced roles, models, and theories of social work to agency practice; using the generalist perspective.

title: Advanced Field Practicum II A
description: Application of advanced roles, models, and theories of social work to agency practice; using the generalist perspective.

title: Advanced Field Practicum III
description: For DCFC Evening cohort only. Students apply advanced roles, models and theories of social work within an agency placement that supports their second-year domain of study. Under the supervision of an approved clinical instructor, students build upon the generalist perspective and increase their skills in ethical, culturally-competent, multi-modal social work practice.

title: Advanced Figure Painting
description: With the human figure as its subject, the class will concentrate on forming and structuring ideas for proper expression of visual literacy.

title: Advanced Film & Philosophy
description: Using advanced material in philosophy and film theory, this course applies film to philosophy and philosophy to film. Subject matter may include philosophy of film, philosophy through film, narration in film, the ontology of film, emotion and film, and the politics of film. The course may also include the theoretical study of various film genres, such as horror, documentary, and Westerns. Students enrolled in 6790 are given assignments appropriate for graduate level work.

title: Advanced Film and Philosophy
description: Using advanced material in philosophy and film theory, this course applies film to philosophy and philosophy to film. Subject matter may include philosophy of film, philosophy through film, narration in film, the ontology of film, emotion and film, and the politics of film. The course may also include the theoretical study of various film genres, such as horror, documentary, and Westerns

title: Advanced Film and Television Acting
description: Continuation of FILM 3860.

title: Advanced Film Animation
description: Production of computer animation films and videos.

title: Advanced Film Production I
description: Techniques of professional film production introduced in year-long sequence course. Equipment provided; however, students must assume film and processing costs.

title: Advanced Film Production II
description: Techniques of professional film production.  The course focuses on film sound, editing, and shooting leading to a completed 16mm film.

title: Advanced Film Production II
description: Techniques of professional film production. The course focuses on film sound, editing, and shooting leading to a completed 16mm film.

title: Advanced Finance
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: The objectives are twofold: to apply corporate financial concepts to case situations; and to introduce more advanced concepts in corporate and investment finance.  Topics include financial statement analysis, forecasting of financial statements, estimation of firms required return, determination of appropriate capital structure, application of risk management, analysis of appropriate dividend policies, economic value-added analysis, and estimation of firm valuation.  The above topics are focused on financial strategies from the prospective of management, lenders, and investors.

title: Advanced Financial Accounting - Acquisitions and Consolidations
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: Corporation acquisitions, mergers and the formation of other strategic alliances are staples of today's business environment. The first two-thirds of this course focus on understanding of the nature and financial reporting aspects of these complex business transactions. Specific topics include accounting for business combinations and the various reporting requirements that lead to consolidated financial statements. The final third of the course covers pass thru entities and governmental entities.

title: Advanced Financial Modeling for Corporate Valuation
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: Forecasting the future cash flows of a company is a common requirement for many finance positions. For example, both corporate executives and lenders want to know whether the firm is generating enough cash to meet its financial obligations. Consultants, investment bankers, and investors use expected future cash flows to estimate the fair value of a company. This course will focus on building standard Excel models for financing and valuation. We will begin with simple models based on historical data and build toward 3-statement models for equity research or for evaluating acquisitions.

title: Advanced Financial Modeling for Investments
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: The course will apply economic theories learned from other courses to solve various problems in financial management and investments. It will take a hands-on approach in building financial spreadsheet models. Microsoft Excel is a primary tool to implement the financial models. The students will have ample examples of numerical and graphical practices on problems that arise in various areas of financial analyses. These include but are not limited to asset return calculations, portfolio theory, index models, the capital asset pricing model and investment performance analysis. The course will also make use of statistics and probability.

title: Advanced Finite Elements
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Applications to problems from solid, heat transfer, and fluid mechanics, and advanced elements. Consideration of nonlinear and time-dependent problems. Students must have the ability to run at least one commercial FEM code or a University of Utah commercial-quality parallel research FEM or FEW-based code; vector calculus; linear algebra; exposure to ordinary and partial differential equations and numerical analysis; ability to program in Matlab, C/C++, Python, Fortran, or other scientific programming language.

title: Advanced First Aid Refresher
description: Allows students who have already taken an advanced first aid class to refresh that information and recertify. Students must have previously taken an advanced first aid class.

title: Advanced Fitness
description: This course will combine advanced weight lighting, sprinting, gymnastics, power lifting, kettlebell training, plyometrics, and medicine ball training each day.

title: Advanced Fluid Mechanics
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Kinematics of flow, stress, strain rate, and vorticity. Derivation of the governing differential equations. Introduction to potential flows. Exact solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations, creeping flow, laminar boundary layers. Introduction to hydrodynamic instability.

title: Advanced Fluid-Solid Reaction Engineering
description: Engineering analysis of chemical reactions between a fluid and solid by combining chemical kinetics with transport phenomena. Application to metallurgical systems. Coupled transport phenomena.

title: Advanced Formal Procedures of the Eighteenth and Nineteenth Centuries I
description: Overview of  several analytical approaches, methodologies, and theories of music of the common-practice period. Primary readings from major theorists as well as secondary readings on a variety of analytical and theoretical topics will serve as an introduction to concepts/theories relating to harmony, tonality, rhythm and meter, and others.

title: Advanced Formal Procedures of the Eighteenth and Nineteenth Centuries II
description: Develops and extends aspects of the theoretical systems and analytical paradigms covered in MUSC 6550 through the close examination of individual works, composers, genres/styles, and/or systems of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. Specific topics will vary.

title: Advanced Formulations and Drug Delivery Systems
description: Basic concepts and rationale of novel and new drug formulations and delivery systems.

title: Advanced Foundation Engineering
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: An in-depth look into the geotechnical and structural aspects of foundation engineering. Topics covered include theories for ultimate bearing capacity, beams on elastic foundations, special footings, mat foundations, lateral earth pressures induced by surcharge loadings, excavation support, arching theory, finite element analyses of sheetpile walls and braced excavations, uplift piles, laterally loaded piles, pile groups, and drilled piers and caissons.

title: Advanced Foundations of Community Education & Social Action
description: Although schools usually take center stage when the topic of education comes up, teaching and learning are not confined by the walls of school buildings. Community centers, grassroots organizations, sports fields, art studios, resettlement agencies, online communities — all of these can be contexts for facilitated educational experiences. The people who work in these spaces may be called teachers but also may go by other names, like youth worker, teaching artist, after-school coordinator, community organizer, or mentor. They continue long traditions in the US and abroad of what is often called “community education.” At its best, community education is rooted in the strengths, cultures, and priorities of particular communities. Not limited by the constraints of traditional school curricula, community education offers a more holistic approach to learning that includes goals related to positive youth development, critical consciousness, community wellbeing, and action for social change. This course introduces the theory and principles of community education and explores the history of community education in the US and abroad. Students will be introduced to an array of different approaches to community education and will have the chance to learn from community-based educators in Salt Lake valley.

title: Advanced French Grammar
description: First course for students who learned the language through residence in a francophone country. Reading and writing as a basis for a systematic review of the syntax, morphology, and lexicon of French.

title: Advanced Game Animation
description: This advanced class builds upon the basic universal principles of animation and physics. The course has a focus on character locomotion and body mechanics. Having completed the initial core studies and exercises, students will have the freedom to explore related topics such as motion capture animation and editing, facial animation, acting, animated shorts, or game engine implementation. Students who successfully complete this course will have created portfolio ready works that show a solid understanding of animation principles.

title: Advanced Game Studio I
description: Students work collaboratively in large teams in the design and development of their master's game project. This course is the first of a two-course sequence that continues in Advanced Game Studio II.

title: Advanced Game Studio II
description: Students work collaboratively in large teams in the design and development of their master's game project. This course is the second course of a two-course sequence that began in Advanced Game Studio I. Students are expected to publish their master's game project as part of this course.

title: Advanced Genetic Epidemiology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Advanced Genetic Epidemiology is an advanced, applied course for graduate students on the Genetic Epidemiology track which includes a 1 hour computer lab.

title: Advanced Genetic Epidemiology: Association
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: An advanced, applied course for graduate students with a strong research focus on genetic epidemiology, and association analysis particularly. Provided sufficient demand, it is taught in the Fall semester. For additional information contact Dr. Nicola Camp. This course is structured as a mixture of lectures, analysis presentations, analysis discussions, paper debates, and computer and analysis labs. The course includes: case-control and family based designs; theoretical aspects and practical analysis exercises using a variety of software; linkage disequilibrium structure; tagging-SNPs; haplotypes and haplotype grouping; meta analyses; sample size, power and significance and multiple testing issues.

title: Advanced Genetic Epidemiology: Association
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: An advanced, applied course for graduate students with a strong research focus on genetic epidemiology, and association analysis particularly.  It comprises 2 hours of lectures per week and a 1 hour lab.  Provided sufficient demand, it is taught in the Fall Semester.  For more information, contact Dr. Nicola Camp.  This course is structured as a mixture of lectures, analysis presentations, analysis discussions, paper debates, and computer and analysis labs.  The course includes: data and file preparation; qualitative and quantitative traits; parametric and non-parametric analyses; case-control and family-based designs; theoretical aspects and practical analysis exercises using a variety of software; linkage disequilibrium structure; tagging-SNPs; haplotypes and haplotype grouping; phylogenetic trees; meta analyses; sample size, power and significance and multiple testing issues.

title: Advanced Genetic Epidemiology: Linkage
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: An advanced, applied course for graduate students with a strong research focus on genetic epidemiology, and linkage analysis particularly. Provided sufficient demand, it is taught in the Spring semester. For additional information contact Dr. Nicola Camp. This course is structured as a mixture of lectures, analysis presentations, analysis discussions, paper debates, and computer and analysis labs. The course includes: data and file preparation; qualitative and quantitative traits; parametric and non-parametric analyses; theoretical aspects and practical analysis exercises of multiple genetic linkage methods; splitting pedigrees for analysis, ordered subset analysis, two-locus analysis; Monte-Carlo Markov-chain methods; sample size, power and significance and multiple testing issues.

title: Advanced Genetics
description: Advanced Genetics covers the fundamentals of classical genetics and genetic analysis in prokaryotes and eukaryotes. Classical genetics encompasses the mechanisms of inheritance and the behavior of genes and chromosomes in somatic cells and germ cells. Genetic analysis is a branch of biological investigation that uses mutations and mutant phenotypes to study the function and behavior of cells and groups of cells, in isolation and in a developmental context. Prokaryotes and eukaryotes have different modes of inheritance and significant differences in gene regulation and in their cellular biology. Prokaryotes provided the foundational discoveries of molecular biology and continue to be a source of new genetic tools and biological understanding with health and ecological relevance. Modern eukaryotic genetics blends the tools of molecular biology, cell biology and classical genetics to investigate gene and cell function in complex organisms.

title: Advanced Genome Analysis Journal Club
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Weekly discussions of papers published in the refereed peer-reviewed literature.

title: Advanced Geographical Data Analysis
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Geographical research increasingly generates large and complex datasets that may cover both space and time, and multiple methods have been developed to analyze these data. The course is designed to introduce students to 1) a suite of techniques for the analysis of such diverse datasets; 2) the interpretation of results generated; and 3) the appropriate (and inappropriate) use of these methods. The majority of topics will be accomplished by in-class lab exercises using the statistical software R, as well as take-home exercises. In addition, students will undertake a short research project using one or more of the techniques covered. The course will include a discussion component each week, allowing a review of the methods covered and presentation of real-world examples of their application.

title: Advanced Geotechnical Testing
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Advanced laboratory and field methods of geotechnical testing, including measurement of suction in the laboratory and the field, borehole shear test, cone penetration test, ko-blade, one- and three-dimensional wetting-induced volume change tests, advanced triaxial testing.

title: Advanced Geotechnical Testing
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Meets with CVEEN 6340.  Advanced laboratory and field methods of geotechnical testing, including measurement of suction in the laboratory and the field, borehole shear test, cone penetration test, Ko-blade, one- and three-dimensional wetting-induced volume change tests, advanced triaxial testing.

title: Advanced German Grammar
description: Focuses on review and deeper understanding of German grammar presented up to GERM 3040/3060. Provides opportunity to refine and practice advanced grammar (reading, writing, listening, speaking). Topics may include the subjunctive, passive, modal verbs, reflexives, etc. Includes study of authentic sources (web, press) for idiomatic usage and vocabulary.

title: Advanced Grammar and Composition
description: The course focuses on developing an advanced level of language and cultural proficiency in the Spanish language, enabling students to communicate in various target language contexts, e.g., oral presentations and writing academic texts. The course aims at further developing students’ language skills through a more advanced acquisition of vocabulary, grammar, and cultural knowledge that will reinforce the knowledge and understanding of diverse life experiences and facilitate fluent, appropriate, and culturally nuanced language interpretation and use. The course emphasizes intensive practice in various forms of Spanish writing, including descriptive, narrative, expository, and argumentative styles. Open for students with a year and a half or more experience in a Spanish-speaking country or area (native speakers, military service, LDS missions, etc.).

title: Advanced Grammar and Editing Skills (for EAS Speakers)
description: Prerequisite for students not placed in EAS 1050. Emphasis in on the review of sentence-level grammar in personal writing. In order to register, students must take the EAS writing placement test.

title: Advanced Grammar Review
description: The course focuses on developing Advanced level of language and cultural proficiency in the Italian language enabling students to communicate in various target language contexts. The course aims at further developing students’ language skills through an advanced acquisition of vocabulary, grammar, and cultural knowledge that will reinforce their understanding of diverse life experiences and facilitate fluent, appropriate, and culturally nuanced language interpretation and use. Intensive reading and writing as a basis for a systematic review of the syntax, morphology, and lexicon of Italian. First course for students who learned the language through residence in Italy or an Italian-speaking environment.

title: Advanced Graphics Studio: Advertising Design
description: Exploration of methods, processes and fundamental skills integral to advertising design. Students will gain an understanding of the use of conceptually driven messages, copy writing, art direction and visual communication in branding environments.

title: Advanced Graphics Studio: Editorial Design
description: Exploration of theory, methods, processes and design skills integral to the understanding and creation of publication design for a variety of media platforms. Students will gain an understanding of the components essential to editorial design; such as art direction, editing, gird systems, typography, image development and narrative structures.

title: Advanced Graphics Studio: Environmental Graphics
description: Exploration of theory, methods, processes and fundamental technical skills integral to graphic design and the built environment. Students will gain an understanding of the design strategies utilized for the development of way finding systems, exhibition design and type in the environment.

title: Advanced Graphics Studio: Graphic Illustration
description: Exploration of methods, processes and fundamental technical skills integral to the creation of illustration for visual communications. Students will gain an understanding of the use of narrative illustration as an editorial or commercial element within design communications.

title: Advanced Graphics Studio: Identity Systems & Branding
description: Exploration of theory, methods, processes and design skills integral to the design of corporate identities and their systems. This includes conceptual and visual strategies for implementation of a brand through a variety of media platforms and environments.

title: Advanced Graphics Studio: Interactive Experiences
description: Exploration of theory, methods, processes and fundamental technical skills integral to the creation of user-centered digital design experiences. Students will research and explore the nuances of designing for various digital channels and the technical strategies unique to interface design.

title: Advanced Graphics Studio: Motion Graphics
description: Exploration of theory, methods, processes and fundamental technical skills integral to the creation of motion graphics for visual communications. Students will create a series of projects that explore time-based graphics through the exploration of story boarding and the use of pertinent digital tools and media platforms. Students should complete the Graphic Design Second-year Review prior to this course.

title: Advanced Graphics Studio: Packaging Design
description: Exploration of theory, methods, processes and design skills integral to the understanding and creation of package designs. Students will gain familiarity with three-dimensional design while being exposed to the unique design and marketing challenges associated with the product development, packaging and branding.

title: Advanced Graphics Studio: Special Topics
description: This variable-content studio course explores the theory, methods, processes and skills integral to a particular design discipline and/or topic.

title: Advanced Graphics Studio: Sustainable Design Practice
description: This course gives an overview of the principals behind ecological sustainability and how design strategies affiliated with it can be applied to creative thinking and design process. Students will be presented with an overview of the environmental impacts of design and production practices. Upon successful completion of the course students will be able to integrate sustainable design principles into their own creative process.

title: Advanced Handbuilding Projects

title: Advanced Health and Wellness Coaching
description: Building on the foundations course, this advanced course delves deeper into the theories and practices of health and wellness coaching. Students will refine their coaching skills and learn advanced techniques for facilitating client growth and change. Competency-based content areas include evidence-based care, ethics and scope of practice, positive psychology, appreciative inquiry, mind-body medicine, and interprofessional care. The course will support students in elevating their health & wellness coaching through an exploration of health & wellness topics across the seven domains of health (emotional, environmental, financial, intellectual, physical, social, and spiritual).

title: Advanced Health Assessment Across the Lifespan
description: Required for Doctor of Nursing Nurse Practitioner students to develop evidence-informed advanced health assessment skills to determine the health status of patients across the life span. Emphasizes a holistic analysis of various aspects of health.

title: Advanced Health Assessment of the Neonate
description: Required for neonatal nurse practitioner emphasis students to develop evidence-informed clinical assessment and decision-making skills for neonatal comprehensive and problem-focused visits.

title: Advanced Health Counseling
description: This course is designed to build upon the patient counseling skills gained during the first and second years of pharmacy school and will prepare students to more effectively participate in direct patient care. Emphasis will be placed on practicing motivational interviewing skills to assist patients with positive health behavior change. These skills will be utilized when assisting patients with managing chronic diseases, overcoming addiction, and improving medication adherence. The majority of this course will consist of hands-on activities including small group discussions, role play, video recordings, and active reflection.

title: Advanced Health Promotion and Developmental Assessment for Neonatal Nurse Practitioners

This course focuses on health promotion and disease prevention of pediatric population within the family context. This includes mastery of obtaining health history, pediatric specific examination skills and developmental surveillance with the goal of health promotion and anticipatory guidance.
