title: Appellate Clinic
college: LW - S.J. Quinney College of Law
description: The Appellate Clinic involves placement in a public, public interest, or private law office to observe and work on appellate litigation. The co-requisite Appellate Practice Course provides a forum for students to share their experiences and explore these issues in greater depth.

title: Appellate Practice
college: LW - S.J. Quinney College of Law
description: An examination of the practical and procedural components of appellate litigation. Students will receive instruction regarding the legal principles and skills involved in appellate practice and apply these lessons by researching and writing an appellate brief, as well as presenting a mock oral argument. This course is recommended, although not required, for students wishing to participate in the Traynor Moot Court Competition. Counts toward the experiential education requirement.

title: Appellate Practice Survey
college: LW - S.J. Quinney College of Law
description: The Appellate Practice Survey course provides an overview of the rules of appellate procedure and an introduction to appellate process. This class is designed to ensure that students will understand how their assigned clinical work fits into the entire appeal and will learn about aspects of the process for which they are not directly responsible. Students may be asked to complete short exercises or to analyze aspects of their case to enhance learning from their clinic work. The course is offered for 1 credit on a Pass/Fail basis.

title: Apple Certification
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: A hands-on course that provides an intensive and in-depth exploration of troubleshooting on Mac OS X and give entry-level system administrators the skills, tools, and knowledge to implement and maintain a Mac OS X Server-based system. This course is designed to give you a tour of the breadth of functionality of Mac OS X and the best methods for effectively supporting users of Mac OS X systems, and install and configure Mac OS X Server to provide network-based services, such as file sharing, authentication, and printing. Tools for efficiently managing and deploying Mac OS X are also covered. The course is a combination of lectures and hands-on case study exercises that provide practical real-world experience. Special fee includes course materials and two vouchers for certification exams.

title: Application and Theory of Projective Techniques
description: Theory and practice of projective techniques. Emphasis on Exner's system of the Rorschach.

title: Application of Competencies of Evidence-Based Practice
description: This course is designed to familiarize the learner with the competencies needed to apply Evidence Based Practice (EBP), which will build on the basic principles of research to this course. The competencies include discovery of knowledge, evidence summary, translation of research findings into practice, and integration and evaluation of outcomes. Note: College of Nursing Matriculated students cannot take this course to fulfill program requirements.

title: Application of Evidence Based Practice for the Athletic Trainer
description: This course will apply evidence based practice principles in clinical practice settings. Critical analysis of the levels of evidence supporting selected clinical interventions will be a major component of the course. This course will explore current advanced manual therapy skills in relation to evidence based practice literature. Further, the students will gain exposure to varied methods for generating evidence relevant to clinical practice.

title: Application of Human Motor Development Across the Lifespan
description: A common theme between KINES sub-disciplines is human movement.  Understanding lifelong human development as it relates to the motor, affective, and cognitive domains is critical for KINES professionals.  A major goal of the course will be to understand developmental appropriateness.

title: Application of Learning Theories in Higher Education
description: This course will include readings in learning theory, adult learning principles, and best practices and methods in teaching in higher education, including discussions about the application of and personal philosophy connections to learning theories in a higher education classroom based on instructor and student preferences.

title: Application of Outcome Measures for Clinicians
description: The purpose of this course is to prepare advanced practice nurses to design and implement processes to evaluate outcomes of practice, practice patterns, and systems of care within a practice setting, health care organization, or community. In this course students will learn how to collect appropriate and accurate data to generate evidence for nursing practice.

title: Application of Research in Aging
description: This course is designed to develop the basic ability of the students as an informed consumer and participants in the process of aging research. Students will collect, analyze, display, and interpret data in order to address issues related to aging populations. Development of sense of inquiry through understanding and applying the logical steps of the research process are emphasized.

title: Application of Statistics to Health Care
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Basic course in the use of statistical methods in the analysis of outcome studies and quality improvement.

title: Applications of Business Statistics
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: This practical and example-based course uses the essential tools and concepts of Six Sigma as a unifying framework. Discussion topics include design of experiments, goodness of fit, contingency tables, correlation analysis, nonparametric statistics, and an introduction to statistical process control. Moreover, hands-on skill is acquired for the development and interpretation of regression models from functional areas of accounting, finance, marketing and operations with a focus on depth rather than breadth of the subject material. Microsoft Excel is used to create graphical and numerical outputs with emphasis on interpretation of output. A comprehensive case write-up and presentation, integrating the essentials of course tools is prescribed as the end-of -term project. Business cases are used throughout the term for reinforcement purposes.

title: Applications of Business Strategy
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: Emphasizes the environment in which strategic decision-making takes place. It provides an opportunity to apply the analytic tools learned in STRAT 6070/6071 in a variety of contexts. Topics vary by year, but have included advanced coursework regarding the critical role of leadership, strategy in dynamic environments, as well as, technologically intensive environments. The course is taught primarily through the use of topical strategy cases. Students can expect written case analyses, group projects, and a major written project.

title: Applications of Economic Principles and Public Policy Statistics
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Course provides a staged learning process and equips students with the fundamentals of microeconomic theory and applied statistics as they relate to public policy issues and processes. The purpose of the course is to provide foundational knowledge needed for subsequent public policy courses.

title: Applications of Evidence in Nursing Practice
description: This course prepares students with foundational knowledge and skills for evidence-based practice in an applied learning environment. The course incorporates the principles and processes for evidence-based practice, including the application of best available evidence, clinical judgement, and patient-centered care. Students demonstrate learning through completion of program-specific evidence-based scholarly project. Discipline-specific written and verbal presentation skills are developed and refined as students generate a learning project targeted toward a specific population or clinical focus area.

title: Applications of Research in Aging

Students will collect, analyze, display, and interpret data in order to address issues related to aging populations. title: Applied Anatomy
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Provides clinical applications of human anatomy, and integrates anatomical terminology, organ systems, regional anatomy, and imaging anatomy. Instructional design for the course provides a dynamic medical context for the study of anatomy.

title: Applied Anatomy
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Provides clinical applications of human anatomy, and integrates anatomical terminology, organ systems, regional anatomy, and imaging anatomy. Instructional design for the course provides a dynamic medical context for the study of anatomy.

title: Applied Anatomy and Physiology
description: H EDU 4660 is an interactive case study approach to the understanding, retention and application of basic anatomy and physiology principles as they relate to the pre-hospital provider. The class will be more than memorization of facts. This course will allow the student to compare the structure and form of the human body and how it normally functions to how it performs when under disease or traumatic conditions.

title: Applied Architectural Communication
description: This half-semester course provides an exploration of applied architectural communication methods in order to inform students' architectural design processes in studio. Students learn critical thinking and problem solving skills through active experimentation and critical evaluation of communication tools and methods.

title: Applied Architectural Practice
description: This course builds on the fundamental principles outlined in 6700 and allows the students the opportunity to apply lessons learned into practice-related problems. Issues related to contracts, project management and delivery, and the economic determinants of practice are covered. The last 7 weeks introduces the students to practice through an internship experience that reinforced the materials covered in 6700 and 6701.

title: Applied Atmospheric Modeling
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: This course focuses on numerical weather prediction (NWP) modeling to simulate atmospheric processes. The Weather Research & Forecasting (WRF) model is a state-of-the-art mesoscale NWP model that is used by over 30,000 people in over 150 countries. WRF is used across disciplines to simulate the atmosphere and provide information to model weather, air quality, hydrology, and renewable energy. This course aims to teach you how to use the WRF model, write computer codes to extract model results, generate data visualizations using the model outputs, and to compare the model results with observations to determine model uncertainty. The course will use high performance computing (HPC) facilities at the University of Utah (CHPC) and the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR). This course provides a hands-on applied numerical modeling experience, enhances computer programming skills, and gives an introduction to HPC platforms.

title: Applied Behavior Analysis I
description: Challenging behavior represents a major area of concern for individuals, their families, and the professionals who work with them. In this class, students will learn the theory and practice to support the implementation of positive behavior supports and interventions to prevent and address challenging behavior. Specific content includes tiered systems of support, functional behavior assessment, behavior intervention planning, contextual behavioral assessment and intervention, and working within systems to prevent and address challenging behavior at the individual level.

title: Applied Behavior Analysis I: Behavior Change
description: In this class, students will learn the theory and practice to support the implementation of positive behavior supports and interventions to prevent and address challenging behavior.

title: Applied Behavior Analysis II
description: Students will continue learning the behavioral principles and concepts introduced in ABA 1. There will be more focus on theory, and we will go more in-depth on procedures. Students will have a deeper understanding of behavior analytic practice and skill building. Each week, students will read articles and book chapters, respond to discussion questions, and practice vocabulary words using methods of SAFMEDS (Say All Fast Minute Everyday Shuffled).

title: Applied Behavior Analysis II: Skill Acquisition
description: In this course students will learn to apply the behavior change principles and procedures introduced in ABA I to the teaching of new functional, adaptive, and academic skills. Students will gain a deeper understanding of the science of behavior as well as its broad applications. Each week, students will read articles and book chapters, respond to questions over the readings, and participate in activities focused on applying new concepts and skills to solve problems of practice in educational and clinical settings.

title: Applied Behavior Change
description: Students will learn how to promote health and wellness in individuals and groups using behavior change theories as a guide. Strategies for effective interpersonal communication and group facilitation are emphasized.

title: Applied Biology: Using Science to Improve Quality-of-Life
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Survey of new approaches to disease diagnosis and therapy including genomics, proteomics, functional genomics and structure-based drug design. The intent is to integrate technical issues with biological ones.

title: Applied Biomedical Principles and Analysis
description: The development of diagnostic and research skills.

title: Applied Clinical Chemistry I
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Clinical experience in pre-analytical, analytical, and post-analytical testing of blood and other body fluids for their biochemical components (e.g. blood gases, hormones, vitamins, therapeutic drugs, trace elements, toxins) using modern analytical techniques (e.g., electrophoresis, immunochemistry, chromatography, spectroscopy, mass spectrometry).

title: Applied Clinical Chemistry II
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Clinical experience performing routine analysis of blood and other body fluids for their biochemical components (e.g., electrolytes, enzymes, hormones, lipids, non-protein nitrogen compounds, proteins) using automated and manual procedures. Students will participate in pre-analytical, analytical, and post-analytical phases of testing.

title: Applied Clinical Hematology I
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Clinical experience performing tests to establish a diagnosis, detect unsuspected diseases, or monitor effects of various treatment protocols for anemias, leukemias, lymphomas, and other hematologic disorders. Also includes experience in body fluid evaluation and urinalysis.

title: Applied Clinical Hematology II
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Includes experience in a special hematology laboratory performing tests designed to aid in the differential diagnosis of leukemias, lymphomas and other hematologic malignancies. Also includes rotations in the immunologic and hematologic flow cytometry laboratories.

title: Applied Clinical Hemostasis
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Evaluation of normal hemostasis, hemostatic disorders, the associated clinical symptoms, and the laboratory testing necessary for diagnosis. Includes laboratory practice in the performance of diagnostic tests.

title: Applied Clinical Immunohematology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Practical application of Immunohematology principles including collection and processing of blood, component therapy, evaluation of prenatal and perinatal blood specimens, pretransfusion compatibility testing, transfusion reaction evaluations and quality assurance. Serologic testing and problem-solving skills such as antibody identification are emphasized.

title: Applied Clinical Immunology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: The integration of the theory and practice of immunology in a clinical setting including immunologic assays used in the diagnosis of infectious disease, autoimmune disorders, and immune deficiencies.

title: Applied Clinical Immunology II
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Utilize techniques for ELISA, protein electrophoresis, hemagglutination, immunoblotting and indirect fluorescent antibody testing. Employ flow cytometric analysis (including immunophenotyping and leukemia phenotyping) and molecular (PCR) testing. Rotation will be tailored to supplement any previously acquired experience.

title: Applied Clinical Microbiology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Isolating and identifying commonly encountered pathogenic bacteria from clinical specimens.

title: Applied Clinical Pharmacokinetics
description: Application of principles of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics to the individualization of pharmacotherapy.

title: Applied Clinical Pharmacokinetics
description: Application of principles of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics to the individualization of pharmacotherapy.

title: Applied Clinical Pharmacokinetics
description: Application of principles of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics to the individualization of pharmacotherapy.

title: Applied Communication Research Methods
description: As a mixed-methods survey course in communication research, students learn a variety of ethical and purpose-driven approaches to collecting data and information necessary in professional, strategic, journalistic, and health and science communication contexts. The course covers the purposes and processes of research as well as the presentation of data for both qualitative and quantitative approaches. Research methods covered may include sampling; surveying; observation; audience analytics; interviews; focus groups; content analysis; or others, as assigned by the instructor.

title: Applied Community Health and Leadership in Tribal, Rural, and Underserved (TRU) Settings
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Physicians in tribal, rural, and underserved (TRU) communities depend on a diverse skill set that goes well beyond clinical care. In resource-limited communities, physicians are often called upon to lead efforts related to community health assessments and improvement, clinical care quality assurance and improvement, public health promotion and education, monitoring and evaluation of health programs, and local non-profit or voluntary organizational missions. Through a mixture of synchronous and asynchronous course work through online modules and didactic sessions, and experiential learning opportunities with community health workers (CHWs), students who complete this course will gain skills in community and organizational leadership, cultural humility, developing and improving health interventions and programs and planning a capstone community-oriented health improvement (COHI) project that may be implemented during the MS4 year. This is the third course for MS2 students completing the TRUE Certificate (MDID 6550/6555 are the first 2 courses in the series). However, this course has no prerequisite requirements and can be completed by any medical student who desires to explore community health and leadership in TRU settings. Students taking this course will have the unique opportunity to develop a longitudinal relationship with a primary care clinical mentor. Students (OPTIONAL Opt-in opportunity for 0.5 credit) will be paired with a primary care physician (Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, OB-Gyn, or Pediatrics, depending on interest and mentor availability), allowing for a rich clinical mentor-mentee relationship to develop over the course of the semester. Students will spend a minimum of 4 clinical sessions during the semester, though, depending on time and mentor availability, more sessions can be scheduled.

title: Applied Complex Variables
description: Analytic functions, complex integration, Cauchy integral theorem, Taylor and Laurent series, residues and contour integrals, conformal mappings with applications to electrostatics, heat, and fluid flow.

title: Applied Complex Variables and Asymptotic Methods
description: Cauchy-Riemann equations, Cauchy integral formulas, Taylor and Laurent series, multivalued functions, branch points and cuts, analytic continuation, Jordan's lemma, evaluation of real integrals; potential theory, stream functions, conformal mapping, special functions, Fourier, Laplace, Hilbert, and Z transforms, scattering theory, asymptopic analysis of integrals, Laplace's method, Watson's lemma, method of steepest descents.

title: Applied Computational Electromagnetics with Commercial Solvers
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Introduction to commercial computation electromagnetics solvers. Solvers can include: CST Studio Suite, Ansys HFSS and COMSOL Mulitphysics. Application projects draw from: antenna design, metamaterials, signal integrity, implanted device telemetry, electromagnetic exposure and other topics of interest in electrical engineering.

Application projects draw from: antenna design, metamaterials, signal integrity, implanted device telemetry, electromagnetic exposure and other topics of interest in electrical engineering.

title: Applied Computational Electromagnetics with Self-Written Codes
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Students will formulate and solve real-world electromagnetics problems computationally. Applications areas range from geolocation to next-generation prosthetic limbs. Emphasis will be on two of the most popular computational electromagnetic techniques: the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method and the finite element method (FEM). Students will write their own codes from scratch. For students who already or might use commercially available electromagnetic software, this course will provide an understanding of the internal workings of such “black box” programs.

title: Applied Computational Genomics
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course will provide a comprehensive introduction to fundamental concepts and experimental approaches in the analysis and interpretation of experimental genomics data. It will be structured as a series of lectures covering key concepts and analytical strategies. A diverse range of biological question enabled by modern DNA sequencing technologies will be explored including sequence alignment, the identification of genetic variation, structural variation, and ChIP-seq and RNA-seq analysis. Students will learn and apply the fundamental data formats and analysis strategies that underlie computational genomics research. The primary goal of the course is for students to be grounded in theory and have the ability to conduct independent genomic analyses. (Instructor has requested students complete the 'Intro to R for Data Analysis' workshop at https://utah.catalog.instructure.com/browse/ds-learn/courses/introduction-to-r-for-data-analysis. Contact department for info.)

title: Applied Data Management
description: This course emphasizes database design, data cleaning, quality control, and data integration, with a focus on ensuring data safety, storage, and sharing. Students will engage in data management for qualitative, quantitative, and mixed methods throughout the course. By its conclusion, students will produce a detailed data sharing and management plan, applying advanced concepts to safeguard and optimize datafor research and analysis.

title: Applied Deep Learning in Biomedicine
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course is an applied introduction to deep learning, a branch of machine learning, that aims to understand and practice the development and application of modern neural networks. In that vein, the course will provide students with a working knowledge of deep learning fundamentals that presents a start point for using more advanced techniques in their future careers. The course will start by reviewing and implementing the main mathematics, statistics, and machine learning principles that will be required during the course. Then, the students will learn how deep learning algorithms extract layered high-level representations of data in order to optimize feature learning, cluster analysis, and classification machine learning tasks. Hands-on activities will provide students with the experience of implementing deep learning architectures for mainly biomedicine applications.

title: Applied Developmental Psychology
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Applied Developmental Psychology will provide a venue for teaching a range of topics that synthesize research and the promotion of positive development across the life span. Content varies depending on subtitle.

title: Applied Econometrics
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: This course covers some important topics in the empirical analysis of micro and macro data. We will discuss selected cross-section, panel data and time series and time series methods. Empirical studies in social sciences frequently use non-experimental data which makes it complicated to study relationships between variables and to evaluate effects of e.g., different programs or policies. We will study extensions and elaborations of the basic multivariate regression model to address this issue.

title: Applied Economic Analysis
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: This is a course about how to analyze and interpret economic data and use it to inform decision making. The goals of the course are to 1) provide you with a broad and a balanced perspective on what data and evidence economic policymakers and business leaders use to understand the economy; 2) to introduce theoretical and analytical tools used to measure economic and financial conditions; 3) and to learn how to analyze and use economic data effectively in presentations and written work. The course is intended for sophomore, junior, and senior students who plan to pursue a business degree, including QAMO majors. Students should have taken an intro microeconomic theory class, and an intro econometrics class and have basic familiarity with Excel and Stata.

title: Applied Entrepreneurship for Musicians
description: This course will prepare aspiring professional musicians to function as small business owners and music entrepreneurs. Topics include defining, understanding, and implementing entrepreneurship, goal setting of a music enterprise, identifying customers, leadership, marketing, and the business plan.

title: Applied Environmental Physiology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Complex interactions of humans and environment.

title: Applied Ethics
description: Theoretical foundations of applied ethics. Ethical and meta-ethical theories and their application to professional and individual decision-making. The rational basis of moral judgments and policies in social and professional contexts.

title: Applied Ethics
description: Theoretical foundations of applied ethics. Ethical and meta-ethical theories and their application to professional and individual decision-making. The rational basis of moral judgments and policies in social and professional contexts. For juniors and seniors.

title: Applied Ethics and Professionalism
description: A review and discussion of applied ethics and professionalism that students faced during dental school as it relates to dentistry in diagnosis, planning, treatment and practice management.

title: Applied Ethics and Professionalism for Mechanical Engineers
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: This course provides the student with a brief applied understanding of societal ethics, engineering ethics and personal morals. Steps and procedures in ethical decision making are presented. Famous engineering ethical cases are analyzed to identify common reasons individuals behaved unethically. Tools for how to protect oneself in ethical situations are discussed. Some principles of engineering professionalism are also covered.

title: Applied Finite Element Analysis
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: A practical approach to finite element analysis (FEA). The course will provide an introduction to the theoretical basis of the direct stiffness, potential energy, and weighted residual formulation methods of simple elements (1D, 2D). Students will also learn commercial finite element software and learn to critically evaluate finite element models. Examples will be provided for solid, fluid, and heat transfer applications. A brief introduction to some advanced methods (design optimization, uncertainty quantification, and solver types) will be provided.

title: Applied Fourier Analysis
description: Fourier series and integrals, uncertainty principle, approximation and convergance theorems, discrete Fouier transforms and the Fast Fourier transform, signal and image processing.  A project/paper will be required.

title: Applied Gemonics II
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: The Applied Genomics class serves to introduce students to different genomic data types and their analyses. In particular, the use of microarray and next-generation sequencing data in prediction and mutation analysis will be examined. This is an introductory class, and a background in programming or bioinformatics is not required. This course is a continuation of Applied Genomics I.

title: Applied Genomics I
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.

In particular, the use of microarray and next generation sequencing data in prediction and mutation analysis will be examined. This is an introductory class, and a background in programming or bioinformatics is not required.

title: Applied Genomics I
description: This course will cover topics related to genomic research, including gene expression/microarray, next-generation sequencing, and other related topics. This class will include a lecture component, integration of genomics-focused projects, and a hands-on lab sessions. At the end of this class, we expect students to understand the different genomic approaches available and an introduction on how to apply these approaches to independent research projects.

title: Applied Genomics II
description: This course will cover more advanced topics related to genomic research and builds from the material taught in PH TX 7777. This class will include a  lecture component, integration of genomic-focused projects, and a hands-on lab session. At the end of this class, we expect students to understand the different genomic approaches available and how to apply these approaches to independent research projects.

title: Applied Health and Fitness Assessment
description: Evaluating health and fitness is an important part of health education. This class provides students with hands-on laboratory experiences to evaluate health and fitness, and evaluate disease risk classification based on current guidelines. Students will practice the skills to provide health and fitness related assessments, interpretation and counseling based on results of health and fitness assessments. This class will also focus on how to address the connection between physical fitness and health status with clients.

title: Applied Health and Fitness Assessment and Exercise Programming
description: This class provides students with hands-on laboratory and field based learning experiences to provide actual clients with: disease risk classification based on current ACSM guidelines, health related fitness assessments, interpretation and counseling based on results of fitness assessments and constructing individually tailored exercise prescriptions to meet the clients' unique needs and goals. This class will also focus on how to address the connection between physical fitness and health states with clients.

title: Applied Health Promotion Technology Lab: Development and Testing
description: In this class students will evaluate the efficacy of a mobile health application as a group in order to practice the process of systematic review. Simultaneously, students will select (or develop) a mobile health application of their own design, which they will later evaluate using the same process. Working individually and in small groups, students will test and then report their results about he efficacy of their custom health technology.

title: Applied Health Promotion Technology: Practicum
description: This practicum provides students with the opportunity to employ the skills they have acquired throughout the Applied Health Technology Certification Program to the challenges faced by Health Promoters and Educators in the field. Students will identify and work with a health agency where they will apply health technology in order to solve problems and create one new educational or behavior changes intervention in addition to a minimum 100 hours of work. Students will create an online portfolio to track their progress. Grading will be based on an evaluation of the program developed, web portfolio, and feedback from the agency.

description: The history of museums as public institutions through which western cultures have presented their understanding of themselves and others. Current debates in museology (cultural property issues, exhibition, interpretation, public education, etc.).

description: This course addresses foundational concepts in information technology and informatics, important for the conduct of health sciences research. The course builds upon basic prerequisite information technology skills, and emphasizes applied informatics concepts as they relate to study design, development, and execution.

title: Applied International Management
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: This course is designed as an overview of international business. The class will explore the ways of doing business internationally for large corporations, as well as small and medium-sized businesses.

title: Applied International Management & Regional Contexts
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: The purpose of the Applied International Management elective course to expand and enhance PMBA students' practical knowledge and understanding of international business environments, to extend their appreciation of cross-country differences through direct interaction, and to expose them to current foreign business practices and regulations.

college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Continuation of MIL S 3010. Focus is on preparation for a National ROTC Advance Camp.

title: Applied Legal Writing
college: LW - S.J. Quinney College of Law
description: Applied Legal Writing builds on skills learned in a first-year legal writing course and provides students with significant experience researching and writing persuasive legal documents. Assignments are designed to improve students' ability to engage in legal research, complex legal analysis, and persuasive argument. The class also addresses critical writing skills such as structure, organization, grammar, word choice, and proper citation form. Enrollment is completed by the Assistant Dean of Students or the Associate Dean of Academic Affairs.

title: Applied Linear Algebra
description: Vector spaces, linear transformations, systems of linear equations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, applications to Markov chains, linear difference and differential equations, numerical methods. There is also an applied computer lab component.

title: Applied Linear Operator and Spectral Methods
description: The theory of linear operators applied to matrix, differential and integral equations, the Fredholm alternative, spectral theory, inverse and pseudo-inverse operators, Hilbert-Schmidt theory and eigenfunction expansions.

title: Applied Machine Learning in Biomedical Informatics
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course develops the student conceptual and applied insights to extract knowledge from biomedical datasets and tackle known modeling and data challenges. The course covers two main parts: most traditional machine learning methods and deep learning essentials. Although the course teaches the fundamental mathematics and statistical aspects behind each learning algorithm, it emphasizes on how to develop and validate baseline and optimal models for practical biomedical applications. During the processes of developing and validating models, students will learn to interpret results properly and conduct an effective error analysis. Students will learn how to use the error analysis results to tune the learning algorithms for mitigating modeling and data challenges.

title: Applied Math and Statistics for Biomedical Engineers
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Introductory course will cover concepts from probability and statistics. Topics will include discrete and continuous random variable, distributions, univariate and multivariate distributions, expected values, moments, normal distribution, and derived distribution; maximum likelihood estimation, confidence intervals, and tests of hypotheses. Graduate students will be given extra projects to exemplify concepts learned.

title: Applied Math and Statistics for Biomedical Engineers

title: Applied Modern Causal Inference In Comparative Effectiveness Research
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course will cover some of the applications of modern causal inference methods in comparative effectiveness research. The course will extend the theoretical frameworks for modern causal inference including counterfactuals, directed acyclic graphs and their use in identifying bias due to confounding, selection bias, and conditioning on intermediates. This course will cover research designs and methods that researchers use to support casual inferences in epidemiology, health services research, and health economics. Some specific topics include randomized trials, network meta-analysis, instrumental variables, propensity score matching, inverse probability of treatment weighting, marginal structural models, and differences in differences.This course will focus on randomized and observational designs used for comparative effectiveness research. Design and statistical analysis will be framed in terms of counterfactual outcomes and required assumptions for causal inference.

title: Applied Modern Causal Inference In Comparative Effectiveness Research
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course will provide an overview of modern causal inference using the framework of counterfactual outcomes to provide rigorous definitions of causal effects, confounding and selection biases. Topics include the development of directed acyclic graphs to characterize patterns of confounding and define assumptions required for causal inferences, adjustment for confounding using propensity scores, inverse probability weighting, instrumental variables, and difference-in-difference approaches. Additionally, the course delves into how causal inference methods interface with techniques for network meta-analysis. Methods for implementing methods for causal inference with standard statistical software will be emphasized. A theoretical supplement to this course will provide a more in-depth theoretical background.

title: Applied Modern Causal Inference In Comparative Effectiveness Research
description: This course will cover some of the applications of modern causal inference methods in comparative effectiveness research. The course will extend the theoretical frameworks for modern causal inference including counterfactuals, directed acyclic graphs and their use in identifying bias due to confounding, selection bias, and conditioning on intermediates. This course will cover research designs and methods that researchers use to support casual inferences in epidemiology, health services research, and health economics. Some specific topics include randomized trials, network meta-analysis, instrumental variables, propensity score matching, inverse probability of treatment weighting, marginal structural models, and differences in differences.This course will focus on randomized and observational designs used for comparative effectiveness research. Design and statistical analysis will be framed in terms of counterfactual outcomes and required assumptions for causal inference.

title: Applied Molecular Diagnostic II
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Utilize principles/techniques in RE/Southern Blotting and RFLP.  Employ PCR detection technologies.  Apply QA/QC process to PCR technology.

title: Applied Molecular Diagnostics
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Nucleic acid isolation, identification and amplification techniques used in disease diagnosis in the clinical laboratory.

title: Applied Multivariate Data Analysis
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Students will study multivariate normal distribution, multivariate regression, MANOVA, principal components, classification, factor analysis, cluster analysis. This is more applies course focusing on applications in health science research.

title: Applied Music Theory and Sight-singing for Musical Theatre
description: This course is the second class in a series of two in which students learn fundamentals of music theory in order to improve their ability to read and write musical notation; and develop their ability to recognize, understand, and describe the basic materials and processes of music that are heard or presented in a score. In the second semester of study, the instructor will address more advanced aural, sight-singing, and compositional skills using listening and written exercises, as well as performance and examination. Building on foundational skills learned in Music Theory for Musical Theatre, the course will progress to include more advanced creative an analytical tasks.

title: Applied Neuropsychological Assessment
description: Reviews advanced concepts in applied neuropsychology assessment, supervised experience in administration and interpretation of the Halstead-Reitan Neuropsychological Battery, and other neuropsychological measures.

title: Applied Nuclear Engineering II with Laboratory
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Meets with CVEEN 5710.  Analysis, control, and design of nuclear systems; radioactive waste management, medical, radiation protection, environmental restoration and disposal. Includes laboratory.

title: Applied Nuclear Engineering with Laboratory
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Meets with CVEEN 6710.  Analysis, control, and design of nuclear systems; radioactive waste management, environmental restoration and disposal. Includes laboratory.

title: Applied Nutrition Through the Lifecycle
description: In this course, you will explore nutrient functions, needs, and sources, as well as common nutrition-related concerns associated with pregnancy, lactation, growth, development, maturation, and aging. This 3-credit class contains highly practical information, whether you intend to work in a healthcare setting or simply want to develop personal skills to promote and maintain a healthy lifestyle at each stage of the human life cycle.

title: Applied Occupational Biostatics
description: Students will learn how to identify and employ statistical concepts to answer important scientific questions in occupational health and safety. Statistical methods learned will be applicable to laboratory, interventional, and epidemiological study settings. Students will develop the ability to design, execute and interpret the results of statistical analyses common in occupational health and safety research. We will use practical occupational health case-based applications of biostatistical concepts including descriptive statistics, correlation, linear and logistic regression, analysis of variance, generalized estimating equations. Sampling, surveillance, repeated measures and longitudinal analytical methods will be introduced. We will also learn about tests for equivalence and sample size calculations.

title: Applied Parasitology and Mycology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Isolation and identification of yeasts, molds, and parasites in the clinical laboratory, using classical identification methods, rapid methodologies, and instrumentation.

title: Applied Physical Geology
description: Applications of physical geology that combine field measurements and computer analysis. Digital elevation models, remote sensing, and computer simulations used to solve four to five basic science and applied problems in landscape evolution, hazards analysis, land use, and natural resources. Field measurements are interpreted using computer analyses and simulations of geological processes, with emphasis on computer mapping, visualization, and modeling.

title: Applied Policy Development in Oral Health
description: This course is a close examination of the process of health policy making from an idea to a bill by shadowing a legislator and interviewing with identified stakeholders.

title: Applied Population Balance Modeling
description: Population balance modeling technique applied to particulate processes: crystallizer, dissolver, agglomeration, grinding, leaching, and droplet dispersion. Variants of the mode as well as analytical solution emphasized.

title: Applied Population Health Sciences Experience
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course is designed to give PHS students to gain practical experience in the clinical or other relevant settings. Students will complete a rotation within their chosen setting and meet together to present and discuss their experiences. Students will shadow a professional in a clinical or health care operations setting 8 hours per month for a full year. After completing their rotations students may register for class. Class includes discussion and a presentation of a case, application of the knowledge gained, or how their research has been informed by the experience. This exposure will provide context for the research areas that they pursue.

title: Applied Positive Psychology Capstone
description: The Capstone course for the Applied Positive Psychology undergraduate certificate program is a one-credit eight-week immersion in recent research and videos describing emerging positive fields such as integrative health, positive leadership, rehabilitation, and others adopting a positive psychology perspective and evidence-cased positive interventions. Students will explore how positive psychology has created new best practices in other professions and will focus on one career area for the research paper. This course also provides an introduction to two popular careers utilizing interventions from positive psychology: health/wellness coaching and leadership coaching. According to author Patricia Marx in an article published in the "New Yorker" on 08 October 2012, the "International Coach Federation (ICF) estimates that there are forty-eight thousand coaches in the world.

title: Applied Probability and Statistics
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Overview of basic probability rules and axioms, probability distributions, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, multi-variable problems, systems reliability.  Examples and homework assignments emphasize Civil Engineering applications.

title: Applied Probability and Statistics
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Meets with CVEEN 6260.  Overview of basic probability rules and axioms, probability distributions, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, multi-variable problems, systems reliability. Examples and homework assignments emphasize Civil Engineering applications.

title: Applied Probability and Statistics for Engineers
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: The purpose of this course is to introduce mathematical concepts and statistical methods used in modern engineering analysis. The goal is to introduce students to analytical and numerical tools that can be used to solve real world engineering problems. Lectures will be supplemented by several programming exercises using R and/or Matlab, and a large number of practical examples on relevant engineering topics. This course covers the role of statistics in engineering, probability theory and distributions, continuous random variables, random sampling, data description, and statistical analyses or a single sample, and common hypothesis testing.

title: Applied Quantitative Methods for Policy Analysis
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Course involves the analysis of quantitative date, the application of statistics for understanding and conducting public policy research and the use of statistical software.  Specific topics include descriptive statistics for discrete and continuous variables, probability theory, hypothesis testing, bivariate associations, ordinary least squares regression and logistic regression.  Emphasis is on interpretation of findings. Graduate students will be held to a higher standard of performance.

title: Applied Regression Analysis I
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: The course will take a pragmatic approach to teach the topic of regression analysis and cover preparing data for analysis, fundamentals of linear and multivariable regression models, model diagnostics, remedial measures, interpreting results, statistical programming, and scientific writing. Learners will be given lab-based assignments each week that corresponds to the topic covered in class. The course will culminate in a final project where learners will design a study using regression analysis on a large dataset to examine predictors of patient outcomes. Project results will be presented and a manuscript will be submitted.

title: Applied Remote Sensing Seminar
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: This seminar-style course explores geographic applications of remote sensing. Students will review and present scientific papers within an application area selected by the instructor, and collaborate on a group project that utilized remotely sensed data. Contact the instructor to determine the specific topics that will be covered by this course.

title: Applied Research in Occupational Therapy
description: This is the second of two courses required in the Occupational Therapy research sequence. Building on their knowledge and experiences from the first research course, students will further their knowledge of quantitative and qualitative research practice as well as apply principles in research labs. Students are required to develop a research proposal. Learning will occur through class activities, lectures, and labs. Knowledge gained through this course may be used to implement beginning level research projects and to evaluate OT interventions.

title: Applied Research in Recreational Therapy
description: This is the second of two courses required in the Recreational Therapy research sequence. Building on their knowledge and experiences from the first research course, students will further their knowledge of quantitative and qualitative research practice as well as apply principles in research labs. Students are required to develop a research proposal. In addition, students will gain experience analyzing quantitative and qualitative data. Learning will occur through class activities, lectures, and labs. Knowledge gained through this course may be used to implement beginning level research projects and to evaluate RT interventions.

title: Applied Research Methods: Practice and Program Evaluation
description: Evaluation of SW programs and interventions and application of advanced evaluative research design to critique and develop research-based intervention strategies, including program development based on documented need, feasibility assessments, monitoring, assessment of effectiveness, and assessment of impact. Course will prepare students to write a proposal for federal funding and builds on previous courses, using methods and skills of study development, research design, population sampling, data collection, and analysis.

title: Applied Research Methods: Quantitative and Mixed Methods
description: The course uses data sets for secondary data analysis; quantitative and qualitative, and composition of methods and results section for a manuscript.

title: Applied Resiliency and Positive Health
description: Positive Applied Resilience and Resiliency embraces the philosophy that by focusing on and enriching mental, physical, spiritual and ecological strengths, gifts, and talents, then people will be fortified to more effectively deal with life challenges. The course will be founded upon positive health theories including chaos theory, hardiness, stress related growth and other foundational theories. Applied resilience applies to individuals as well as to families, groups, organizations, communities and nations. Students will develop skills in resiliency mapping, accessing resilient sources of strength; learn resonation and integrative health skills, as well as how to overcome undesirable health thoughts an behaviors using resilient strategies.

title: Applied Social Work Statistics
description: This class prepares students to setup, maintain, and use agency-based databases. Specifically, students learn how to enter data into a database, use data analyses to make clinical decisions, provide outcome information to track treatment progress or obtain funding, and answer hypotheses in order to improve treatment.

title: Applied Statistical Analysis
description: This course expands upon previous course work in graduate level statistics in several ways: 1) Focuses on the implementation of statistical analyses that were learned in the Stats I & II sequence (NURS 7201 and 7202) through the use of statistical programming (within established standards for programming) in both SPSS and SAS;  2) Emphasizes the need to establish questions and an analytical plan prior to accessing or analyzing data; 3) Provides practice in accessing public use data sets such as YRBS and National Health Interview; 4) Instructs students how to work with researchers to access study based data sets; 5) Introduces and provides practice in how to shift focus in the face of null findings and how to pursue questions that emerge in the course of the analyses; 6) Promotes movement from data analysis to dissemination.

title: Applied Statistical Techniques
description: This case/example-based course introduces exploratory data analysis (EDA) using R. No prior knowledge of R is assumed. A primary objective is for students to apply graphical EDA techniques (including: scatter plots, box plots, histograms, probability plots, residual plots, and mean plots) to representative data sets using the RStuido platform. Additionally, students evaluate data using standard, quantitative statistical techniques. Practical exercises and industry cases are used throughout the term. Students are encouraged to bring laptops to class.

title: Applied Statistics
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: An advanced undergraduate-level examination of statistical procedures commonly used in the health, social and behavioral sciences. Topics include: Sampling distributions, probability, confidence intervals, t tests, ANOVA, correlation, regression, nonparametric statistics, data transformation, and the logic of null hypothesis significance testing.

title: Applied Statistics
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: A graduate-level examination of statistical procedures commonly used in the health, social and behavioral sciences. Topics include: Sampling distributions, probability, confidence intervals, t tests, ANOVA, correlation, regression, nonparametric statistics, data transformation, and the logic of null hypothesis significance testing.

title: Applied Statistics I
description: An introduction to basic probability theory, sampling from normal populations, large-sample problems, sampling from one or two populations, estimation, and testing. R is used to perform statistical analyses. There are three lectures and one 1 1/2 hour lab per week.

title: Applied Statistics II
description: Introduction to analysis of variance, regression analysis, correlation analysis, and nonparametric techniques. Continued use of R programming language. There are two lectures and one 1 1/2 hour lab per week.

title: Applied Venture Skills
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: The task of conceiving and launching a new venture requires specific knowledge about products, industries, and the competitive environment. In order to be successful in different industries, entrepreneurs need industry-specific skills and blocks of knowledge. The purpose of this class is to provide students with the skills and knowledge to succeed in the industries studied in ENTP 6820: Venture Trends. This class is taught in collaboration with business professionals who have deep industry experience in the relevant industries.

title: Applying Dissemination and Implementation Science Theories, Models & Frameworks
description: This course will develop student capacity to apply dissemination and implementation (D&I) science theories, models and frameworks (TMFs) to the promotion of evidence-based behavioral intervention reach, effectiveness, adoption, implementation, and maintenance of behavioral interventions in community settings. Students will critically evaluate and contrast TMF strengths and weaknesses as they relate to improving D&I outcomes through the application of context, strategy, mechanism, and outcome relationships. This will include aligning strategies to fit within context and address specific mechanisms to improve outcomes. Finally, students will explore how levels of community engagement align with and benefit D&I science.

title: Applying Integrated 3D Imaging
description: Incorporate the skills acquired from this Pathway course into your clinical treatment of patients where possible and permissible. Help oversee teaching assistants in basic radiology lab course. Finalize and present Pathway portfolio and research results.

title: Applying to Medical School
description: This course is designed for students who are nearing the time in their academic careers to begin preparation for applying to medical school. The primary focus is to help students prepare for the medical school application process by teaching them about how to best portray themselves and their accomplishments using tools such as the premed planner, the Medical School Admissions Requirements (MSAR) website, AMCAS, and more. Students will not only learn about resources for applying, but also reflect on themselves within the context of becoming future physicians. These objectives will be met by the following: (1) Provide information on the resources available when applying to medical schools. (2) Expand networking opportunities with professionals in this area. (3) Offer opportunities to develop quality components of the medical school application through practice and feedback from peers and the instructor. (4) Provide students with vital information for them to make informed decisions that impact their medical school applications.

title: Approaches to the Study of Politics
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: This course provides an introduction to the discipline of political science and the graduate study of politics.  Course content includes history of the discipline and theoretical approaches within the study of politics.

title: Aqua Tone
description: The primary objective is to increase the general well-being and fitness level of each participant. Aqua-tone is a complete body workout. It improves coordination, reflexes, flexibility, and aerobic fitness as it builds a strong body.

title: Aqua Zumba
description: An integration of the Zumba formula and philosophy with traditional aqua fitness disciplines. Aqua Zumba is a challenging, water-based, interval-tempo workout that combines cardio conditioning with water resistance training and total body toning/exercise.

title: Aquacise
description: Familiarizes students with the benefits of a water workout and increase general well-being and fitness level.

title: Aqueous Geochemistry
description: Meets with GEO 5690 and GEO 6690; additional work required of graduate students.  See GEO 5690 for course description.

title: Arabian Days: The Islamic Caliphates
description: Arabian Nights is the most famous piece of literacy fiction in Islamic civilization.  "Arabian Days" is a course that will focus on this civilization during its formative and mature periods (700-1259 C.E.).  During these periods, Muslims shaped their religion, science, arts, architecture, and literature which will be investigated in this course.

title: Arabic Culture and Civilization
description: A survey of intellectual, literary, religious, and artistic traditions that express themselves through the medium of the Arabic language. Readings are in English.

title: Arabic Grammatical Tradition
description: The topic of the seminar will be the Arab linguist who explicitly dealt with phonetic/phonological and syntactic issues.  Treatises and sections of treatises that dealt with the above topics will be discussed.  The course will emphasize the study of the Medieval Arab grammarians.  The discussion will focus on the primary sources themselves.

title: Arabic Historical Texts
description: Literary analysis of passages from historians who used Arabic language with particular skill and effect. Stylistic mannerism, vocabulary practice, and historiographic approach.

title: Arabic Paleography
description: Meets with MID E 4143. Additional work required of graduate students. The history of Arabic writing, the historic script styles, the arts of calligraphy, the Arabic book tradition. Training in use of original Arabic manuscripts of the 7th-18th centuries, emphasizing work related to the individual student's interests.

title: Arabic Paleography
description: Meets with ARAB 6430 and MID E 6143. The history of Arabic writing, the historic script styles, the arts of calligraphy, the Arabic book tradition. Training in use of original Arabic manuscripts of the 7th-18th centuries, emphasizing work related to the individual student's interests.

title: Aramaic
description: Introduction to the Aramaic language and some of its literary masterworks. Dialects: biblical Aramaic, the Targumim and Babylonian Jewish Aramaic.

title: Arbitration
college: LW - S.J. Quinney College of Law
description: The law, theories and practices of arbitration will be taught in a variety of settings. Topics typically include initiating and managing the arbitration process, as well as drafting and enforcing arbitration awards.

title: Archaeological Field Methods
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Introduction to basic archaeological field techniques; mapping, field notes, photography, survey and basic excavation techniques. Combines lectures and field exercises.

title: Archaeological Fieldwork in Italy
description: A faculty-led, archaeological field school opportunity in Italy that allows students to gain hands-on excavation experience. Students will learn transferable skills in the field, contribute to cutting-edge archaeological research, and participate in an immersive cultural experience. Students will be trained in archaeological skills needed in the field and lab. They will be introduced to the basics of archaeological thinking and interpretation of archaeological data, and the ongoing importance of cultural heritage. Hands‐on work will be supplemented by readings, discussions, and visits to nearby museums/historical sites. Admission to the field school is by application only. Applications are welcomed from both current University of Utah students, non-students and out-of-state students.

title: Archaeological Practice
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Seminar on the current practice of archaeology in the U.S., including coverage of legal, regulatory, and commercial topics. Coordinated by a regular faculty member, with participation of members of the regional archaeological community.

title: Archaeological Science
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Our knowledge of variation in prehistoric human behavior is based virtually exclusively on archaeological analyses of the physical remains left behind by ancient peoples. This course reviews the history, goals, theories, and methods of archaeological research, especially as influenced by the natural sciences. Substantive examples are drawn from a diverse set of time periods and geographical locations.

title: Archaeology and Paleoecology of the Arid West
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: During the late Pleistocene and Holocene, the Great Basin and Colorado Plateau experienced multiple periods of climate change and landscape evolution. Wetlands expanded and contracted, plant compositions and distributions changed, and range shifts and local extinctions in fauna occurred. For humans, these climate-driven environmental changes significantly impacted resource structure and availability. This class will use concepts drawn from evolutionary ecology to examine how people in the past interacted with the landscapes around them. This will allow us to understand why the archaeological record looks the way it does and to understand it in the context of the corresponding paleoecological record/s. This class will enable students to have a full appreciation of how complex the past can be and how it is worth understanding in terms of today.
