title: Asian Pacific American Contemporary Issues
college: CT - Sch for Cultural & Social Tran
description: Survey of emerging social and political issues concerning Asian Pacific Americans in the post-1965 era. Discussion topics include the meaning of being Asian Pacific American and its intersection with ethnic culture, class, gender, school, work, law, media, and politics in the contemporary setting.

title: Asian Pacific American Education Experiences
description: Course will address historical and contemporary educational issues in the Asian American and Pacific Islander American community in both the elementary, secondary and higher-education context nationally and in Utah. Examines the ideological factors behind the "model minority education myth" in schools and colleges, Pan-Asian diaspora and its influence on education.

title: Asian Pacific American History
college: CT - Sch for Cultural & Social Tran
description: A comparative analysis of the international context of Asian immigration into the United States. An in-depth examination of the Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Asian Indian, and Filipino settlement, community development, intra-Asian American group relationships, and the evolution of Asian American cultures. Explores the impact of American federal and local legislation and the broader relationship between Asian Americans and the mainstream society.

title: Asian Pacific American Literature Seminar
description: Special readings selected to broaden the student's background in Asian American Literature.

title: Asian Pacific American Politics
college: CT - Sch for Cultural & Social Tran
description: Survey of the historical and contemporary political experiences of Asian Americans and their pursuits of equal rights and opportunities in the U.S. political system.

title: Asian Pacific American Women
college: CT - Sch for Cultural & Social Tran
description: An analysis of the lives and changing status of Asian-immigrant women--past and present, American-born women of Asian ancestry, and their diverse lifestyles in the American socio-economic framework. An examination of women's issues in the context of intergenerational relationships, community pressures, and the influence of the larger community.

title: ASL/English Instructional Strategies
description: The purpose of this course is to develop both the understanding and the skills of signed language communication in educational settings, with emphasis on the development of ASL/English strategies for classroom instruction of Deaf and hard of hearing students. Students participating in this course will compare, contrast and practice American Sign Language, English sign language systems and Cued Speech. Students will investigate home and educational use of sign language and the issues impacting sign language choice and implementation. Cultural issues as well as community impacts will be reviewed. Students will reinforce their classroom learning within the school and community settings.

title: ASL/English Instructional Strategies
description: The purpose of this course is to develop both the understanding and the skills of signed language communication in educational settings, with emphasis on the development of ASL/English strategies for classroom instruction of Deaf and hard of hearing students. Students participating in this course will compare, contrast and practice American Sign Language, English sign language systems and Cued Speech. Students will investigate home and educational use of sign language and the issues impacting sign language choice and implementation. Cultural issues as well as community impacts will be reviewed. Students will reinforce their classroom learning within the school and community settings.

title: Aspects of Injury and Illness Prevention
description: This course focuses on important aspects of injury prevention and screenings of active populations. Prevention concepts from a pre-participation exam, functional movement screenings, and injury prevention programs will be discussed and performed in practical laboratory sessions.

title: Assesment and Evaluation in Instructional Technology
description: This course provides an in-depth coverage of principles and methods of evaluation and assessment, with a focus on the development of instructional technology applications.  The course will emphasize the importance of data-driven instructional decisions, and the role of both formal and informal assessment in this.  The course will cover the overall program evaluation cycle, as well as specific methods and strategies for both formative and summative evaluation goals.  Students may design assessment and evaluation methods for their instructional design projects from ED PS 6030 if taken concurrently.

title: Assessing Health Indicators
description: This course develops student’s skills in holistic health assessment, focusing on various health indicators and social needs to evaluate individual health risks. Emphasis is placed on integrating these findings with each patient’s unique circumstances to prioritize needs and create effective care plans. The course also explores the impact of chronic and complex conditions on health, including illness progression, destabilization points and care transitions.

title: Assessment  Specialties Practicum
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Students administer comprehensive test batteries, develop case formulations, treatment recommendations and write integrative reports. A minimum of two reports must be completed; these may include specialty assessments under the supervision of adjunct faculty with instructor approval.

title: Assessment and Clinical Reasoning Skills for CNL Practice
description: This is a course to facilitate the Clinical Nurse Leader (CNL) student in developing the CNL role.  The major focus is on assessment of self, individuals, and systems.  The student will develop clinical reasoning and clinical judgment skills for implementation of the CNL role in health care organizations.  Subcomponents of clinical situations will be explored related to their impact on achieving desired and appropriate outcomes.

title: Assessment and Curriculum Development in Adapted Physical Education
description: This course was designed to provide students the background knowledge and skills to implement the achievement-based curriculum model in their teaching. Students are provided opportunities to develop a curriculum, assess students in motor skills and fitness, plan lessons based on assessment, implement the lessons incorporating the principles of teaching, evaluate student outcomes by measuring their progress, and evaluate their own teaching based on student outcomes.

title: Assessment and Curriculum Development in Adapted Physical Education
description: This course was designed to provide students the background knowledge and skills to implement the achievement-based curriculum model in their teaching. Students are provided opportunities to develop a curriculum, assess students in motor skills and fitness, plan lessons based on assessment, implement the lessons incorporating the principles of teaching, evaluate student outcomes by measuring their progress, and evaluate their own teaching based on student outcomes.

title: Assessment and Curriculum Development in Special Physical Education
description: Designed to provide students with information about instruments to assess students with disabilities in physical education. Students will learn how to administer tests, interpret results, prescribe programs, and evaluate the effectiveness of programs. In addition, students will learn how to develop a curriculum in special physical education.

title: Assessment and Evaluation
description: Required for nursing students in the Master of Science program with an emphasis on Nursing Education (and open to graduate and post-graduate students exploring opportunities for nurse educators), students apply evidence-based approaches to formative and summative assessment to promote learner competency.

title: Assessment and Evaluation
description: The purpose of this course is to apply evidence-based approaches to formative and summative assessment to promote learner achievement. Students will have the opportunity to create sample assessments, practice written and oral feedback, and evaluate instructional effectiveness using student assessment data. Concepts of assessment validity and quality will be incorporated throughout.

title: Assessment and Feedback in Education
description: The purpose of this course is to provide evidence-based approaches to formative and summative assessment of learners. Providing useful feedback to learners will be emphasized. Using multiple sources of information to determine effectiveness of instruction and student learning will be addressed.

title: Assessment and Instruction for Reading Difficulties
description: This course covers how to assess students with reading difficulties and how to develop, implement, and evaluate a program designed to intervene instructionally to improve students' reading performance.  The course covers formal and informal assessments with a special emphasis screening and progress monitoring measures.  The course requires students to tutor one or more children at  the University of Utah Reading Clinic during teh entire semester.  In this way, previous reading and writing courses are applied to practical situations where teachers develop an instructional program specifically to prevent and remedy reading difficulties.

title: Assessment and Intervention for Beginners At-Risk for Reading Difficulties, Early Steps Practicum
description: To help educators develop in-depth theoretical and practical knowledge of effective, research based assessment and intervention for beginning readers at-risk reading failure.

title: Assessment and Intervention for More Advanced Struggling Readers: Higher Steps Practicum
description: This course is designed to help educators develop theoretical and practical knowledge of effective, research-based assessment and intervention for struggling readers of all ages who have reached an end-of-second-grade level, but whose reading abilities are below grade level expectations.

title: Assessment and Intervention for More Advanced Struggling Readers: Higher Steps Practicum
description: This course is designed to help educators develop theoretical and practical knowledge of effective, research-based assessment and intervention for struggling readers of all ages who have reached an end-of-second-grade level, but whose reading abilities are below grade level expectations.

title: Assessment and Intervention for Reading Difficulties
description: The purpose of this course is to help practicing interventionists become knowledgeable and proficient with: (a) administering and interpreting various reading assessments and (b) understanding and implementing research-based literacy instruction with struggling readers. Students will learn how to screen for reading difficulties, identify specific areas of strengths and needs, and monitor students’ mastery and progress throughout intervention. In addition, students will learn about implementing research-based reading instruction across the five components of reading: phonemic awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary, and comprehension. Finally, this course will focus on the assessment/instruction cycle, discussing the iterative process of using assessment data to inform instruction. This course includes hands-on practice tutoring a student at the University of Utah Reading Clinic (UURC). As such, you will be working with a student directly and will have the opportunity to apply the content you will learn about in this course under the supervision of a clinical faculty member. The UURC faculty will provide you with ongoing feedback and guidance throughout your tutoring. Please note that for this course to count toward the USBE’s Secondary Intervention Endorsement, educators must implement Higher Steps in a small group of secondary students (i.e. grades 6–12).

title: Assessment and Intervention for Struggling Readers: Next Steps Practicum
description: To help educators develop theoretical and practical knowledge of effective, research-based assessment and intervention for struggling readers of all ages who have reached primer level, but whose reading abilities are below mid-grade three level.

title: Assessment and Service Delivery for Students with Mild/Moderate Disabilities
description: This course is designed to provide experience in the administration and interpretation of assessment procedures for planning and implementing instructional interventions for students with mild/moderate disabilities. The primary emphasis for assessment is on evaluation and linking IEP goals and objectives to the assessment results. It also provides an introduction to the service delivery and professional and practical ethics required to meet the knowledge area outlined in the Council for Exceptional Children Special Education Professional Ethical Principles (see http://www.cec.sped.org/Standards/Ethical-Principles-and-Practice-Standards). Additionally, this course meets the diversity requirement of the English as a Second Language (ESL) endorsement requirements.

title: Assessment and Service Delivery for Students with Mild/Moderate Disabilities
description: This course is designed to provide experience in the administration and interpretation of assessment procedures for planning and implementing instructional interventions for students with mild/moderate disabilities. The primary emphasis for assessment is on evaluation and linking IEP goals and objectives to the assessment results. It also provides an introduction to the service delivery and professional and practical ethics required to meet the knowledge area outlined in the Council for Exceptional Children Special Education Professional Ethical Principles (see http://www.cec.sped.org/Standards/Ethical-Principles-and-Practice-Standards). Additionally, this course meets the diversity requirement of the English as a Second Language (ESL) endorsement requirements.

title: Assessment in Physical Education
description: The purpose of the course is to increase one's knowledge of performance-based assessment related to teaching Pre K-12 physical education. Students will focus on four primary themes as a theoretical basis for improving student assessment: a) Assessment drives instruction, b) Assessing content across the psychomotor, cognitive and affective domains of learning, c) Using assessment in ways in which allow students to apply information & perform competently, and d) Using a balanced approach when selecting assessment strategies.

title: Assessment in Physical Education
description: Designed to provide students with information about instruments to assess students with disabilities in physical education. Students will learn how to administer tests, interpret results, prescribe programs, and evaluate the effectiveness of programs. In addition, students will learn how to develop a curriculum in special physical education.

title: Assessment in the Arts
description: Assessment techniques appropriate for arts programs are discussed to develop arts assessment competence.  Quantitative and qualitative evaluation systems for museums, arts organizations, arts education organizations, and arts programs will be the focus of the course .Open to any arts graduate student or others.

title: Assessment Lab
description: Application of specific assessment methods and materials with students in simulated and actual settings. Students enrolled in SP ED 6131 will be assigned additional coursework.

title: Assessment Lab
description: Application of specific assessment methods and materials with students in simulated and actual settings.  Students enrolled in SP ED 6131 will be assigned additional coursework.

title: Assessment of Child Language Disorders
description: Examination of the diagnostic process and its application to children with language disorders.

title: Assessment of Clinical Learning
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course focuses on the processes used to locate, appraise, and appropriately use existing assessment tools in one's own scholarly work. Learners may find this helpful in selecting tools relevant in planning their scholarly project.

title: Assessment of Learning and Issues of Accountability
description: This course will examine theoretical concepts that are foundational in educational evaluation and assessment such as standardized testing, alternative assessment and reliability and validity.  The course will then explore the implications of the above concepts in K-12 classrooms and address issues surrounding accountability of student performance.

title: Assessment of Linguistically Diverse Populations
description: This course critically explores policies, procedures, and formal and informal measures used to assess the language proficiencies and academic achievement of linguistically diverse students in U.S. public schools. Including in this are the areas of English and native language competence; program placement, progress, and exit; and classroom-based assessments, as well as other forms of alternative assessments. Students enrolled in ECS 6645 will be expected to meet a higher standard of performance and may be assigned additional assignments. Meets Utah State Office of Education ESL Endorsement Standard IV on Assessment.

title: Assessment of Linguistically Diverse Populations
description: This course critically explores policies, procedures, and formal and informal measures used to assess the language proficiencies and academic achievement of linguistically diverse students in U.S. public schools. Including in this are the areas of English and native language competence; program placement, progress, and exit; and classroom-based assessments, as well as other forms of alternative assessments. Meets Utah State Office of Education ESL Endorsement Standard IV on Assessment.

title: Assessment Practicum: Traditional Adult and Child Assessment Skills
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Students administer comprehensive test batteries, develop case formulations, treatment recommendations and write reports. Five reports must be completed.

title: Assessment Tools for HPE Scholarship
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course focuses on the assessment of learner achievement at the program level. Emphasis is on designing assessment systems to determine learners' status relative to program outcomes.

title: Assessment, Documentation, & Evaluation in Recreational Therapy
description: This class is designed to teach the critical components of client assessment, documentation, and evaluation in the RT Process. Course content includes protocol development, client assessment (standardized assessment, interview, observation, and record review) and the process of treatment planning, documentation, and evaluation. Client evaluation will be discussed as it relates to client assessed outcomes. Students will learn about the WHO International Classification of Functioning and Disability (ICF) and role within the assessment process.

title: Assessment, Documentation, and Evaluation in Recreational Therapy
description: This class is designed to teach the critical components of client assessment, documentation, and evaluation in the RT Process. Course content includes protocol development, client assessment (standardized assessment, interview, performance), and the process of treatment planning, documentation, and evaluation. Client evaluation will be discussed with client-assessed outcomes. Students will learn about the WHO International Classification of Functioning and Disability (ICF) and RT practice models and their role in the assessment process.

title: Asset Pipeline
description: The Course will cover the entire game art pipeline and the interdependencies at two meta levels--the asset production pipeline, and the team pipeline. This course will extend the practical knowledge learned in GAMES 1050-Digital Content Creation and allow students to begin to apply that knowledge to the interdependencies of the asset pipeline for games. The course is team-project based and students will demonstrate competency in asset design, development, and production using software packages that are used in the game industry.

title: Asset Pricing
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: This course will discuss established concepts and recent developments in the area of asset pricing. The focus of the class is going to be put on the discussion of theoretical foundations and their testable implications. The goal of this class is to provide students with the appropriate techniques required to read and evaluate the academic literature in this field and to start their own research in the area of asset pricing.

title: Assistive Technology for Students with Visual Impairments
description: Meets with SP ED 5480. Introduction to assistive technology used by individuals with visual impairments. The course teaches strategies for assessment and instruction of assistive technology.

title: Assistive Technology for Students with Visual Impairments
description: Introduction to assistive technology used by individuals with visual impairments. The course teaches strategies for assessment and instruction of assistive technology.

title: Assistive Technology for Young Children with Visual Impairments
description: Introduction to assistive technology devices, strategies for assessment and instruction on assistive technology for young children who are blind or visually impaired.

title: Assistive Technology for Young Children with Visual Impairments
description: Introduction to assistive technology devices, strategies for assessment and instruction of assistive technology for young children who are blind or visually impaired.

title: Asthma Camp
description: Field experience with children who have asthma. Drug and nondrug aspects of care.

title: Asymptotic and Perturbation Methods
description: Asymptotic analysis, initial-value problems, multiscale analysis and the averaging theorem, homogenization theory, boundary- and transition-layer problems, matched asymptotic expansions, relaxation oscillations and propagating transition layers. Applications to problems from the physical and life sciences.

title: Asymptotic Methods
description: Offered on the basis of need or interest.

title: Athletic Training as a Health Care Profession
description: This course will provide students with an understanding of the history, roles and responsibilities, and current state of the athletic training profession. The sports medicine team will be identified with specific instruction on the athletic trainers’ role. Professional development plans within athletic training will be discussed.

title: Athletic Training Laboratory I
description: General principles in the evaluation of musculoskeletal injuries and conditions.

title: Athletic Training Laboratory II
description: General principles of the physiologic response to and use of therapeutic modalities.

title: Athletic Training Patient and Professional Advocacy
description: This course will focus on how athletic trainers can advocate for their patients and populations they care for and communities they work in. Students will also discuss the current professional mission and goals of athletic training and how they can advocate for these causes.

title: Atlantic Rim Politics
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Meets with POL S 6425. Graduate students should register for POL S 6425 and will be held to higher standards and/or additional work. Selected countries and topics from the North Atlantic political region.

title: Atlantic Rim Politics
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Meets with POL S 5425. Graduate students should register for POL S 6425 and will be held to higher standards and/or additional work. Selected countries and topics from North Atlantic political region.

title: Atmospheric Chemistry
description: Introduction to the physical and chemical processes affecting the dynamics and fate of air pollutants at the local, regional, and global scales.  Particular emphasis is on tropospheric pollutant chemistry and transport, photochemistry of ozone, smog formation, aqueous-phase chemistry, and acid rain.

title: Atmospheric Chemistry and Air Pollution
description: The course will apply basic principles of physics and chemistry to quantitatively describe the processes that control the chemical composition and evolution of the Earth's atmosphere. Special topics include acid rain, the ozone hole, photochemical smog production, health effects of air pollution, and alternative energy sources.

title: Atmospheric Radiation
description: Theory of solar and infrared radiation; fundamentals of energy balance and climate models; parameterization of infrared and solar-flux transfer in clear, aerosol, and cloudy atmospheres; climate perturbations due to greenhouse gases, aerosols and clouds.

title: Atmospheric Thermodynamics & Boundary Layer Processes
description: Thermodynamics of dry and moist air, including adiabatic processes, parcel theory, and thermodynamic diagrams; boundary layer structure and processes, including turbulence, surface fluxes, vertical structure and diurnal cycle.

title: Attachment Theory Across the Lifespan
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Meets with FCS 6940. This course takes a lifespan approach to the study of human attachment relationships. Attachment theory, research and clinical application are considered through a seminar format that focuses primarily on reading and discussion.

title: Attachment Theory Across the Lifespan
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: This course takes a lifespan approach to the study of human attachment relationships. Attachment theory, research and clinical application are considered through a seminar format that focuses primarily on reading and discussion.

title: Au.D. Capstone Project
description: Capstone project for clinical doctorate completed prior to initiation of final clinical traineeship year. Project may consist of research project, literature review, or community service project. It is mentored by a faculty committee, and a final written paper must be submitted to and approved by the committee. A oral presentation of the project must also be given before start of clinical traineeship year. Each student will enroll for 6 credits (3 credits for 2 consecutive semesters)

title: Audio Technology for the Arts
description: This course is a comprehensive examination of technology used for sound design in the arts. With a strong emphasis on the fundamentals, students can expect to be knowledgeable about audio technology after this course.

title: Audiology and Listening Technology for Teachers of Students Who are Deaf or Hard of Hearing
description: This course provides the participant with understanding of sound, audiological measures in assessing hearing loss, how to read and interpret audiological test results, knowledge of amplification devices and how to care for and troubleshoot these devices. This course also provides the participant with knowledge of the anatomy and physiology of the auditory and vestibular systems, embryological development of the systems and common causes of hearing loss.

title: Audiology and Listening Technology for Teachers of Students Who are Deaf or Hard of Hearing
description: This course provides the participant with understanding of sound, audiological measures in assessing hearing loss, how to read and interpret audiological test results, knowledge of amplification devices and how to care for and troubleshoot these devices. This course also provides the participant with knowledge of the anatomy and physiology of the auditory and vestibular systems, embryological development of the systems and common causes of hearing loss.

title: Auditing Research Seminar
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: Review of selected auditing research topics.

title: Auditing, Controls, and Ethical Issues in Accounting
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: This course introduces students to the flow of information through the various accounting cycles and the corresponding internal controls. Overview of the basic theory and concepts associated with the attest function, including the various types of audits; objectives of audit engagements; political, legal, social, and ethical environment in which auditors work; and procedures used by auditors in meeting their objectives.

title: Audition Preparation for Majors and Non-Majors
description: Concepts and techniques will be presented to hone the students' understanding of an proficiency with auditioning skills. Skills presented in this class will be useful for multiple types of auditions with main emphasis on preparing for a career in professional dance, especially commercial dance. The course requires activity as well as classroom lecture.

title: Audition Preparation for Non-Majors and Majors
description: Concepts and techniques will be presented to hone the students' understanding of and proficiency with auditioning skills. Skills presented in the class will be useful for multiple types of auditions, job interviews and preparation for career in professional dance, with an emphasis on commercial dance. The course requires activity as well as classroom lecture. Students must have completed or be concurrently enrolled in a Jazz II class in order to put in practice the lessons presented in Jazz I and Jazz II.

title: Audition Technique I for ATP
description: An introduction to the business of acting, including discussion of graduate school and professional possibilities, resume preparation, headshot selection, and career choices (regional theatre, New York, L.A., Chicago). Students practice presenting themselves through theatrical monologues and film audition scenes.

title: Audition Technique II for ATP
description: Acceptance into the Actor Training Program required. The second in a two-course sequence. In this semester, the text material is primarily classical. Each student will develop a repertory of classical audition pieces. Students also study the business as currently practiced by working theatre professionals.

title: Audition Techniques for MTP
description: The techniques involved in finding work in today's commercial musical theatre are skills that students can learn and practice. In this course, students will learn to select and prepare audition material suitable to their particular type, strengths, and abilities.

title: Auditions for Actors
description: Students develop an awareness and appreciation of the art of acting as an actor and as an observer. Explores the basics of the audition process and examines various points of view regarding it. Students will also create a simple resume.

title: Augmentative and Alternative Communication
description: This course will provide a general introduction and overview of augmentative and alternative communication. This course will address the broad range of individuals who require AAC as well as the broad range of systems and strategies, including aided and unaided approaches and symbol sets of pictures and traditional orthography. Some of the topics will include assessment, selection of AAC systems, and intervention.

title: Augmentative and Alternative Communication
description: Assessment and determination of need for electronic and/or non-electronic systems designed to augment or replace communication for persons with severe motor, cognitive, and/or perceptual disabilities.

title: Augmentative and Alternative Communication Instructional Strategies
description: This course will focus on recommended strategies for teaching the functional use of augmentative and alternative communication (AAC). The course will address intervention principles and procedures for low-tech, light-tech, and high-tech AAC systems.

title: Augmentative and Alternative Communication Instructional Strategies
description: This course will focus on recommended strategies for teaching the functional use of augmentative and alternative communication (AAC). The course will address intervention principles and procedures for low-tech, light-tech, and high-tech AAC systems.

title: Augmentative and Alternative Communication Recommended Practices
description: This course is designed for professionals who work with individuals who have severe speech and language disabilities (e.g., students who use or would benefit from augmentative and alternative communication, students with limited verbal language). This course will provide information reqarding ways to incorporate language and literacy learning into routines and activites. The specific topics address in this course will change based on changes in recommended practices.

title: Aural Habilitation and Rehabilitation
description: Auditory development and current methodologies for management of children and adults with peripheral hearing loss and/or auditory processing disorders.

title: Aural Skills I
description: This aural skills course provides an introduction to sight-singing and dictation.

title: Aural Skills II
description: This aural skills course provides further development of sight-singing and dictation skills.

title: Aural Skills III
description: This aural skills course provides intensive development of chromatic sight-singing and dictation skills.

title: Aural Skills IV
description: This aural skills course provides further development and practice of sight-singing and dictation skills.

title: Australia and New Guinea Ethnography
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Meets with ANTH 3152; additional work required of graduate students. See ANTH 3152 for course description.

title: Australia and New Guinea Ethnography
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Meets with ANTH 6152. Continent of hunters, island of gardeners--sites of classic anthropological work. Prehistory and ethnography of Australia and New Guinea from 50,000 years ago to present. Ecology, economics, political and social organization, marriage systems, and religion.

title: Authentic Leadership and Management in Recreational Therapy
description: This course is design to prepare the graduate student with the skills and abilities to assume a management position in the health and human service industries or engage in private practice in recreational therapy. The class will explore the qualities of leadership and the components of daring leadership. The student will develop an understanding of contemporary healthcare systems and human service agencies, the influence of licensing and regulatory bodies, and the necessity of funding sources. The class will apply this learning through implementation of the quality improvement process as it relates to recreational therapy management practices. Students will also be introduced to the core concepts of clinical supervision as they relate to student internships and professional supervision and in the end will be asked to discern, how to create Work…Life/Balance.

title: Autism Across the Lifespan
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: This course examines the experiences of people with autism spectrum disorder in each major life stage. Drawing on local, multidisciplinary and inter-professional expertise, students will be presented with a variety of perspectives, and offer a balanced and supportive overview of autism issues, the impact on family and community, and contemporary issues related to disability, advocacy, and policy.

title: Autism across the Lifespan
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: This course examines the experiences of people with autism spectrum disorder in each major life stage. Drawing on local, multidisciplinary and inter-professional expertise, students will be presented with a variety of perspectives, and offer a balanced and supportive overview of autism issues, the impact on family and community, and contemporary issues related to disability, advocacy, and policy. Graduate students will be required to (1) upload a five-minute presentation that is an overview of their final paper. This presentation should include preliminary key findings and other pertinent information from their comparative analysis. (2) post along with their presentation one thought-provoking discussion question related to their presentation and (3) watch and respond to all the other presentations including each thought-provoking discussion question.

title: Autism Spectrum Disorder: Interventions
description: This is an intensive course offered for five days the Summer semester. It provides in-depth interactive training on evidence-based interventions for children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD). This is the second part of a two-part ASD course. The first part, ED PS 7836, focuses on ASD overview and assessment. Students registered for 7838 will have additional assignments and he held to a higher scholastic standard.

title: Autism Spectrum Disorder: Interventions
description: This is an intensive course offered for five days the Summer semester. It provides in-depth interactive training on evidence-based interventions for children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD). This is the second part of a two-part ASD course. The first part, ED PS 6836, focuses on ASD overview and assessment. Students registered for 7838 will have additional assignments and he held to a higher scholastic standard.

title: Autism Spectrum Disorder: Overview and Assessment
description: This is an intensive course offered for five days across a two-week period in the Summer semester Content includes: history of autism, symptoms trajectory and outcomes, ASD diagnosis, special education classification, assessment tools and methods (ADOS-2/ADI-R, checklists), and issues pertinent to school and clinic-based services and community support (e.g., occupational therapy, speech and language therapy, and pediatrics/psychiatry). This is the first part of a two-art ASD course. The second part, ED PS 7838, focuses on empirically-based interventions. Students registered for 7836 will have additional assignments and be held to a higher scholastic standard.

title: Autism Spectrum Disorder: Overview and Assessment
description: This is an intensive course offered for five days across a two-week period in the Summer semester. Content includes: history of autism, symptom trajectory and outcomes, ASD diagnosis, special education classification, assessment tools and methods (ADOS-2/ADI-R, checklists), and issues pertinent to school and clinic-based services and community support (e.g., occupational therapy, speech and language therapy, and pediatrics/psychiatry). This is the first part of a two-part ASD course. The second part, ED PS 6838, focuses on empirically-based interventions. Student registered for 7836 will have additional assignments and he held to a higher scholastic standard.

title: Autism Spectrum Disorders
description: This course will address development and impairment of language and communication in individuals with autism spectrum disorders (ASD). Differential diagnosis, assessment and intervention strategies are emphasized with a focus on empirically supported treatments and evidence-based practices. Current developments and research findings related to all aspects of assessment and intervention with individuals with ASD will be highlighted.

title: Autoimmunity and Immunodeficiency
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course will provide an opportunity for students to examine basic immunological mechanisms underlying immune dysregulation with focus on autoimmunity and immunodeficiency. The course is a combination of lecture, primary literature analysis, and in class discussion. Classes will be moderated by a group of faculty with relevant research backgrounds. The course will provide an opportunity for students to apply their basic immunology knowledge toward understanding how perturbation of specific immunological pathways or cells leads to disease.

title: Autopsy
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: The main goals are to learn to perform an autopsy, to interpret the findings, to synthesize the anatomic findings and the clinical data to analyze how and why the patient died, and to explain these findings in the written autopsy report and directly with the clinicians.

title: Avalanche Awareness
description: This online course is designed to introduce students to the avalanche phenomenon, causes, and hazards. Aspiring backcountry travelers can learn where to find the gear, resources and training to responsibly enjoy winter recreation. Students will begin to recognize and avoid avalanche terrain. This course is a stepping stone to Avalanche Level 1, PRTS 2007.

title: Avalanche Fundamentals - Level 1
description: Practical skills for travel over mountain snow, avalanche causes, snow stability, decision making, terrain selection, and companion rescue. Level 1 certificate upon completion of course. No camping required.

title: Avalanche Level 2
description: This course is designed for backcountry recreationists with Level 1 avalanche skills who want to go deeper with their snow and avalanche knowledge, as well as travel in more complex terrain. In this course, we spend time expanding student’s knowledge of the science of snow metamorphism and apply this knowledge to have a better understanding of the season snowpack history and the nature of existing avalanche problems. We present and utilize a systematic approach for sorting and prioritizing information in the field, setting a tone of teamwork, and minimizing human factor traps. Prior to enrollment in the course, students must provide Level 1 Avalanche and Rescue Fundamentals certifications. Students must be proficient in traveling in the backcountry and downhill skiing in variable conditions in avalanche terrain on skis or snowboard in a winter environment.

title: Avalanche Level I
description: This course will cover the basics of avalanche hazard awareness and stability assessment. Introductory level material covering terrain evaluation, safe travel protocols, self-rescue, snowpack formation and metamorphosis, stability test procedures, and interpretation and decision-making strategies, will be presented and practiced. Students should have some experience in winter backcountry travel and skiing.

title: Avalanche Processes & Leadership - Level 2
description: Class will focus on snowpack, analysis of stability, decision making, snowpack metamorphosis (change), terrain features, safe travel, human factors and rescue scenarios. This is Level II of a two part avalanche sequence. No camping required.

title: Avalanche Rescue
description: This class covers the standards published by the American Avalanche Association for Avalanche Rescue Courses, including (a) avalanche rescue principles, (b) avalanche gear and technique, (c) companion rescue process, (d) avalanche victim basic patient care, and (e) recognizing needs and identifying additional resources.

title: Avalanche Rescue Techniques and Theory
description: This is an intensive course covering the theoretical background and essential skills for responding to emergencies and rescues in avalanche terrain.  Stability analysis, terrain evaluation, travel techniques and decision making tools are integral to accessing patients.  Avalanche specific medical topics such as Triple H Syndrome have implications for long term patient care.  Advanced search and patient transport techniques are inherent to rescues in this environment.  Classroom theory will be balanced with in-field practice.

title: Awakening to the Heart of Zen
description: This course offers a practical introduction to Zazen, the heart of Zen-Buddhist training. Various meditation methods from the Soto and Rinzai schools are presented. Looking directly into one's innate wisdom or Buddha nature and the compassionate manifestation of this wisdom in everyday life situations has been the focus of all authentic training throughout the history of Zen. This wisdom is universal and does not depend on any particular religious doctrine. It has been transmitted from Shakyamuni Buddha down to the present day through successive generations of Zen masters. **Course offered Fall only**

title: BA Advanced Architectural Design Workshop
description: The course provides additional experience and training in studio-related projects, and skill development and refinement relating to formal and contextual issues in architecture.

title: BA Architectural Career Explorations
description: This course introduces students to a wide range of careers that frequently utilize design skills, spanning various interests and disciplines. Students will explore how fields such as architecture, urban planning, art, and design intersect with social, economic, and environmental concerns, examining the creative and professional practices that shape our highly designed contemporary environments. Throughout the class, students will gain foundational insights into each profession’s unique contributions, ethical considerations, and evolving challenges in an interconnected and global context. Emphasis is placed on the role of design in fostering sustainable development, cultural identity, and social impact, and students will learn to engage with these ideas in critical and novel ways.

title: BA Architectural Communications Core
description: This course will introduce the application of analog and digital media, verbal and visual communications, architectural graphic standards, and representational techniques in the architectural design and communication process. The class will establish proper workflow and best practices between various platforms. Through the course assignments, students will be challenged to expand their creative and conceptual approach to incorporating drawing and media into their design process through the intelligent use of appropriate tools to create well-crafted, evocative, and highly informative representations of your designs.

title: BA Architectural Research Methods
description: This course will introduce students to different approaches to architectural practice through the use of research methods. Students will learn to identify and think critically about a design problem and, develop techniques and strategies to communicate their ideas in response to that problem. Research Methods will explain a) definitions of different research methods, b) how to employ them, c) their strengths and challenges, and d) examples of their use by architects in the past.

title: BA Capstone Studio
description: The Capstone course will challenge students with a self-directed project that addresses an issue or problem in the Built Environment. This issue or problem they address should be derived from the coursework they have taken for their chosen area of exploration. PRECEDENT | the importance of research: To understand a problem, you must first understand the history and culture of the material you are working with. To do this, we explore the past – projects, ideas, books, papers.PROGRAM | defining the problem: Before we can design, we have to define a goal by understanding who we are designing for and what are their needs ITERATION | designing a solution:  For your final project, you will pursue a project that can address the problem you identified in your research.

title: BA Foundations of  Building Technology
description: Exploration of how a building’s design affects the human experience of its occupants thus defining how architecture is about people not buildings. People are fundamentally supported by the successful design of a building. Within this context the course explores how the human experience is affected by building designs and environmental demands for thermal comfort, environmental/resource conservation, and sustainability. Introduces environmental stewardship, fundamentals of passive thermal systems, and daylighting.

title: BA Introduction to Architectural Theory
description: This theory course will introduce students to the fundamentals of historical and contemporary  theories in architecture and its related fields (art, philosophy, technology, etc.). Emphasis is placed on the analysis and construction of written thought in two analytical essays on architectural theory subjects.

title: BAAS Seminar
description: The BAAS Seminar serves as the central spine of the degree, providing continuity, community, and a space for synthesizing ideas and experiences related to ongoing coursework providing a consistent cohort-based experience for students throughout the program. The seminar will meet weekly to discuss a topic relating to the  education and practice of architecture. After a brief presentation contextualizing the theme by the faculty member, students will be asked to reflect on their experience with that topic in their coursework and/or project how they can integrate the approach into future academic and professional planning. The intention of the seminar is to support students in shaping their own educational and professional journeys.

title: Bachelors Thesis
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Only students who have previously worked with a faculty member in a research group may register for bachelor's thesis credit, and then only with the permission of the faculty member. An undergraduate thesis is a publication-quality description of work done in previous semesters. At a minimum, a thesis must be published as a technical report; ideally, it should be submitted to a conference or journal. A bachelor's thesis is intended as an alternative to the senior project for students who are headed for graduate school.

title: Backcountry Ski Guide
description: Through class and field sessions, students examine resource management issues, and learn specific skills related to commercial guiding of backcountry skiers. Includes safety, consumerism, and Leave-No-Trace skills.

title: Backcountry Ski Touring - Wasatch Range
description: This course is designed to introduce students to the foundational techniques for skiing in backcountry alpine terrain in the Wasatch Range of Utah. Course content will focus on avalanche awareness (rescue, terrain, weather, snowpack and decision-making/human factors), travel techniques (split board, alpine and telemark, route-finding, laying of a skin track, terrain selection), side-country ethics, choosing appropriate tours, navigation, basic 1st aid, and field repairs. Course content will be learned and applied over one classroom session and four field-based experiences. Leave No Trace skills appropriate for the winter and information regarding natural resource management will also be covered in the course. Expert level skiing is not required.

title: Backcountry Yoga - Mindful Living in the Outdoors
description: This introductory class is designed for students to unplug, let go, and find their Zen in a nature based setting. The focus will be on forgetting about "what's next," making the connection between mind, body, and spirit and how we can more freely do this in nature by having a full sensory experience through sights, sounds, smells, etc. Students will also learn about making healthy living and lifestyle choices. Students will have the opportunity to learn the  necessary skills to enjoy entry level paddle boarding, hiking, as well as incorporating and practicing yoga both on land and on the water. Overnight camping, cooking outdoors, hiking and stand-up paddle boarding will be covered in this class.

title: Bad Bodies: Gender & Disability
college: CT - Sch for Cultural & Social Tran
description: This course introduces students to the field of disability studies and examines the intersections between theories of disability, on the one hand, and theories of gender, race/ethnicity, and sexuality, on the other. The course explores the ways in which bodies considered deviant or “bad” can also be understood also as defiant, resistant to conventional understandings of gendered, sexual, and “normal” identity. We will examine the ways in which disabled people have been and continue to be marginalized and dehumanized, but we’ll also explore the ways in which the ideas and practises of disability scholars, activists, and artists are remapping how all of us think about and experience gender, identity, and humanity.

title: Bad Bodies: Gender & Disability
college: CT - Sch for Cultural & Social Tran
description: This course introduces students to, or expands their knowledge in, the field of Disability Studies, particularly examining the intersections amongst disability and gender, race/ethnicity, class, and sexuality. The course explores how bodyminds often considered “bad” can also be understood as defiant, resistant to conventional understandings of “normal” identity. We will examine how disabled people have been and continue to be marginalized, but we’ll also explore how disability scholars, activists, and artists are remapping how we think about and experience gender, identity, and humanity.

title: @#$!:  Bad Words & Taboo Terms
description: This course is an introduction to linguistic study through the lens of taboo language, a pervasive part of all languages. The course surveys topics in modern linguistics by studying taboos in various languages. Students sensitive to obscene words are discouraged from enrolling, as are students who do not have a scholarly interest in taboo language.

title: Badminton: Elementary
description: Developing and/or improving the basic skills needed to actively enjoy the sport of badminton. Students will learn to perform the fundamental strokes, understand the basic rules and strategy.

title: Badminton: Intermediate
description: Ways to improve your badminton technique and strategy.

title: Balanchine: Graduate Seminar
description: In this graduate seminar, taught by one of Balanchine's leading men, Conrad Ludlow, the students will address the intricacies and the conventions of the Balanchine technique.  Aided by the Suki Schorer's definitive book, On Balanchine's Technique, stylistic, technical, and aesthetic issues will be discussed.  The context of this course is further personalized by anecdotes and memories of Professor Ludlow.

title: Ball/Core Cardio
description: This class involves the usage of Physio-balls in combination with a traditional cardiovascular training format.

title: Ball/Core Cardio

title: Ballet Basics for Non-Majors
description: Meets with BALLE 1140. Ballet technique for non-majors with limited or no experience.

title: Ballet Class Music: A Tutorial for Ballet Teachers
description: This course will include a comprehensive analysis of the predominant music/dance rhythms and forms commonly used in the ballet technique class. The students will use about 45% of their class time in studio labs developing skills in musically using and communicating established music/dance rhythms and forms. It is expected that they will com to understand the relationship that applicable musical elements have with ballet technique and artistry. This should help them understand and apply these skills in their own ballet technique experience as well as in their role as a ballet pedagogue.

title: Ballet History Non-Majors
description: A contextual study of the relationship and effect of ancient and early dance forms that laid the basis for the establishment of classical ballet during the Renaissance period. Changes in dance technique, production and style as they relate to political, religious, and artistic developments during specific periods. Emphasis on the two classical periods, the romantic period and the neoclassical period. Course culmination explores the relationship between classical ballet and current contemporary dance forms.

title: Ballet I for Non-Majors
description: A foundation course covering the basic vocabulary, technique, and styles of ballet.

title: Ballet II for Non-Majors
description: Ballet Technique for non-majors with some experience in ballet.

title: Ballet III for Non Majors
description: Ballet Technique for non-majors with considerable experience in ballet.

title: Ballet Pedagogy I
description: This course provides graduate students with a theoretical base, practical application of principles, and mentoring in the teaching of ballet.

title: Ballet Pedagogy I
description: This course covers techniques for teaching creative movement and for introducing classical ballet to children age 3-9. Students learn how to analyze technique progression, utilize the vocabulary of age-appropriate ballet movements, and develop teaching goals and objectives. The course is taught in a lecture and lab format.

title: Ballet Pedagogy II
description: This course builds upon topics covered in BALLE 6780, and focuses on providing graduate students with a theoretical base, practical application of principles, and mentoring in the teaching of dance.

title: Ballet Pedagogy II
description: This course is a continuation of BALLE 4780 and offers a more in-depth examination of the art of teaching classical ballet. It specifically includes material for ages 10-17. The student will: acquire techniques for teaching age-appropriate ballet movement vocabulary; learn how to incorporate class progression in the studio; develop a teaching curriculum, accompanying syllabi, and lesson plans for sequential levels of ballet technique.

title: Ballet Showcase
description: Student participation in ballet and modern dance student-choreographed works performed twice yearly. For ballet and modern dance majors.

title: Ballet Technique Analysis
description: This course requires the graduate student to attend the daily technique class, to prepare research materials significant to the concepts introduce in that class, and to share his/her research with other students in the class, thus transitioning the graduate student from class participant to class contributor.

title: Ballet Technique for Men II
description: Upper-division ballet technique for male majors. Meets with 3290, a co-ed class, during part of the semester, and meets in a male-only section during part of the semester to work on technique particularly needed by the male dancer.

title: Ballet Technique for Men III
description: Upper-division ballet technique for male majors. Meets with 4290, a co-ed class, during part of the semester, and meets in male-only section during part of the semester to work on technique particularly needed by the male dancer.

title: Ballet Technique for Men: Lower Division
description: Ballet technique for first-year majors. Meets with 2290, a co-ed class, during part of the semester, and meets in a male-only section during part of the semester to work on technique particularly needed by the male dancer.

title: Ballet Technique for Men: Utah Ballet
description: Advanced ballet technique for male majors. Meets with 4590, a co-ed class, during part of the semester, and meets in a male-only section during part of the semester to work on technique particularly needed by the male dancer.

title: Ballet Technique I
description: This course is the second of a two-semester sequence of ballet technique courses for freshman (first-year) Modern Dance majors. This course builds on material presented in DANC 1330, continuing to provide technical training in classical ballet technique and introducing students to a more extensive understanding of ballet terminology. Students receive instruction in principles of alignment, placement, and carriage in classical ballet.

title: Ballet Technique I
description: Ballet technique for first-year majors.

title: Ballet Technique I
description: This course is designed for freshmen (first-year) modern dance majors and serves as the foundation for continued ballet studies throughout the curriculum for Modern Dance majors. The course provides technical training in classical ballet technique and introduces students to ballet movement terminology. Students receive instruction in principles of alignment, placement, and carriage in classical ballet.

title: Ballet Technique II
description: Upper-division ballet technique for Ballet Majors.

title: Ballet Technique II - 2nd Semester

title: Ballet Technique III - 2nd Semester

title: Ballet Technique IV - 2nd Semester
description: This is a second of a two-semester sequence. The course provides modern dance majors with opportunities for mastery of ballet technique at an advanced level.

title: Ballet Technique: Ballet West Trainee
description: Advanced technique for Ballet West Trainees.

title: Ballet Technique: Graduate
description: Advanced ballet technique study for graduate students.

title: Ballet Technique: Professional
description: Advanced ballet technique credit for professional training as a member or apprentice with a professional company. Professional training credits must be approved by the School of Dance and overseen by a member of the faculty.

title: Banking Law
college: LW - S.J. Quinney College of Law
description: This course introduces the legal and regulatory framework of the banking system in the U.S.  The course begins with a review of the historical development of American banking and then moves to a discussion of various issues that have arisen as a result of this distinctive history, including the definition of the banking business, the rationales for bank regulation, geographic restrictions, liability issues, and limitations on bank activities.  The course also examines the growth of the modern "financial services" industry and the legal, political and public polity issues surrounding the most recent attempts to reform this industry in the context of a general overhaul of the banking system.

title: Bankruptcy
college: LW - S.J. Quinney College of Law
description: This introductory course studies the U.S. Bankruptcy Code, including the law of preferences, fraudulent transfers, executory contracts, and the bankruptcy relief available under Chapters 7, 11, and 13 of the Code. Basic consumer and business bankruptcies are explained, and current issues in bankruptcy law are addressed.

title: Bankruptcy Survey
college: LW - S.J. Quinney College of Law
description: With an eye toward both business and consumer issues, the course briefly surveys state law collection remedies and then focuses on federal bankruptcy relief available in cases under Chapter 7, Chapter 13 and Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code.

title: Baroque Art in Europe
description: The 17th century was a time of dynamic political, social, and religious changes calling for a re-examination of tradition and the purposes of art. Many artists in Italy, Flanders, Holland, Spain, France, and England experimented with ways of involving the viewer in their art for persuasion and more engagement in the issues of the day.

title: Baroque Music
description: In-depth discussions of issues related to Baroque music, including musical sources, notational systems, performance practice, and social context.

title: Baroque Music Grad
description: In-depth discussions of issues related to Baroque music, including musical sources, notational systems, performance practice, and social context.

title: Barre Tone
description: This course will involve a total body workout fusing elements of ballet, Pilates, and weight training into a circuit program. Emphasis of training will be placed on the hips, seat, core, and balance.

title: Basic Applied Electricity and Magnetism
description: In this course topics in advanced undergraduate electricity and magnetism (cf.PHYS 4420) are covered with an emphasis on the connection to technology. The course is taught with an innovative approach in which lectures, laboratories, and computation are integrated.

title: Basic Applied Modern Physics
description: In this course topics in undergraduate quantum mechanics, solid state physics, and thermal physics are covered with an emphasis on the connection to technology. The course is taught with an innovative approach in which lectures, laboratories, and computation are integrated.

title: Basic Architectural Communications I
description: Introduction to the practice and rationale underlying sketching and architectural graphic conventions as a way of communicating meaning.

title: Basic Architectural Communications II
description: This course covers concepts and tools for basic architectural communication.

title: Basic Assessment and Intervention for Struggling Readers: Next Steps Practicum
description: This graduate education course is designed to help educators develop in-depth theoretical and practical knowledge of effective, research-based assessment and intervention for struggling readers of all ages who have reached a primer level, but whose reading abilities are below mid-grade three level.  The course follows a "practicum model,"  in which educators build a conceptual framework for reading development and effective intervention through a year-long, mentored tutoring experience.

title: Basic Behavior Analysis
description: In this course students will develop a graduate level understanding of the basic assumptions, techniques, practices, and findings associated with the experimental analysis of behavior (EAB). Behavior science is comprised of three domains: application, basic research and theory & philosophy. EAB is the branch of behavior science involved in basic research. Findings from research within EAB serve as the basic building blocks of our science, as well as past, current and future practices in applied behavior analysis (ABA). A thorough understanding of the methods, assumptions and seminal works within EAB are integral to effective practice as a clinician.

title: Basic Cellular Neurobiology Lab
description: Methods and instrumentation of neurobiology: emphasizes electrophysiology with computerized data acquisition and control; features and phenomena associated with action potentials in nerve and muscle.

title: Basic Communications III
description: Concepts and tools for architectural communications.

title: Basic Digital Photography
description: An introduction to the basic principles of digital photography covering aperture, shutter and ISO exposure controls. We also explore light, color, storytelling and composition as methods to create images that communicate emotions and concepts. We will use image-editing software to adjust the digital image and for creating a library using keywords and metadata.

title: Basic Immunology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Study of immune system as it relates to human body's defense against foreign substances coming in contact with and entering the body.  It includes clinical and experimental topics in immunology.

title: Basic Immunology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This is a survey course covering the basic principles in Immunology with lectures provided by faculty directly involved in particular areas. The final third of the course will feature clinical and experimental topics in Immunology. The course is primarily slated for graduate and master students. It is also open for particularly interested undergrad students, but is not specifically intended as preparation for Med School due to its programmatic depth. Students should have some exposure to biochemistry, modern genetics, and cell biology. Undergrad students are encouraged to complete BIOL 2020, 2030 and 3510 prior to taking this course.
