title: Clinical  Internship I
description: One, part-time clinical placement, 16 weeks in length. Students practice patient management skills in the clinical environment under the direct supervision of experienced clinicians. Students observe and begin to perform supervised patient examination/measurement techniques, evaluate and interpret examination results, determine a prognosis, design and implement a thorough plan of care, and evaluate patient outcomes. The student will also practice and progressively develop a variety of skills critical for developing appropriate professionalism. Students should refer to the online course site for ongoing course updates and assignments.

title: Clinical & Public Health Informatics Terminologies & Standards II
description: This course is an extension of BMI 6120. Students will be introduced to additional terminologies and standards used in the fields of clinical and public health informatics. Learning will occur through lectures, hands-on exercises and projects to help students better understand how to apply the knowledge into practice in real clinical and/or public health settings.

title: Clinical and Behavioral Aspects of Occupational Injuries and Disease
description: This course is a didactic course to teach common diseases encountered in occupational medicine (as well as general medical practice). The course includes a significant amount of instructional time on musculoskeletal disorders and respiratory conditions. Evidence based treatment regimens for common conditions will be discussed.

title: Clinical and Behavioral Aspects of Preventive Medicine
description: This course utilizes the current recommendations from the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force, but updates it with cutting edge knowledge about evidence-based clinical preventive strategies.  The target audience is physicians and PhD candidates.

title: Clinical and Laboratory Hemostasis
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Focuses on clinical and laboratory evaluation of hematologic and hemostatic disorders. Students will participate in the coagulation consultation service and evaluate inpatients and outpatients with bleeding or thrombotic disorders. Students will also participate in two weekly conferences to discuss clinical and laboratory issues.

title: Clinical and Molecular Cancer Biology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: In alternating years, this course is focused on the current understanding of the molecular and cellular biology of cancer along with how this knowledge relates to the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of cancer.  The complementary sister-course is focused on clinical cancer biology.  It is designed for graduate students and post-doctoral fellows in basic science departments with an interest in modern principles and practice of oncology.  It will cover general principles and new developments in cancer etiology, detection, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention.  The course is organized around specific diseases, using advances in each area to highlight modern principles and practice of oncology.

title: Clinical and Translational Epidemiology Seminar
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: The clinical and translational seminar exposes students to research in progress over a wide variety of disease states. Students will lead a seminar and participate in others through readings and preparing questions for other speakers.

title: Clinical Application of Basic Sciences
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Second-year elective course.

title: Clinical Applications of Health Promotion and Integrative Health
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Clinical Applications of Health Promotion and Integrative Health will give students an opportunity to discuss how the themes of the pathway can be implemented into clinical practice both in self-care during the MS3 year and the care of patients. Students will meet four times over the year to discuss relevant material. Students will be expected to write about and discuss their clinical experiences. This course is the fifth in the Health Promotion Integrative Health Pathway; it provides one-half credit hour towards graduation. Course Goals As a result of successfully completing the Clinical Applications of Health Promotion and Integrative Health course, students will be able to: 1. Identify and utilize self-care strategies to manage the stress of MS3 year. This might include a focus on nutrition, physical activity, sleep, mindfulness, and/or connection to others. 2. Describe the relationships between health and disease and the following factors: emotion, stress, nutrition, physical activity, social support, spirituality, sleep, and environment. 3. Recognize the multivariate and sometimes unknown factors that influence health and healing. 4. Discuss how personal, cultural, ethnic, and spiritual beliefs shape an individual’s interpretation and experience of disease and its treatment. 5. Create meaningful health and wellness plans with patients. 6. Identify factors leading to well being of teams. 7. Use narrative medicine to manage thoughts and feelings that arise during clinical experiences.

title: Clinical Applications of Research & Evidence-based Practice
description: This course involves students investigating opportunities to improve care in a clinical environment. Students will learn to access and apply research data and current evidence to an identified problem. They will further analyze information that pertains to the problem and identify potential solutions supported by evidence. Students demonstrate competency by creating and implementing a durable project for their area of interest in nursing.

title: Clinical Applications of Therapeutic Recreation
description: This courses is an advanced study of the Therapeutic Recreation (TR) profession. Course content includes critical investigation of the professions theoretical foundation, an examination of the continuum of practice and program design, analysis of current research and evaluation of the profession as a whole.

title: Clinical Assessment and Research Methods Laboratory
description: Techniques used to assess nutritional status are discussed and practiced including analysis and interpretation of food intake, body composition, energy expenditure, biochemical indices, and physical anthropometric measurements. Clinical and research applications are emphasized. Biochemical laboratory methods to assess nutritional status are performed

title: Clinical Assessment for Nonclinical Researchers
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: This graduate course covers basic assessment methods that can be used by nonclinical scientists in a variety of research projects.  Both practical skills (test administration & scoring) & theoretical topics (psychometrics, test development) will be covered.

title: Clinical Cancer Biology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course is designed to complement the existing Molecular Biology of Cancer course.  The course is designed for graduate students and post-doctoral fellows in basic science and clinical departments with an interest in modern principles and practice of oncology.  The course will focus on general principles and new developments in cancer etiology, detection, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention.  The course is organized around specific diseases, using advances in each area to highlight various principles.

title: Clinical Cancer Genetics
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This hybrid course is designed to provide the fundamentals of clinical cancer genetics and genetic counseling of hereditary cancer syndromes. Topics include cancer screening, prevention, diagnosis and treatment. The course also includes an in-depth survey of cancer genetic syndromes and techniques to conduct appropriate cancer risk assessment for high risk patients. Students will be expected to review lectures and complete assessments online in addition to applying learned skills to practice cases in class. Core and guest lectures will be supplemented with interactive discussions and student presentations. This course aims to provide a foundation for the genetic counseling cancer rotation.

title: Clinical Capstone
description: This clinical and simulation capstone course focuses on transition to the professional nursing role. Emphasis is placed on the application and integration of concepts associated with professional practice as students work collaboratively with nurse preceptors and other members of the inter-professional team in selected clinical sites. Upon completion of this course students will be able to synthesize all previously learned knowledge in the delivery of safe and effective nursing care.

title: Clinical Capstone in Athletic Training
description: This clinical capstone project focuses on transitioning to a professional athletic trainer and making important decisions that impact patients' health care. Students will complete a capstone project that emphasizes evidence practice, quality improvement, and the inter-professional health care team.

title: Clinical Care Across the Lifespan
description: This course applies concepts related to the health and illness experience of specific populations. Emphasis is placed on the concepts associated with health promotion and illness prevention, risk reduction, and management of acute and chronic illness. Upon completion, the student should be able to apply concepts to individuals, families, and populations.

title: Clinical Care of Individuals and Families
description: This clinical course applies concepts related to the illness experience of individual patients and families.  Emphasis is placed on enhanced development of communication, information management, assessment, evaluation, and specified clinical skills.  Upon completion of this course, the student will be able to analyze data from a variety of sources for clinical decision-making in the safe provision of holistic evidence-based nursing care simulation.

title: Clinical Care of Vulnerable Populations
description: This clinical course applies concepts related to the health and illness experience of specific populations. Emphasis is placed on the concepts associated with health promotion and illness prevention, risk reduction, and management of acute and chronic illness. Upon completion, the student should be able to apply concepts to individuals, families, and populations.

title: Clinical Case Studies
description: Therapeutic problem-solving using case-study approach. Review of clinical literature.

title: Clinical Challenges
description: This course will provide students the opportunity to present clinically challenging cases to their peers, with a review of the literature, and discuss outcomes of difficult cases. Professionalism, Ethics, Patient Management, Diagnosis and Treatment Planning, and proper referral will be aspects of the presentation. Additional lectures, and guest lectures will present on subjects of advanced techniques, technologies, and evidence based treatments. Self assessment and peer assessment will be a primary focus of grading.

title: Clinical Chemistry
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course addresses clinical chemical analysis of human blood and body fluids in normal and abnormal physiological conditions. Emphasis on clinical testing methods, correlation of data and physiological condition, and identification of aberrant results affecting chemistry results. Topics include: human organ system function, endocrinology, blood gases, electrolytes, clinical laboratory calculations, and toxicology. This knowledge will also be applied to problem-solving case studies typical to the clinical setting.

title: Clinical Chemistry Laboratory
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course addresses laboratory applications in chemical analysis of blood and body fluids with emphasis on spectrophotometric methods, electrophoresis, and immunoassays. Students will participate in method evaluation studies, quality control testing, sample measurements, troubleshooting, and correlation of data with possible disease states or analytical issues.

title: Clinical Clerkship in Otolaryngology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This clerkship is designed as an intensive 4 week exposure to otolaryngology.  Clerkship is carried out at UH and PCMC and is designed to totally immerse the student in all activities of the otolaryngology service, including outpatient clinics, inpatient work-up and care, and participation in surgery.  Participation in the didactic sessions designed for residents and interns is also required.

title: Clinical Clerkship: Community
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This four-week clinical rotation provides an opportunity for the student to acquire skills in neurologic examination and diagnosis with a physician in the community.  Fulfills Neurology requirement.

title: Clinical Clerkship: VAMC
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This clinical rotation provides an opportunity to sharpen skills in neurologic examination and diagnosis at the VA Medical Center. Students are assigned to adult neurology units under the supervision of the neurology staff. Activities include direct patient care, daily ward rounds, procedures such as lumbar puncture, and participation in clinical conferences, brain-cutting sessions, multiple sclerosis clinic, muscle clinic, and the neurology outpatient clinics.

title: Clinical Concepts in Critical Care Nursing
description: The purpose of this course is to explore selected clinical concepts and skills used in critical care nursing and independent professional nursing.  Mastery of course content will enable the student to use critical thinking and research skills to identify, plan, and provide individualized patient care.  Expertise from life and work experiences will be used as a foundation from which to expand nursing practice in the critical care environment.

title: Clinical Concepts in Nursing
description: Selected clinical concepts and skills used for independent professional nursing are explored. Content enables use of diagnostic (inductive and deductive) reasoning to identify patient resources from which individualized approaches to patient care can be planned. Theoretical frameworks of diagnostic reasoning, the bifocal clinical model, and functional health patterns are integrated. Expertise from life and work experiences used as a foundation. Verbal, written, and problem-solving skills learned in previous educational experiences are extended.

title: Clinical Correlations
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This capstone course is designed to enhance students' clinical rotations by providing an opportunity for reflection of events, test results, ethical situations, troubleshooting problems and other experiences that occur during rotations and professional practice. In addition, students will explore a disease or condition through an interdisciplinary case study assignment. Students will also have the opportunity to evaluate their own professional behavior.

title: Clinical Cytopathology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Clinical rotation involving the cytopreparation laboratory and fine-needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB) service. Also prepares students for entry into profession and for certification examination in cytology. Thorough review of theoretical and practical laboratory cytology.

title: Clinical Cytopathology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: During this clinical rotation, students gain practical experience in phases of routine diagnostic non-gynecologic cytology, fine needle aspiration biopsy and daily laboratory function. Augments classroom learning.

title: Clinical Cytopathology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: During this clinical rotation, students gain practical experience in phases of routine diagnostic cytology and daily laboratory function. Augments classroom learning.

title: Clinical Cytopathology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: During this clinical rotation, students gain practical experience in phases of routine diagnostic gynecologic cytology and daily laboratory function. Augments classroom learning.

title: Clinical Database Design
description: Required for Nursing Informatics students to develop competencies in the development and maintenance of clinical databases or applications in solving clinical problems including design methods, database structures, indexing, data dictionaries, retrieval languages, and data security.

title: Clinical Database Design
description: Development and maintenance of clinical databases or application in solving clinical problems. Design methods, database structures, indexing, data dictionaries, retrieval languages, and data security are presented.

title: Clinical Database Design
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Development and maintenance of clinical databases or application in solving clinical problems. Design methods, database structures, indexing, data dictionaries, retrieval languages, and data security are presented.

title: Clinical Database Design
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Clinical database is the foundation and essential components of clinical information systems such electronic health records, clinical decision support systems, and big data warehousing environments. Designing a clinical database may require thorough understanding of the theories of database systems, underlying information models, and architectural features of clinical information systems. The course provides systematic learning activities for fundamentals of clinical databases and practices of database design. In addition, students spend time learning SQL (Structured Query Language) to develop relational databases and use SQL queries to answer clinically relevant questions using example data sets in the databases. Lastly, the course will cover learning of how clinical information models are associated with database design and state-of-the art trends in the healthcare IT industry.

title: Clinical Database Design Lab
description: Focuses on development and maintenance of clinical databases for application in solving clinical problems. Laboratory sessions support the design and implementations of a database to solve a clinical problem. Techniques, such as SQL, object oriented programming and GUI development are used.

title: Clinical Decision Support
description: Decision-making theories and strategies related to clinical reasoning discussed. Methods of computer support for different reasoning strategies in clinical settings presented.

title: Clinical Decision Support
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Clinical decision support (CDS) “provides clinicians, staff, patients, or other individuals with knowledge and person-specific information, intelligently filtered or presented at appropriate times, to enhance health and health care.” CDS is one of the most critical components of health information systems because they can improve patient outcomes and lead to higher-quality health care. With the adoption of electronic health record (EHR) systems reaching over 90% of healthcare settings in the U.S., unprecedented opportunities exist to improve the quality and value of healthcare through CDS interventions at the national scale. However, to improve patient outcomes, increase clinician efficiency, and reduce clinician burnout, CDS tools need to be designed and implemented according to best practices and disseminated across healthcare settings through standards-based approaches.

title: Clinical Decision Support
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: The course includes asynchronous and synchronous methods to introduce students to CDS tools, implementation, design and future efforts.

title: Clinical Decision Support Lab
description: Decision making theories and strategies related to clinical reasoning are discussed.  Methods of computer support or different reasoning strategies in clinical settings are presented.  Laboratory sessions provide an opportunity  to explore research strategies and to develop prototype systems to support clinical decision making.

title: Clinical Diagnosis and Management by Laboratory Methods
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Full-time, four-week elective currently offered in February. It consists of three 50 minute didactic sessions per day. The remaining time will be spent with directed reading and independent study. The elective will stress concepts of laboratory decision making, appropriate choice of laboratory tests in given clinical situations, test interpretations, common pitfalls, use of test algorithms, etc. Students will be evaluated by their performance on a final examination.

title: Clinical Diagnostic Reasoning
description: Required for Doctor of Nursing Nurse Practitioner students to integrate the principles of advanced clinical problem-solving into their practice to promote safety and quality of care.

title: Clinical Elective
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: The primary objective is for the individual to become competent in a clinical area of choice and gain an appreciation of the process involved in preparing, analyzing, interpreting and reporting techniques. The individual will be encouraged to learn diagnostic and laboratory management principles of adult and pediatric clinical pathology in the context of actual patient care through consultation with clinicians, chart review and discussion of interesting cases, clinical seminars, rounds and management meetings, and didactic presentations.

title: Clinical Electives
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Students will complete an elective rotation in a specialty area of the clinical laboratory.

title: Clinical Exam in Athletic Training I
description: An upper-division course designed for athletic training majors. Utilizing knowledge of anatomy and physiology, students will be introduced to Evidence Based prevention, evaluation, and rehabilitation of lower extremity injury and other sport related conditions.

title: Clinical Exam in Athletic Training II
description: Utilizing knowledge of anatomy and physiology, students will be introduced to prevention, evaluation, and rehabilitation techniques for the head, spine, and upper extremity. Evidence based medicine will be used to research injuries and sport related problems related to this region. This is an upper-division course designed for athletic training majors.

title: Clinical Experience I
description: Four part-time clinical placements, 3-4 weeks in length. Students practice patient management skills in the clinical environment under the direct supervision of clinical preceptors. Students observe and begin to perform supervised patient encounters. The student will also begin to integrate and progressively develop a variety of skills critical for developing appropriate professionalism.

title: Clinical Experience II
description: Two part-time clinical placements, 3-4 weeks in length. Students practice patient management skills in the clinical environment under the direct supervision of clinical preceptors. Students observe and begin to perform supervised patient encounters. The student will also begin to integrate and progressively develop a variety of skills critical for developing appropriate professionalism.

title: Clinical Experience II
description: Part-time clinical experience one afternoon per week. Students are supervised and evaluated by clinical instructors. Students practice evaluation, treatment skills, and appropriate professional behavior learned during the semester.

title: Clinical Experience III
description: Optional clinical experience designed to help students become further socialized to the clinical environment and the professionals who work within it, and to practice and integrate specialized knowledge, practical skills and professional behaviors into the specialized clinical world.

title: Clinical Experience in Athletic Training I
description: Clinical rotations in the athletic training field designed for second year student athletic trainers.

title: Clinical Experience in Athletic Training II
description: Clinical experience in the athletic training field designed for the senior student athletic trainer.

title: Clinical Experience IV
description: Part-time clinical experience one afternoon per week. Students are supervised and evaluated by clinical instructors; practice evaluation, treatment skills, and appropriate professional behavior learned during the semester.

title: Clinical Externship in Audiology
description: Full time experience in audiologic settings. Provides final experience necessary for doctoral preparation as a clinical audiologist.

title: Clinical Genetics
description: Provide the student with knowledge of the principles and application of human genetics, as they apply to the health care professional.

title: Clinical Genetics
description: Provides the student with knowledge of principles and application of human genetics as they apply to the health care professional.

title: Clinical Genetics
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Clinical genetics is concerned with the diagnosis and management of the individual or family with an inherited or genetic condition or birth defect.  In this rotation the student will learn to evaluate individuals by attending Genetic and Metabolic Clinics and will assist with inpatient consultations.  They will attend and participate in patient review conferences and prenatal diagnosis conference.  Didactic focused learning is also available.  If desired, there is opportunity to present a case study or write one up for publication.

title: Clinical Genetics Across the Lifespan
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course consists of a series of lectures on a wide variety of genetic disorders, their natural history over the course of an individual’s life, medical management, available treatment, and inheritance patterns. Lectures will be given by a variety of content experts. The application of medical and genetic information to genetic counseling with families will be emphasized.This course consists of a series of lectures on a wide variety of genetic disorders, their natural history, available treatment and inheritance patterns. The application of the medical and genetic information to genetic counseling with families will be emphasized.

title: Clinical Gerontology
description: An overview of the biopsychosocial issues of the aging process and the impact these might have upon treatment and rehabilitation of the individual when they become ill.  Role of the health care provider in maintaining function and promoting self-efficacy/self care through the use of community, personal and family resources.  Selected chronic illnesses will be described and discussed in terms of the effect upon the coping skills of the patient and caregiver, the health care provider, and the health care system.

title: Clinical Grand Rounds and Case-based Scenarios
description: Case-based guided discussions relative to clinical skills and sciences.

title: Clinical Hematology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course examines normal hematopoiesis, hemoglobin structure, function, synthesis and degradation; red blood cell morphology and metabolic processes; the pathogenesis and pathophysiology of anemia; morphology function, and metabolic processes of normal white blood cells and platelets; and hematologic diseases resulting in abnormal leukocyte production and morphology. Discussion of leukemias, other hematologic malignancies, and special laboratory testing procedures will be provided.

title: Clinical Hematology Laboratory
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course provides hands-on activities in a laboratory setting for the evaluation of erythrocytes, leukocytes, platelets and hematologic diseases. Practical skills and the theoretical information on diagnostic tests performed in a clinical hematology laboratory are employed.

title: Clinical Hemostasis
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: A discussion of normal hemostasis, hemostatic disorders, the associated clinical symptoms, and the appropriate laboratory evaluation necessary for diagnosis. Laboratory sessions help to develop skills necessary for the performance of diagnostic tests.

title: Clinical Hypnosis
description: A beginning through intermediate course focused on practical skill development in using hypnosis clinically. Content includes facilitating hypnotic induction and phenomena, deepening techniques, practice in formulating hypnotic suggestions and constructing therapeutic metaphors, teaching patients self-hypnosis and anxiety management, administering hypnotizability scales, strategies and techniques for pain management, methods of unconscious exploration, hypnosis and memory, age regression and working with victims of abuse, applications with medical problems, habit disorders, methods of ego-strengthening and enhancing self-esteem, analysis of videotapes of Dr. Milton H. Erickson, technique selection and treatment planning, and ego-state therapy. Over 100 pages of practical handouts are included. The course is pre-approved toward national certification in clinical hypnosis. **Course offered Fall only every other year**

title: Clinical Hypnosis
description: A beginning through intermediate course focused on practical skill development in using hypnosis clinically. Content includes facilitating hypnotic induction and phenomena, deepening techniques, practice in formulating hypnotic suggestions and constructing therapeutic metaphors, teaching patients self-hypnosis and anxiety management, administering hypnotizability scales, strategies and techniques for pain management, methods of unconscious exploration, hypnosis and memory, age regression and working with victims of abuse, applications with medical problems, habit disorders, methods of ego-strengthening and enhancing self-esteem, analysis of videotapes of Dr. Milton H. Erickson, technique selection and treatment planning, and ego-state therapy. Over 100 pages of practical handouts are included. The course is pre-approved toward national certification in clinical hypnosis. **Course offered Fall only every other year**

title: Clinical Hypnosis
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: A basic and intermediate-level course that teaches practical skills in clinical hypnosis. Topics include induction and deepening, pain management, self-hypnosis, psychosomatic disorders, and methods of unconscious exploration.

title: Clinical Immunohematology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course covers transfusion medicine procedures and blood group serology including: ABO, Rh and other blood groups, antibody screen and identification, crossmatch and special tests, blood donation, transfusion therapy, transfusion reactions, hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn, and immune hemolytic anemias. It will introduce theoretical perspectives, professional practice with an emphasis in application, and ultimately prepare graduates for a career in a clinical blood bank.

title: Clinical Immunohematology Laboratory
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This simulated clinical laboratory experience provides the opportunity to perform routine testing and resolve common serologic problems. Students are also introduced to laboratory management, accreditation, and regulatory standards.

title: Clinical Immunology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Training in clinical immunology, pediatric rheumatology, and allergy evaluation and management of patients with immunodeficiency, childhood rheumatic disease, and allergic diseases, including developing a working knowledge of common immunologic tests. Lecture series and laboratory instruction by members of the division. Research opportunity, if desired.

title: Clinical Immunology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Clinical Immunology is an introduction to basic immunology. The course reviews theoretical principles of immunology and provides an overview of using basic immunologic, serologic, and molecular technologies to diagnose disease. Hypersensitivity, autoimmunity, immunodeficiencies, tumor immunology, transplant medicine, serologic detection of viral and bacterial diseases, and immunization and vaccinology will be discussed in detail.

title: Clinical Immunology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: The course introduces theoretical principles of immunology and provides an overview of basic concepts in immunology and serologic techniques used to diagnose disease.  Discussion of immunological responses include: hypersensitivity, autoimmunity, immunoproliferative disorders, and immunodeficiencies.  Course replaces MD LB 5030 as required immunology courses for MLS Program undergraduate students only.  It also incorporates content of MDLB 3750

title: Clinical Immunology Laboratory
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course focuses on representative serology and immunology principles, procedures, methodology, and laboratory safety. Selected diseases will also be discussed.

title: Clinical Immunology Techniques
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: A short course to accompany PATH 5030. Focus on representative clinical immunology techniques/ procedures and diseases.

title: Clinical Information Systems Architecture
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course will review and describe the various architectural components that comprise modern clinical information systems. The course will examine clinical data repositories, clinical decision support systems, knowledge repositories, terminology servers, and interface engines. How these components may be linked together using various technologies will be described. The course will also review architectures for the clinical application layer. How these components are used in the public health and translational and clinical research environments will be analyzed. Other architectural considerations such as mobile technology and service-oriented architectures will also be presented. Throughout the semester, the role of the informaticist in CIS architecture will be emphasized.

title: Clinical Instruction in Nursing Education
description: The purpose of this course is to apply educational theories and principles of clinical instruction across practice settings. Emphasis is placed on teaching within the framework of the learner's identified content/clinical area.

title: Clinical Internship I
description: One full-time session of clinical experience eight weeks in length. Students practice evaluations, program planning, treatment procedures, and appropriate professional behavior. Competency based objectives and skills are practiced under the direct supervision of and evaluated by a clinical instructor.

title: Clinical Internship I
description: One full-time clinical placements, 15 weeks in length. Students practice patient management skills in the clinical environment under the direct supervision of clinical preceptors. Students observe and begin to perform supervised patient encounters. The student will also begin to integrate and progressively develop a variety of skills critical for developing appropriate professionalism.

title: Clinical Internship II
description: Two full-time clinical placements, 7-8 weeks in length. Students practice patient management skills in the clinical environment under the direct supervision of clinical preceptors. Students observe and begin to perform supervised patient encounters. The student will also begin to integrate and progressively develop a variety of skills critical for developing appropriate professionalism.

title: Clinical Internship II
description: One full-time session of clinical experience eight weeks in length. Students practice evaluations, program planning, treatment procedures, and appropriate professional behavior. Competency-based objectives and skills are practiced under the direct supervision of and evaluated by a clinical instructor.

title: Clinical Internship II
description: Students practice patient management skills in the clinical environment under the direct supervision of an experienced clinician. Students perform patient examination/measurement techniques, evaluate and interpret examination results, determine a prognosis, design and implement a thorough plan of care, and evaluate patient outcomes. The student will also practice and progressively develop a variety of skills critical for developing appropriate professionalism. Students should refer to the online course site for ongoing course updates and assignments.

title: Clinical Internship III
description: Two, part-time clinical placements, 8 weeks each in length. Students practice patient management skills in the clinical environment under the direct supervision of an experienced clinician. Students perform patient examination/measurement techniques, evaluate and interpret examination results, determine a prognosis, design and implement a thorough plan of care, and evaluate patient outcomes. The student will also practice and progressively develop a variety of skills critical for developing appropriate professionalism. Students should refer to the online course site for ongoing course updates and assignments.

title: Clinical Internship in Audiology
description: Supervised clinical internship in University Speech-Language-Hearing Clinic. The University of Utah Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders requires training of audiology graduate students in a minimum of 100 clinical/contact hours spent in on-campus clinical experiences for a Doctorate of Audiology Degree and for ASHA certification. This course provides graduate audiology students with clinical practicum at the University of Utah Speech-Language-Hearing clinic provided by persons holding the ASHA Certificate of Clinical Competence.

title: Clinical Internship IV
description: Students practice patient management skills in the clinical environment under the direct supervision of an experienced clinician. Students perform patient examination/measurement techniques, evaluate and interpret examination results, determine a prognosis, design and implement a thorough plan of care, and evaluate patient outcomes. The student will also practice and progressively develop a variety of skills critical for developing appropriate professionalism. Students should refer to the online course site for ongoing course updates and assignments.

title: Clinical Internship V
description: One, part-time clinical placement, 16 weeks in length. Students practice patient management skills in the clinical environment under the direct supervision of an experienced clinician. Students perform patient examination/measurement techniques, evaluate and interpret examination results, determine a prognosis, design and implement a thorough plan of care, and evaluate patient outcomes. The student will also practice and progressively develop a variety of skills critical for developing appropriate professionalism. Students should refer to the online course site for ongoing course updates and assignments.

title: Clinical Internship with Seminar--III
description: Third optional, 12-week, Level-II clinical internship in specialty setting to increase skills as an entry-level occupational therapist. Seminar to integrate theory with application of treatment principles. Students practice evaluations, program planning and treatment procedures under the supervision of a licensed occupational therapist.

title: Clinical Internship with Seminar-I
description: First 12-week, Level-II clinical internship in either a community-based or health-care based setting to qualify for professional certification and registration. Seminar to integrate theory with application of treatment principles. Students  practice evaluations, program planning and treatment procedures under the supervision of a licensed occupational therapist.

title: Clinical Internship with Seminar-II
description: Second 12-week, Level-II clinical internship in either a community-based or health-care based setting to qualify for professional certification and registration. Seminar to integrate theory with application of treatment principles. Students practice evaluations, program planning and treatment procedures under the supervision of a licensed occupational therapist.

title: Clinical Investigation Workshop Series
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Workshop series designed for students pursuing their Master in Clinical Investigation.

title: Clinical Management Clerkship
description: Advanced clinical clerkship in pharmacy management.

title: Clinical Management Clerkship (RxAmerica)
description: Advanced clerkship in Clinical Management.  This will include, but not be limited to, organizational structure, P&T Committees, interconnection between formulary design and benefit design, PBM interventions, participate in the measurement of current clinical interventions, discuss PBM issues as they relate to key stakeholders, and improve verbal and written communication skills through active participation in projects.

title: Clinical Management of Pain
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Rotation which will introduce the student to the pathophysiology of pain and the management of acute pain, chronic malignant pain and chronic non-malignant pain for inpatients, home care patients and ambulatory care.  Students will receive training through case presentations and bedside teaching.  During the rotation, students will attend acute pain service rounds, see patients through the pain management center, and participate in Hospice team rounds.

title: Clinical Medical Ethics
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Student will develop skills in moral reasoning, become acquainted with major ethical theories and primary ethical principles, be able to identify and present ethical problems, and become familiar with selected aspects of health law as they bear on ethical issues in medicine. Several out of hospital activities are included.

title: Clinical Medicine I
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This multidimensional course will prepare students to obtain patient history and perform an integrated physical exam. Special emphasis on interviewing skills, interpretation of laboratory results and medical data bases, and search strategies for the practice of evidence-based medicine.

title: Clinical Medicine II
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Comprehensive study of the various body systems and common primary-care problems particular to the areas of: gastroenterology, ophthalmology, orthopedics, nephrology, dermatology, urology, cardiology, endocrinology, obstetrics/gynecology, neurology, and hematology/oncology.

title: Clinical Medicine III
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Comprehensive study of the various body systems and common primary-care problems particular to the areas of: gastroenterology, ophthalmology, orthopedics, nephrology, dermatology, urology, cardiology, endocrinology, obstetrics/gynecology, neurology, and hematology/oncology.

title: Clinical Method Curriculum 1
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This Clinical Method curriculum is a four year longitudinal development series of courses required of all medical students. It emphasizes acquisition of core clinical skills and medical decision making capacity along the domains of: history taking, physical examination, clinical test selection and interpretation, procedure selection of performance, accessing/interpreting/applying medical literature, patient and inter/professional communication and documentation, clinical reasoning, health care system navigation, patient safety and quality improvement, and self-direction and self-assessment. A learning community model of core faculty mentors following students through their training is central to the education methods employed in the curriculum.

title: Clinical Methods in Audiology Practice
description: This undergraduate course will provide students interested in speech and hearing science the opportunity to learn about the profession of audiology and develop some fundamental clinical audiology skills. Students will develop foundational knowledge and skills for standard testing protocols implemented in diagnostic audiological assessments and will perform these clinical skills under the direct supervision of a licensed audiologist in the audiology clinic at the University of Utah Speech-Language-Hearing Clinic. Students will also have the opportunity to observe audiology patient appointments at the clinic.

title: Clinical Methods in Communication Disorders
description: This course is designed to provide advanced undergraduate students with an introduction to clinical methods and principles of clinical practice in speech-language pathology and audiology. Topics and activities include the ASHA Code of Ethics, public laws, observation, documentation, assessing/treating communication disorders, writing reports, selecting goals, managing behavior, and interviewing/counseling; students also complete 25 hours of clinical observation.

title: Clinical Microbiology I
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Provides a basic understanding of medical microbiology: characteristics of clinically significant bacteria, their biochemical profiles, media for isolation, identification of select pathogens, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Also introduces clinically significant viruses and mycobacteria and means for their laboratory identification.

title: Clinical Microbiology II
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Students will learn about the diagnostic implications of clinical microbiology learned in previous MD LB courses. Emphasis on the clinical correlation of organisms infecting major organ systems, methods and rationale for laboratory identification of groups of clinically significant organisms and distinction from the normal microbiome, and rationale for proper specimen collection, transport, and processing.

title: Clinical Microbiology Laboratory I
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Students will participate in laboratory exercises highlighting basic identification processes and susceptibility methods for major groups of bacterial pathogens.

title: Clinical Microbiology Laboratory II
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This is an intensive laboratory course in which students will process simulated patient samples. Emphasis will be placed on processes for identifying and documenting results for the identification of clinically significant bacterial pathogens.

title: Clinical Microscopy
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Four sessions weekly. Course provides detailed instruction in microscopic findings of female genital tract and the Pap Test. Cancerous conditions, pre-cancerous conditions, infectious processes, and related disorders are covered.

title: Clinical Microscopy
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Four sessions weekly. Covers detailed microscopic study of the respiratory tract, gastro-intestinal tract, body cavity fluids, urinary tract, cerebrospinal fluids, and fine-needle aspiration (FNAB) biopsy.

title: Clinical Nursing Research Seminar
description: Focus on issues and problems associated with conducting research in clinical settings. A research practicum may be taken concurrently.

title: Clinical Ophthalmology at a Community Clinic
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Students work with an ophthalmologist in private practice who demonstrates advanced use of ophthalmoscope and slit lamp, and provides in-depth exposure to diagnosis and treatment of common eye problems.

title: Clinical Oral Pathology & Oral Medicine
description: This course reviews oral pathology/oral medicine entities of the hard and soft tissues with emphasis on diagnosis and management. This is a comprehensive course that requires description, differential diagnosis, and diagnosis and management of the entities encountered in dental practices.

title: Clinical Outcomes Management I
description: Clinical Outcomes Management I is designed to assist the student in developing awareness of factors that contribute to improving health care and outcomes for patients.  The content is distributed within 2 modules-Illness/disease Management, and Knowledge Management.  Each module is 1.5 credits.  Specific topics that are covered are listed under course content.

title: Clinical Outcomes Management II
description: This course is a continuation of COM I, designed to assist the student in developing awareness of additional factors that contribute to improving health care and outcomes for patients.  The content is distributed within 2 modules-Health Promotion/Disease Reduction/Prevention management and Evidence Based Practice.  Each module is 1.5 credits.  Specific topics that are covered in each module are listed under course content.

title: Clinical Pathology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: The student will be exposed to the field of Laboratory Medicine (Clinical Pathology) through a variety of media.  These include case conferences, laboratory rotations, and didactic session with pathology faculty.  The student will work with the course director to tailor the teaching objectives of this elective.  This course is intended for those students who are considering a career in Pathology.  Faculty approval should be obtained two months prior to beginning the course.

title: Clinical Pharmacology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: An introduction to the basic principles of pharmacology, including pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. It provides a foundation for students to learn more about and subsequently utilize pharmacotherapeutics in the practice of patient-centered care.

title: Clinical Pharmacology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: An introduction to the basic principles of pharmacology, including pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. It provides a foundation for students to learn more about and subsequently utilize pharmacotherapeutics in the practice of patient-centered care.

title: Clinical Pharmacology Faculty Consultations
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course is designed to initially help the student choose the Clinical Pharmacology Program research track (e.g., pharmacometrics or special populations) and the thesis research project, and guide the student in the preparation of the thesis defense and document. Students will receive individual instruction, including one-to-one discussions of their planned and ongoing projects.

title: Clinical Pharmacology in Special Populations
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course establishes a foundation for understanding the clinical significance of the pharmacological effects of drugs across different stages of life and human development.

title: Clinical Pharmacology Non-thesis Independent Study
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This is a hands-on course where students will be exposed to projects in the clinical pharmacology of special populations and/or pharmacometrics. Students complete individualized and often self-paced plans of study. Students will review recent literature on their interest, work on the wet beach, and retrospective or prospective projects of their interest. This course will help students to choose the research project topic for their dissertation.

title: Clinical Pharmacology Research Orientation
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: The Clinical Pharmacology Research Orientation is a course designed to introduce students to topics in clinical pharmacology, in vitro/ in vivo model studies, analytical method development, biostatistics, clinical trial simulation, and optimal trial design. The course will be offered as one-on-one sessions with the faculty members of the Division of Clinical Pharmacology and work hands-on in the laboratories. The course's objectives are to: 1. Familiarize the individual with particular areas of clinical pharmacology-related research. 2. Teach the individual appropriate research techniques and research design.

title: Clinical Pharmacy Seminar
description: Seminars in pathophysiology, drug therapy of specific disease states, and other topics relevant to clinical practice.

title: Clinical Physiology
description: This course provides a review of basic physiology of the major organ systems and includes an introduction to advanced topics in human physiology. Emphasis is placed on topics relevant to general nursing practice in individuals across the lifespan. Normal body function and the human response to illness will be a focus of the course.

title: Clinical Physiology
description: This course will include a review of basic physiology of the major organ systems and an introduction to current advanced topics in physiology.  It will emphasize topics relevant to the advanced practice nursing and will serve as a preparatory course for NURS 6007.

title: Clinical Placement
college: LW - S.J. Quinney College of Law

title: Clinical Practice with Grief and Loss
description: This course presents models of grief and bereavement applicable to social work practice with individuals and families. Emphasis is placed on direct practice knowledge and clinical skills understood in the profession to constitute what is called “grief therapy.” The Worden model, consisting of the ‘Four Tasks of Mourning’, is the primary model used in this course to guide students in their development. In addition, diverse experiences of loss and non-death related loss are considered across the lifespan.

title: Clinical Practicum for Nursing Education Specialty
description: The purpose of this practicum experience is to synthesize knowledge in the planning and provision of advanced nursing care at the Master's level to improve health outcomes for individuals, families, communities, and/or populations within a clinical focus area. Emphasis is placed on application of advanced skills in comprehensive assessment, systems-based practice, safe transitions in care, leadership, quality improvement, and translation of evidence into practice in designing, implementing and evaluating plans/programs of care.

title: Clinical Practicum in Speech-Language Pathology
description: The University of Utah Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders requires training of graduate students in a minimum of 150-175 clinical clock hours in on-campus clinical experiences. This course provides graduate speech-language students with clinical practicum in The University of Utah Speech-Language Clinic and at selected off-campus facilities with supervision provided by persons holding the ASHA Certificate of Clinical competence.

title: Clinical Preceptorship in Otolaryngology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This clinical preceptorship is designed as an intensive 2 to 4 week rotation in otolaryngology. During this period of time, the student works closely with the otolaryngology attending staff.  This close association fosters involvement in all aspects of the clinical practice of otolaryngology.

title: Clinical Prevention & Health Promotion
description: Small group conferences integrating principles of health promotion and disease prevention.

title: Clinical Prevention & Population Health
description: Introduction to the philosophy and need for preventive dentistry by developing the student's concepts of self-motivation; knowledge of dental diseases and abnormalities; application of the principles of fluoridation and patient motivation. The student will develop skills for effective oral hygiene with reference of disclosing agents, toothbrushing, flossing, oral physiotherapy aids, and topical fluorides.

title: Clinical Principles of Patient Management I
description: This course is designed to help the student apply the didactic principles they learned in Dent 7610 to clinical practice. The students will be taught how to review patient histories to identify medically complex situations. Students will begin to search for 3 patients that they can utilize in their complex management portfolio. Students will also be taught how to use electronic health records to refer patients to medical colleagues.

title: Clinical Principles of Patient Management II
description: Students will be taught how to search for and review the diagnostic and laboratory results of their medically complex patients. The student will be taught what bearing these results may have on the management of systemic disease. The student will also be familiarized with relevant medical terminology and how to communicate with medical colleagues about collaboration on patient treatment. The student will continue to search for the 3 patients that will comprise their complex management portfolio.

title: Clinical Problem Solving Through Strategic Analysis I
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: First semester of a two semester course sequence focused on the process of strategic analysis of complex clinical problem solving through evaluation of diagnostic processes, current therapeutic approaches, and clinical outcomes. Students will learn to critically evaluate real-world clinical problems from a global perspective, and then identify diagnostic and therapeutic deficiencies that can be addressed through the process of innovating medical technologies. The academic-based lectures in clinical problem solving through bioinnovation will be reinforced through applied application of course material in clinic-based workshops. The course will provide the academic foundation for mastery of the entire spectrum of the problem solving process from clinical needs finding to need analysis, concept generation and refinement to prototyping, intellectual property protection, and business planning. The text-based lecture series will be complimented with interactive lectures that provide real-world examples of the medical innovation process given by guest lecturers who have successfully navigated the strategic biodesign process and impacted healthcare through innovating technologies. The first semester of this course sequence will focus on clinical needs finding, needs screening, concept generation, and concept selection.

title: Clinical Problem Solving Through Strategic Analysis II
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Second semester of a two semester course sequence focused on the process of strategic analysis of complex clinical problem solving through evaluation of diagnostic processes, current therapeutic approaches, and clinical outcomes. Students will learn to critically evaluate real-world clinical problems from a global perspective, and then identify diagnostic and therapeutic deficiencies that can be addressed through the process of innovating medical technologies. The academic-based lectures in clinical problem solving through bioinnovation will be reinforced through applied application of course material in clinic-based workshops. The course will provide the academic foundation for mastery of the entire spectrum of the problem solving process from clinical needs finding to need analysis, concept generation and refinement to prototyping, intellectual property protection, and business planning. The text-based lecture series will be complimented with interactive lectures that provide real-world examples of the medical innovation process given by guest lecturers who have successfully navigated the strategic biodesign process and impacted healthcare through innovating technologies. The second semester of this course sequence will focus on case studies, regulatory compliance, marketing and stakeholders, business strategies, financing, and business development.

title: Clinical Problem-Solving for Medical Technology Innovations
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Clinical Problem Solving for Medical Technology Innovations introduces students to a structured method for developing high-impact, innovative, disruptive medical devices and technologies with potential for successful commercialization and translation into real-world clinical practice. The foundation of this method is the structure described in the Stanford Biodesign system (Yack et al., see textbook information below). Students will learn to approach real-world clinical problems from a multidisciplinary global perspective, and then to identify diagnostic and therapeutic deficiencies that can be addressed through the process of innovating medical technologies. Students will also learn to incorporate end-user feedback, U.S. FDA regulatory assessment, intellectual property (IP) assessment, and business commercialization perspectives in the initial development of new technologies. This course will provide the academic foundation for mastery of a structured medical technology innovation and development process from clinical needs finding to needs analysis. Online module completion, textbook chapter reading assignments, and self-study assignments are critical.

This course will provide the academic foundation for mastery of a structured medical technology innovation and development process from clinical needs finding to needs analysis. Online module completion, textbook chapter reading assignments, and self-study assignments are critical.

title: Clinical Problems in Occupational Therapy
description: Specific application of occupational therapy practice in varied health/community settings. Seminar to integrate theory with application of treatment. Prior to enrolling, student and sponsoring faculty should write a contract defining objectives, goals and criteria for the course.

title: Clinical Systems Analysis Lab

The organizational context of complex health care settings and informatics roles will be examined as they relate to clinical systems analysis. Methods for clinical systems analysis and requirements determination will be emphasized. The course project will be a request for proposal (RFP) based on the clinical information requirements of a local health care setting. Clinical laboratory sessions will be used for field-based clinical systems analysis activities and development of a request for proposal (RFP) based on identified clinical information requirements.

title: Clinical Systems Implementation Lab
description: This course addresses the implementation, management and outcomes of clinical information systems (CISs). Concepts and theories related to innovation diffusion, organizations, implementation, and group processes are applied. Project management techniques including human and fiscal resourcing are applied throughout the course. Common strategies and major implementation issues are evaluated and applied. Approaches for evaluating the impacts of clinical information systems are critiqued. Clinical laboratory sessions will focus on the analysis and synthesis of key success and major risk factors of clinical systems in integrated delivery systems using material in case studies, field sites and CIS vendors.

title: Clinical Toxicology
description: At the end of the course the student should be able to: Identify the necessary pieces of information to analyze a poisoning, describe the services of the Poison Control Center and the role it plays in the practice of pharmacy, understand the principles involved in the general approach to the poisoned patient, describe the toxicology mechanism of action for each of the agents discussed, describe the typical presentation following a poisoning with each specific agent, and outline a specific management plan for each of the agents discussed. This course will integrate knowledge of pharmacology, medicinal chemistry, pharmacokinetics and therapeutics. This course is intended to provide a foundation for future pharmacists in all practice settings to recognize the toxicological manifestations of unintentional or intentional misuse of drugs, to assess the potential severity of an exposure and to understand the principles involved in the management of a poisoned patient. This course will provide the student with an overview of the clinical manifestations, assessment tools and treatment of common drugs, chemicals and biologic agents.

title: Clustering
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Clustering is the most basic unsupervised learning task: Organize a collection of objects into groups so that objects in the same group are similar. But almost every word in the sentence above has different specific meanings, leading to different ways to thinking about clusterings. What is similar? What is a group? What are the objects being grouped? And what does it even mean to organize them? In this course, we will develop a conceptual understanding of the problems of clustering such as: What's the best clustering formulation for a given problem? What kinds of clusters might I expect (or will I end up with) if I use a particular formulation? What kinds of formal guarantees can we provide on the behavior of a particular algorithm for a clustering formulation? How do we extract meaning from the results? And given that clustering is usually unsupervised, how do we know that we have a good answer?

description: This course provides in-depth coverage of the Cognitive-Behavioral model of therapy practice. Students will learn how to use cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) to address a wide array of client issues. The empirical bases of the theory and model will be examined, as well as applications to direct social work practice. Students will learn to utilize the cognitive model to inform treatment planning, case conceptualization and develop CBT skills and interventions. Several therapeutic techniques are explored, including identification of cognitive distortions, automatic thoughts, intermediate and core beliefs, development of behavioral activation plans for depression, anxiety and other mental health concerns, cognitive reframing, imaginal rehearsal for skill development, exposure, and relaxation therapy for treatment of anxiety and phobias. By the end of the course, students will have attained an advanced level of proficiency in CBT and will be able to apply cognitive-behavioral techniques in their work with clients.

title: Cognitive Development Across the Lifespan
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Graduate students should register for PSYCH 6220 and they will be held to a higher standard or do additional work. Survey of theories and research on cognitive development (e.g., Piaget, neo-Piagetian, information processing, contextual). Theories related to cognitive development in childhood, adolescence, adulthood and late life.

title: Cognitive Neuroscience
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: In this survey course, the goal is to explore the overlapping fields of cognitive neuroscience, neuropsychology, and cognitive psychology. To this end, course topics will include an overview of the nervous system and cognitive neuroscience research methods, as well as extensive discussion of the neural bases of mental functions and behaviors such as hemispheric specialization, object recognition, motor control, visual-spatial processing, attention, language, cognitive control, and memory.

title: Cognitive Psychology
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Introduction to an information-processing analysis of cognition. Perception, attention, and memory.

title: Cognitive Science
description: Cognitive science is an interdisciplinary field studying the human mind. Related fields include philosophy, psychology, computer science, neuroscience, and linguistics. This course introduces students to the basic issues in the field and the contributions made by each discipline, especially philosophy of mind. The course can be used as a capstone for the cognitive science minor.

title: Cognitive-Affective Bases of Behavior
description: Advanced course in the psychological theory of emotion and cognition. Students will develop a critical perspective on cognitive and affective bases of behavior, with a focus on classic theory and research on cognitive and emotion; debates about the definition of emotion and cognition; research methods in the study of cognition and emotion; and gender and cultural differences in the expression of emotion and cognition.

title: Cognitive-Communication Disorders
description: Nature, assessment, and remediation of a variety of cognitive-communication disorders including traumatic brain injury, right hemisphere brain damage, and dementia. Additional professional practice issues include issues of aging, cultural diversity, and the rationale and methods for providing family-focused treatment.

title: Collaborative Early Intervention for Infants and Toddlers with Developmental Delays
description: Students examine policy issues, curriculum content, teaming and service coordination strategies, and assessment and intervention techniques for providing family-centered early intervention for infants and toddlers with developmental delays. Prerequisites and corequisites apply only to early childhood special education certification students.

title: Collaborative Early Intervention for Infants and Toddlers with Developmental Delays
description: Students examine policy issues, curriculum content, teaming and service coordination strategies and assessment and intervention techniques for providing family-centered early intervention for infants and toddlers with developmental delays.

title: Collaborative Research Project
description: A three-hour course where students and faculty collaborate on a research project.  The purpose of the course is for students to learn the process of doing research.  The course may or may not result in authorship of a published article.

title: Collaborative Writing Studio
description: Collaborative Writing Studio is a one-credit, small-group collaborative that meets asynchronously each week. It is designed as a nurturing support forum for students who desire weekly writing feedback similar to that provided in the University Writing Center. The course is specifically intended for students concurrently enrolled in writing-intensive courses, as it provides a place for students to give and receive feedback on the writing they are doing in their other courses. WRTG 1000 can most easily be described as a structured peer collaboration on all aspects of the writing process, including discussion, drafting, and revision.

title: Collective Bargaining
college: LW - S.J. Quinney College of Law

title: College Algebra
description: Functions, inverses and graphs; polynomial, rational, radical, exponential and logarithmic functions; systems of equations and matrices; applications; arithmetic and geometric sequences and series.

title: College and Career Readiness for Professional Educators
description: This is an online course offered for in-service school counselors and other educational professionals. The course teaches the importance of college and career readiness for students today, and illustrates how to promote college and career readiness in a school setting. The course is presented through three modules. In module one, participants learn how to create a college-going culture for all students, including effective strategies for working with diverse populations. In the second module, participants learn the effective use of college, career, and academic planning. Module three teaches participants how to help students work through the college and financial aid application process. The course emphasizes the importance of using data-driven interventions and contains information and materials specific to the state of Utah.

title: College of Fine Arts Internship
description: The College of Fine Arts Internship Course is designed to help you connect your academic studies in the arts to practical application by offering academic credit focused on work experience. This internship experience will allow you to develop your professional and networking skills, attain hands-on experience, and evaluate career opportunities.

title: College of Social and Behavioral Sciences Internship Program
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: This course provides an opportunity for a student to gain first-hand experience working with a local agency that aligns with the student’s professional interests. Students may find an internship independently, or they may work with the CSBS Internship Coordinator to identify and apply for internships before enrolling in this course. Students create work goals with their supervisors, and both parties remain continually accountable for the completion of these goals through evaluations and student reflections. In addition to the valuable hands-on experience and academic credit received, some students may find that the internship facilitates professional networking that may lead to an employment opportunity.

title: College On-Ramp
description: This is designed to prepare students for post-secondary education, enable a smooth transition into college, and facilitate success once enrolled. Topics covered will include mindfulness, guide to college, and communication.

title: College Readiness Course Facilitator Training
description: This course trains facilitators to supervise the on-line module course ED PS 6260 College and Career Readiness for Educational Professionals.

title: College Student Development Theory
description: This course is designed to synthesize major theoretical concepts that explain how and why students develop during college. It reviews the most significant types of college experiences that research identifies as affecting change and development in students, and explores how and why particular experiences may impact students. Added emphasis is placed on exploring the extent to which the same type of college experience may affect different students differently. Students enrolled in 7620 will be held to a higher standard and may be assigned additional coursework.

title: College Student Retention Theory
description: In this course students develop an understanding of how college students make and implement persistence decisions, and how institutional structures, policies, and practices impact those decisions. Reading and discussing theory and research on college student retention, students consider who makes up the college-going population and the issues these constituents bring to campus, examine retention theory's history, and conduct a critical examination of various theories of retention. Readings and discussions focus on the role of leadership in creating environments that promote retention for the diverse student populations. Students enrolled in 7560 will be held to a higher standard and may be assigned additional coursework.

Readings and discussions focus on the role of leadership in creating environments that promote retention for the diverse student populations. title: College Students and Campus Environments
description: The purpose of this course is to understand the nature of campus environments and student populations. By exploring the influences of campus environments on students’ experiences related to inclusion, equity, involvement, and retention, students in this course will learn to enhance campus environments to maximize student learning and development.

title: College Teaching
description: Survey of college teaching methods and development of specific teaching competencies appropriate to the needs, skills, problems and interests of college students.

title: College Teaching and Social Justice
description: This course explores what it means to teach about social justice in higher education, given that such courses typically have been preceded by years of mis-education and are primed for conflict. Although the course will make some recommendations, the focus will not be on best practices or solutions, but on exploring the issues from a number of angles. The course is designed to be of particular interest to teaching assistants and doctoral students who hope to gain experience teaching at the college level, but it is open to all master's and doctoral students.

description: While working with a mentor, the student will participate in one or more of the following activities: the development of teaching materials, grading of assignments, recording of scores, conduction of help sessions, preparation of select class sesstions.

title: College Teaching II
description: While working with a mentor, the student will take responsibility for using departmental lines to develop the course syllabus and related instructional materials and teach a section of a course.

description: Additional work required of graduate students. Listening and conversation in an Arabic dialect (Egyptian or Levantine). Survival skills and everyday conversational topics based on authentic listening materials.

title: Colloquial Arabic II
description: Additional work required of graduate students. Develops communicative skills in the Arabic dialect started in ARAB 6010 and improves cultural awareness of modern Arab society and way of life. Authentic reading and listening materials include plays, proverbs, poems.

title: Colloquium  on Slavery in the Atlantic World
description: This course explores the history of slavery in the United States, from the colonial era to the Civil War. Students will be exposed to key academic debates that have shaped the field of slavery-related history. While the course primarily focuses on the historiography of slavery in the colonial and early United States, we will also pay considerable attention to how slavery in America developed from, and compared to, slavery in its wider Atlantic World context.

title: Colloquium in 19th Century U.S. History
description: A graduate-level reading course in 19th Century United States History.

title: Colloquium in American History
description: A graduate-level reading course in American History. Topic Varies.
