title: Pathokinesiology
description: This course is designed to develop the foundational knowledge of human motion, including biomechanical concepts of movement and muscle/joint interplay in the production of motion. An overall goal of the course is to develop the student’s ability to utilize current evidence-based literature and foundational textbook knowledge in analyzing human movement.

title: Pathologic Principles for the Basic Scientist
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course will present a detailed study of normal microscopic anatomy of human tissues and organs. Alterations in tissue structure that occur in various human diseases will be discussed. This visual course will emphasize the morphologic differences between normal and abnormal tissues. Inflammatory, immunologic, infectious, neoplastic, and other disease states will be presented. Structure-function relationships will be discussed in detail. The course objective is to provide students in the basic sciences with an understanding of normal tissue morphology and the alterations that occur under various pathologic conditions. (offered for 1/2 semester every other year)

title: Pathology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Conceptual introduction to the basic mechanisms of disease and to an understanding of the components of disease processes. Studies include cell injury and necrosis, tissue injury, acute and chronic inflammation, specific responses to infectious agents, some immunologic aspects of disease processes, neoplasia, growth disorders, and circulatory disturbances.

title: Pathology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Systemic pathology taught in conjunction with the neuroscience and the organ system courses covering the pathologic basis of disease, along with applications of laboratory medicine, by organ system.

title: Pathology and Rehabilitation of Athletic Injuries
description: This course presents an overview of the etiology for head and neck, upper and lower extremity, and trunk injuries.  Also included are the contemporary therapeutic exercise protocols for each of these injuries.

title: Pathology Away Rotation
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Away rotation in pathology specialty or sub-specialty. Away rotations can be arranged in other medical schools in the U.S. by special prior arrangement only.

title: Pathology Faculty Consultation
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Designed for students to periodically meet with their committee members during preparation of their final defense.

title: Pathology Journal Club
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Faculty and student forum for presentation of current scientific literature. This is a required course for Ph.D. students.

title: Pathology Research in Progress
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Faculty and student forum for presentation of current research. This is a required course for Ph.D. graduate students.

title: Pathophysiology
description: This course is designed to provoke in students a general understanding of physiological body responses to certain pathologies related to rehabilitation practice and to build the foundation for patient screening. Human pathophysiology is a crucial basic science to the practice of physical therapy.  Review of normal physiology and the study of related pathology are key to your comprehension and differentiation of potential health problems.  The concepts will be presented related to system function and how various systems respond to normal stresses, disease and injury.

title: Pathophysiology
description: Study of physiological changes resulting from disease or injury; disturbances of normal physiology resulting in functional changes of one or multiple organ systems leading to impairment.

title: Pathophysiology
description: Introduction to major pathophysiological mechanisms that cause disease or altered body functioning throughout the lifespan. Epidemiology and clinical manifestations integrated throughout.

title: Pathophysiology
description: Introduction to major pathophysiological mechanisms that cause disease or altered body functioning throughout the lifespan. Epidemiology and clinical manifestations integrated throughout.

title: Pathophysiology for EMS Providers
description: This course discusses human pathophysiology as a foundation for pre-hospital emergency medical care. We will explore the causes of common diseases found in humans through a concept-based approach of each body system including the relationship of each system in the disease process.

title: Pathophysiology II
description: Introduction to major physiological mechanisms that cause disease or altered body functioning across the lifespan with emphasis on multiple health problems. Epidemiology and clinical manifestations are integrated throughout.

title: Pathophysiology III
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Comprehensive study of the various body systems and common primary-care problems particular to the areas of: gastroenterology, ophthalmology, orthopedics, nephrology, dermatology, urology, cardiology, endocrinology, obstetrics/gynecology, neurology, and hematology/oncology.

title: Pathophysiology of Disease for Laboratory Medicine
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: The “Pathophysiology of Disease” course is a flipped course consisting of online assignments and in-class activities. This course builds a foundation for understanding mechanisms responsible for the development of common diseases and conditions including immune, genetic, blood, nervous and endocrine system disorders, as well as pathophysiological processes responsible for the development of infectious, liver, kidney, and lung diseases. This course is suitable for graduate students and postdoctoral fellows who want to learn more about normal structures and functions of organs and systems in the body, and the pathophysiologic mechanisms underlying common diseases. Online activities comprise of watching recorded lectures, studying textbook chapters and reading additional materials covering major topics of pathophysiology of the diseases. In-class activities include online material and case study discussions. This course is a preparatory course for PATH 6900 (Biochemical Techniques).

title: Pathophysiology, Pharmacology, and Health Assessment for Nurse Educators
description: This course focuses on pathophysiology, pharmacology, and health assessment in the context of health, wellness, and acute and chronic illness. Utilizing a concept-based approach, the course explores the assessment of patients and population groups impacted by acute and chronic disease with an analysis of advanced pathophysiology and pharmacology underlying these conditions. In addition to these clinical elements, the course integrates concepts related to care – including health and risk assessment, effective communication, and ethical considerations.

title: Pathophysiology, Pharmacology, and Physical Assessment for Nurse Educators
description: Required for nursing students in the Master of Science program with an emphasis on Nursing Education, students focus on advanced pathophysiology, pharmacology, and physical assessment in the context of health, wellness, and acute and chronic illness.

title: Pathophysiology, Pharmacology, Health Assessment of Acute Illness and Chronic Disease
description: This course is focused on developing Master's level nursing skills of health assessment, pharmacology, and pathophysiology related to clients experiencing select acute and chronic conditions and disease. Topics include assessment of clients and population groups with acute and chronic diseases. As well as the pharmacokinetics and actions of drugs commonly used for these population groups and the pathophysiology of selected acute and chronic diseases.

title: Pathophysiology, Pharmacology, Health Assessment of Health and Wellness
description: This course is focused on developing advanced Masters level nursing skills related to health assessment, pharmacology, and pathophysiology in support of health and wellness. Topics included are health and risk assessment, health promotion, genetics/genomics and issues surrounding drug interaction, polypharmacy and medication reconciliation.

title: Pathway in Pediatric Dentistry
description: The course will explore principles of pediatric dentistry through independent study, didactic seminars, and clinical observation at Primary Children's Hospital. Students will be expected to prepare and present assigned topics in a small group format.

title: Pathway in Pediatric Dentistry II
description: The course will explore principles of pediatric dentistry through independent study, didactic seminars, and clinical observation at Primary Children's Hospital. Students will be expected to prepare and present assigned topics in a small group format. Additionally, students will participate in a Pediatric Dentistry and Orthodontics course for the University of Utah General Practice Residency as directed by the Primary Children's Hospital Pediatric Dental Residency Program.

title: Pathway in Pediatric Dentistry III
description: The course will explore principles of pediatric dentistry through independent study, didactic seminars, and clinical observation at Primary Children's Hospital. Students will be expected to prepare and present assigned topics in a small group format. Additionally, students will participate in a Pediatric Dentistry and Orthodontics course for University of Utah General Practice Residency as directed by the Primary Children's Hospital Pediatric Dental Residency Program

title: Pathway in Pediatric Dentistry IV
description: The course will explore principles of pediatric dentistry through independent study, didactic seminars, and clinical observation at Primary Children's Hospital. Students will be expected to prepare and present assigned topics in a small group format.

title: Pathway in Pediatric Dentistry V
description: The course will explore principles of pediatric dentistry through independent study, didactic seminars, and clinical observation at Primary Children's Hospital. Students will be expected to prepare and present assigned topics in a small group format.

title: Pathway in Pediatric Dentistry VI
description: The course will explore principles of pediatric dentistry through independent study, didactic seminars, and clinical observation at Primary Children's Hospital. Students will be expected to prepare and present assigned topics in a small group format.

title: Pathway Seminar
description: This seminar will facilitate peer learning, further the development of skills in professional presentations and share students completed projects.

title: Pathways Development I
description: This course provides students the opportunity to lay the foundation of their Pathway with didactic instruction, focused engagement, and group discussion.

title: Pathways Engagement I
description: This course will provide student focused engagement experiences in selected dental areas. Students will select one area of interest. Engagement experiences include shadowing, experiential, group discussion, etc. Students will reflect on their experiences and write a reflection paper to be included in their portfolio.

title: Pathways Engagement II
description: This course will provide students focused engagement experiences in selected dental areas. Students will selected two areas of interest. Engagement experiences include shadowing, experiential, group discussion, etc. Students will reflect on their experiences and write a reflection paper to be included in their portfolio.

title: Pathways Exploration
description: The Pathways program in the School of Dentistry provides students the opportunity to explore the many facets of dentistry and options for careers in dentistry. This course introduces the Pathways program and allows students explore Pathway options that are available for in-depth study during the third and fourth year of their dental education. Each Pathways Course Director (PCD) will present to the students, discussing their area of expertise in dentistry. They may explore how and why they came to make the professional selection that they did and how they prepared for it. They will present to the students the elements of and expectations for the elective “Pathway” program that they direct. Students will reflect on each presentation and submit the reflection to the Pathways Program Director (PPD). The Pathways Program Director will meet with the students to further explore the program and student options. Students will reflect on the Pathways available and personal interest. A portfolio including all reflections papers will be submitted to the PPD as the final project for Pathways Exploration.

title: Pathways I
description: Instruction and exercises to assist students in their selection and implementation of professional pathways for their dental careers.

title: Pathways II
description: Continued instruction and exercises to assist students in their selection and implementation of professional pathways for their dental careers.

title: Pathways to Community Engagement
description: The Pathways to Community Engagement course will serve as a foundational introduction to the myriad opportunities individuals have to participate as active citizens. Students in this course will explore and examine the history and key tenets of community engagement, develop an understanding of civic competencies, and participate in community-engaged learning experiences.

title: Pathways to Periodontolgy IV
description: Periodontal and dental implant surgeries will be provided under the supervision of the periodontists in the Periodontics Section.

title: Pathways to Periodontology I
description: Selected readings will be reviewed that focus on etiology, pathogenesis, diagnosis, and treatment planning of periodontal surgical principles. Diagnosis and treatment planning for dental implant surgery will also be reviewed. This may also include viewing CE courses presented at professional meetings.

title: Pathways to Periodontology II
description: A review of surgical procedures will be provided. This will be accomplished by viewing recordings of CE presentations along with select YouTube videos.

title: Pathways to Periodontology III
description: Select readings for periodontal surgeries will be reviewed. Principles presented in the readings will be applied in laboratory settings.

title: Pathways to Periodontology V
description: In this course periodontal and dental implant surgeries will be provided under the supervision of the periodontist in the Periodontics Section.

title: Pathways to Periodontology VI
description: Discussions for the long-term management of periodontal and dental implants will be provided. A portfolio of procedures will be compiled and presented to the members of the Periodontics Section and other parties of interest.

title: Patient Assessment and Treatment Planning
description: Lectures designed to acquaint the preclinical student with the fundamentals of the interview, the principles and procedures of clinical examination, the methods of identifying oral diseases and the rational for oral therapy. Following the correlation of facts obtained, the formulation of a diagnosis and treatment plan is made. Includes a clinical section.

title: Patient Assessment and Treatment Planning II
description: Lectures designed to acquaint the pre-clinical student with the fundamentals of the interview, the principles and procedures of clinical examination, the methods of identifying oral diseases and the rational for oral therapy. Following the correlation of facts obtained, the formulation of a diagnosis and treatment plan is made. Includes a clinical section.

title: Patient Care Administration Practicum
description: Practicum to integrate patient care services administration concepts and theories through participation within a health-oriented organization, analyzing complex functioning of a multidisciplinary health team, evaluating personal behaviors/negotiations in health care organizations and impact, assessing system dynamics used to unity/integrate functional aspects, and integrating current research findings relative to the practice of patient care service administration. Repeatable for credit.

title: Patient Care I
description: This course is designed to introduce basic patient care concepts to the student including: Body mechanics, suctioning and support equipment, vital signs and medical emergencies. The concepts presented in class will provide students the information needed to be able to apply the skills directly to their clinical education so that they are able to provide quality patient care techniques.

title: Patient Care II
description: This course is designed to introduce advanced patient care concepts and techniques to the student for specific settings including: Fluoroscopic setting, drug administration/pharmacology, medical and surgical asepsis. The concepts presented in class will provide students the information needed to be able to apply the skills directly to their clinical education so that they are able to provide quality patient care techniques.

title: Patient Care in Nuclear Medicine
description: Patient care in nuclear medicine is a required nuclear medicine program course that provides the knowledge, learning experiences and skill assessment environment necessary for technologist to safely and effectively care for nuclear medicine patients.

title: Patient Communication
description: This course will focus on creating and demonstrating effective strategies for communicating effectively with patients of all ages in a clinical setting. This course will be case-based and will emphasize the delivery of patient-centered care to a diverse group of patients.

title: Patient Communication
description: This course will focus on creating and demonstrating effective strategies for communicating effectively with patients of all ages in a clinical setting. This course will be case-based and will emphasize the delivery of patient-centered care to a diverse group of patients.

title: Patient Education
description: This course teaches health educators to effectively provide and facilitate patient education and health promotion programs in clinical settings including hospital, clinic and home care. The expanding role of health educators in the health care system will be discussed, as well as various formats for patient education.

title: Patient Problem Management 1
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This seminar is the first in a series that utilizes community Physician Assistants to provide students with small group instruction to learn and apply physical exam techniques to patient cases.

title: Patient Problem Management 2
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This seminar is the second in a series that utilizes community physician assistants to provide students with small group instruction to work through case studies to practice critical thinking skills and practically apply their proficiency in medical interviewing and evidence-based practice. During this semester, students also begin putting these skills into practice with patients in a community clinic setting.

title: Patient Problem Management I
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: A problem-based learning format to introduce the concepts of: clinical decision making and evidence-based medicine, interdisciplinary team patient care, health care systems, and community-oriented primary care. Also explores professional issues including: medical ethics, medical-legal issues, health policy, and managed care.

title: Patient Problem Management II
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: A problem-based learning format to introduce the concepts of: clinical decision making and evidence-based medicine, interdisciplinary team patient care, health care systems, and community-oriented primary care. Also explores professional issues including: medical ethics, medical-legal issues, health policy, and managed care.

title: Patient Problem Management III
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: A problem-based learning format to introduce the concepts of: clinical decision making and evidence-based medicine, interdisciplinary team patient care, health care systems, and community-oriented primary care. Also explores professional issues including: medical ethics, medical-legal issues, health policy, and managed care.

title: Patient Safety
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: Quality improvement efforts in healthcare must always focus on patient safety. This course introduces students to the infrastructure that underlies successful improvement efforts, such as culture change, data systems, payment methods, and management roles.

title: Patient Safety & Quality
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Course topics include; Patient Safety and Quality Improvement: Developing a Systems View (Patient Safety I), Setting the Stage for Success An Eye on Safety Culture and Teamwork (Patient Safety II) Planning a Patient Safety or Quality Improvement Project (Patient Safety III), Designing for Sustainment: Keeping Improvement Work on Track (Patient Safety IV), Implementing a Patient Safety or Quality, Improvement Project (Patient Safety V), Measuring the Success of a Patient Safety or Quality Improvement Project (Patient Safety VI), and Taking Safety and Quality Improvement Work to the Next Level (Patient Safety VII).

title: Patient Safety and Handling
description: This course covers necessary theory and application required for physical therapists to create and maintain a safe environment while treating patients in outpatient and inpatient settings. Course topics will include safety topics such as patient education, and fitting of adaptive equipment as well as topics related to patient handling such as proper technique for assistance and patient comfort and modesty.

title: Patient-Centered Outcomes and Preference-Based Methods
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course will explore patient-centered and preference-based outcome measurement (PROs and PROMs) with a focus on how to develop, implement, analyze and interpret the data derived from these measures using health-economic and outcome research methods from several perspectives: societal, governmental, insurer, healthcare system, provider, and patient/individual. These skills are foundational in Population Health Sciences Research, an important addition to our program. Students should have the ability to code in a programming language (SAS, STATA, R, Python) and basic statistical knowledge is recommended.

title: Patient-Centered Pharmaceutical Care
description: Introduction to philosophy, knowledge and skills needed to successfully practice pharmaceutical care.

title: Patient-Centered Teaching
description: This course is focused on the implementation of patient-centered teaching regarding assessment, pathophysiology, and pharmacology knowledge from NURS 6724. The student identifies an individual or group with a knowledge deficit and provides education to fill that gap. The student also obtains and discusses feedback on their teaching intervention.

title: Patterns of Global Terrorism: Law, Policy and Supranational Institutions
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: The course examines the philosophical, policy, legal and tactical issues of the recent rise of terrorism and the international responses to the rise in terrorism.  Particular attention is placed on the global geography (and supranational) issues related to terrorism.  The first portion of the class will examine the causes of terrorism and the global patterns of terrorist activities.  The second portion of the class will focus on the current state of policy, legal and tactical responses to terrorism from both comparative and evaluative views.  The course activities will include lecture, group discussion, guest speakers, readings and critiques of reading for each section of the course.

title: Patterns of Traditional Chinese Culture
description: Focuses on the historical, literary, social, and political trends of traditional China. Both primary and secondary sources will be read and analyzed for their insights on the formation of Chinese culture. The class is taught in English, although the readings are in Chinese.

title: Pavement Design
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Meets with CVEEN 6570. Presents the concepts of mechanistic pavement design for flexible and rigid pavements. It introduces the students to the analysis of stresses and deflections in multi-layered pavement systems. Evaluates existing pavement design methods including Mechanistic Empirical Pavement Design Guide (MEPDG) and reviews factors that affect pavement performance.

title: Pavement Design
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Presents the concepts of mechanistic pavement design for flexible and rigid pavements. It introduces the students to the analysis of stresses and deflections in multi-layered pavement systems. Evaluates existing pavement design methods including Mechanistic Empirical Pavement Design Guide (MEPDG) and reviews factors that affect pavement performance.

title: Pavement Distress and Rehabilitation
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Meets with CVEEN 6550.  A study in the cause and effect of distresses that affect both flexible and rigid pavements, including potholes, cracks, ruts, joint faulting, etc.  Evaluation of the relationship between material selection, traffic loads, environment, and pavement performance.  Development of condition surveys and non-destructive testing as methods for selection rehabilitation techniques.  Introduction to pavement management systems.

title: Pavement Distress and Rehabilitation
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: A study in the cause and effect of distresses that affect both flexible and rigid pavements, including potholes, cracks, ruts, joint faulting, etc.  Evaluation of the relationship between material selection, traffic loads, environment, and pavement performance.  Development of condition surveys and non-destructive testing as methods for selecting rehabilitation techniques.  Introduction to pavement management systems.

title: Pavement Maintenance and Rehabilitation
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: A study in the cause and effect of distresses that affect both flexible and rigid pavements, including potholes, cracks, ruts, joint faulting, etc. Evaluation of the relationship between material selection, traffic loads, environment, and pavement performance. Development of condition surveys and non-destructive testing as methods for selection rehabilitation techniques. Analysis of currently used rehabilitation and maintenance techniques. Introduction to pavement management systems.

title: PCNP Practicum I
description: The first in a series of four clinical coursers, this course introduces the Primary Care Nurse Practitioner student to the role of the independent nurse practitioner. The student will apply evidence based didactic knowledge and clinical skills under the supervision of a faculty or clinical preceptor. The focus of the semester is on application of techniques of patient history taking, performing an appropriate physical assessment and beginning to identify differential diagnoses for the provision of primary health care in the outpatient setting.

title: PCNP Practicum II
description: The second in the series of four clinical course, this course provides additional opportunities for the Primary Care Nurse Practitioner student to increase expertise in application of evidence based didactic knowledge and clinical skills in the provision of primary health care. Emphasis is placed on refinement of techniques that assist in reaching a diagnosis, including obtaining a history, performing an appropriate physical exam and applying principles of differential diagnosis. Focus also includes beginning development of a plan of care in the management of interpretation of findings and laboratory results is expected.

title: PCNP Practicum III
description: The third in a series of clinical courses, this course supports the Primary Care Nurse Practitioner student's role as an independent practitioner. The student applies evidence based didactic knowledge and clinical skills in the supervised provision of health care. The student is continuing to refine differential diagnosis skill in the approach to episodic and chronic medical diagnoses. The student develops, implements and evaluates the plan of care under supervision of faculty/preceptors including management of chronic medical diagnoses Incorporation of health promotion concepts as well as interpretation of findings and laboratory results is expected.

title: PCNP Practicum IV
description: This is the final clinical course for the primary care nurse practitioner students. In this course the student works with a preceptor to demonstrate mastery of skills required to assess, diagnose and manage episodic and complex acute and chronic health problems. Evolution of knowledge and skills attained through previous practicum rotations and residency results in producing a capable, qualified primary care provider, who will transition into a safe novice independent nurse practitioner.

title: PCNP Practicum V
description: The fifth in a series of six clinical courses, this course providers additional opportunities for the Primary Care Nurse Practitioner student to increase expertise in the role of an independent practitioner in the provision of primary health care. Emphasis is placed on greater refinement of techniques that assist in reaching a diagnosis, including obtaining a history, performing an appropriate physical exam and applying principles of differential diagnosis in primary care or specialty clinics. There is a focus on a more independent role of the development, implementation, and evaluation the plan of care for patients in the management of episodic and chronic disease. Incorporation of health promotion concepts as well as interpretation of clinical findings and laboratory results is expected. The focus also includes a more independent role of the development and implementation of skills in leadership/policy/quality improvement.

title: PCNP Practicum VI Residency
description: This is the final of six clinical courses, it provides opportunities for the Primary Care Nurse Practitioner student to develop mastery of the application of evidence based didactic knowledge and clinical skills in the provision of primary health care. There is a focus on an independent role of the development, implementation, and evaluation the plan of care for patients in the management of complex episodic and chronic diseases with the support of the preceptor. The focus also includes an independent role of the development and implementation of skills in leadership/policy/quality improvement. Evolution of knowledge and skills attained through previous practicum rotations and residency results in producing a capable, qualified primary care provider, who will transition into a safe novice independent nurse practitioner and health care leader.

title: PE for Individuals with Disabilities
description: Offered to any University of Utah student, faculty member, or staff employee with a disability. Course content is determined by assessing the fitness level of the class members and designing a physical-education program to meet each member's individual needs. Individual goals are established in the areas of physical fitness, motor skills, aquatics, and/or individual and group games. However, the emphasis of the class is on improving the physical fitness levels of the class members. The primary activities in the class include weight training, jogging, biking on a tandem bike or stationary bike, armcrank ergometry work, swimming, and/or flexibility exercises.

title: Peace & Conflict Studies - Special Topics
description: Variable subject matter. Repeatable when topics vary.

title: Peace & Conflict Studies: Special Topics
description: Variable subject matter. Repeatable when topics vary.

title: Peace and Conflict in Asia
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: This course seeks to provide an overview of regional cooperation and competition among Northeast Asian states with a focus on Korea. As East Asian economies become increasingly integrated, the linkages between these societies are deepening and broadening. However, this region faces considerable challenges as well. Security issues are dominant, examples being North Korean nuclear weapons and territorial disputes around the Korean peninsula. Issues concerning nationalism and unresolved historical debates provide other key challenges. How can we understand these challenges and how do we evaluate the responses of South Korea and its neighbor states? This course will begin by outlining prominent theories of global politics, which will then become the tools we use to analyze the important issues and challenges facing East Asian countries and the U.S. We will select from a number of case studies in contemporary East Asia and investigate them from the perspective of Korea’s international relations. Students are expected to become familiar with historical and current affairs in the East Asian region and to exercise their understanding of basic theories of international relations for the analysis of events occurring there. The course will end with a discussion of identity and globalization and their relation to peace and trust in Asia.

title: Peace and Conflict Studies Capstone
description: This course will examine reconciliation after conflict at the individual and collective levels. This course will focus on the kinds of resolutions that are possible after serious conflict, and will consider the processes and factors (e.g., personal, legal, institutional, popular and scholarly discourse, religious and literacy/artistic aspects) that can enhance the chances for peaceful resolutions rather than a resurgence of violence. This course is an advanced seminar structured around readings, discussions, and interactive writing assignments.

title: Peace and Conflict Studies Capstone Course
description: This course will examine reconciliation after conflict at the individual and collective levels. This course will focus on the kinds of resolutions that are possible after serious conflict, and will consider the processes and factors (e.g., personal, legal, intuitional, popular and scholarly discourse, religious and literary/artistic aspects) that can enhance the chances for peaceful resolutions rather than a resurgence of violence. this course is an advanced seminar structured around readings, discussions, and interactive writing assignments.

title: Pedagogical Methods
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course will cover theoretical concepts for effective adult learning, skills for classroom management, active learning, syllabus preparation, and objective-based evaluation. Students will have the opportunity to develop class plans, develop and deliver and review recorded lectures, prepare and use evaluation tools, and receive feedback from peers and faculty.

title: Pedagogical Structure of English
description: An analysis of a broad range of English phonetic and grammatical structures and models for teaching this material in the ESL/EAS classroom.

title: Pedagogical Structure of English
description: An analysis of a broad range of English phonetic and grammatical structures and models for teaching this material in the ESL/EAS classroom.

title: Pedagogical Structure of English
description: Meets with LING 6233. An analysis of a broad range of English phonetic and grammatical structures and models for teaching this material in the ESL classroom.

title: Pedagogy Seminar
description: In depth study of skills and knowledge involved in being an effective teacher.  Student will be involved in CTLE workshops and one content courses in the department.

title: Pediatric Audiology
description: Principles of normal auditory development, auditory development in deaf and hard-of-hearing infants and children, assessment of hearing disorders in infants and children including study of causation of hearing loss. Principles for treatment of hearing loss in children, and choices of communication modality. Laboratory practice to apply principles provided.

title: Pediatric Away Rotation
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Away rotation in pediatrics specialty or sub-specialty. Away rotations can be arranged in other medical schools in the U.S. by special prior arrangement only.

title: Pediatric Bone Marrow Transplantation Clerkship
description: For a short time, the student will be a part of a health-care team comprised of professionals with a common goal of providing optimal care for the patient.  This clerkship will allow the student to become involved in caring for delicate patients in an immunocompromised setting.

title: Pediatric Cardiology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: The main objectives of the elective are: (1) accurate interpretation of physical findings in diagnosis of cardiac diseases in children; (2) knowledge of the clinical features of common cardiac conditions, especially those of the newborn (cyanotic newborn and neonatal congestive heart failure); and (3) accurate interpretation of electrocardiograms. Students will attend clinics and conferences, make ward rounds with attendings, assist with inpatient consultations, and read ECGs. Students will become familiar with cardiac ultrasonography (M-mode, 2D, and Doppler) as it applies to common anomalies. Students have the option to be called in for emergencies and assist in cardiac catheterization. This block may be offered as a 2 or 3 week rotation based on availability.

title: Pediatric Cardiology Camp - Camp Hawkins
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: As Camp "medical counselors," students will supervise congenital and acquired heart condition management and Camp activities for a group of 8-10 youth, including children with heart disease and their siblings, 4-18 years of age at Camp Hawkins, a Summer Camp for Children with Heart Disease, under the supervision of a "unit" physician and the Camp medical director (Dr. James Hoffman). Includes one week of pre-camp chart review, as well as one day pre=camp volunteer orientation in which the student will teach other non-medically trained volunteers about the signs and symptoms of dehydration and over-exertion. Scheduled times for Camp may be obtained from the Camp Hawkins website, www.camphawkins.org. Please download the application and submit to Dr. James Hoffman.

title: Pediatric Cardiothoracic Surgery Elective
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This elective is designed as an initial full-time exposure to pediatric cardiothoracic surgery. The elective is carried out at Primary Children's Hospital, and is designed to totally immerse the student in all activities of the pediatric cardiothoracic service, including the cardiac intensive care unit and the operating room. In addition, participation in the didactic sessions of Cardiology Sign-Out and Cath Conference is required. Grading is based on a student's proficiency in the different aspects of patient care and medical knowledge. These aspects include fund of knowledge, differential diagnosis generation, patient presentations, and professional demeanor. Evaluations will be completed informally throughout the 4 week rotation and formally at the conclusion of the rotation by the attending physicians with whom the student works.

title: Pediatric Clinical Research
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Research credit by students arrangement with individual faculty/instructor(s) and the Pediatric Research Education Office. Studies will vary each semester, but will usually be in one of the following pediatric specialties: emergency medicine, hematology/oncology, critical care, medical genetics, immunology & rheumatology, inpatient medicine, obstetrics/gynecology, or cardiology.

title: Pediatric Critical Care Clerkship
description: Advanced-specialty clinical clerkship. Drugs in the care of pediatric critical-care patients.

title: Pediatric Dentistry Principles and Techniques
description: Foundational elements of pediatric dentistry and orthodontics will be covered. The eruption of the primary dentition through exfoliation and eruption of the permanent dentition, as well as specific treatment options for the pediatric population will be outlined. Space maintenance and basic orthodontics will be reviewed to give perspective to the challenges of the growing mouth.

title: Pediatric Dentistry Principles and Techniques Lab
description: Foundational elements of Pediatric Dentistry will be covered. The eruption of the primary dentition through exfoliation and eruption of the permanent dentition, as well as specific treatment options for the pediatric population will be outlined. This course include simulation exercises.

title: Pediatric Dentistry Rotation
description: This 1 to 2 week clinical rotation is designed to give the senior dental student an overview in understanding problems in treating patients with serious medical and behavioral disorders.

title: Pediatric Development and Health Promotion
description: This is the first pediatric course in the PNP/FNP/NNP/AGNP curriculum that focuses on well-child care including pediatric development, health promotion, and physical exam findings specific to children and adolescents. Students are required to attend according to the course schedule and complete all activities and assignments. The course focuses on knowledge of a developmental approach to health promotion and disease prevention of pediatric population within the family context. This includes mastery of obtaining age appropriate health history, pediatric specific examination skills, and developmental surveillance with the goal of health promotion and anticipatory guidance.

title: Pediatric Emergency Department
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Students in Pediatric Emergency Medicine (PEM) will have the opportunity to evaluate multiple patients in a tertiary care Pediatric Emergency Department (ED) and Level 1 Pediatric Trauma Center. Students will evaluate pediatric patients with a variety of complaints (infectious problems, congenital disorders, traumatic injuries, etc.) and levels of medical acuity. Students will experience the busy nature of the ED setting an learn how to assess and manage patients efficiently and effectively. Finally, students will be exposed to different areas of the specialty of Pediatric Emergency Medicine including direct patient care, ED nursing and technician roles, patient triage and the academic endeavors and commitments of the PEM staff.

title: Pediatric Emergency Medicine Point-of-Care Ultrasound
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Hands-on ultrasound scanning of patients will require adequate understanding of anatomy as well as cardiac pathophysiology. The goal of the ultrasound elective is to train medical students to be proficient at recognizing normal anatomy and in using point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) for the E-FAST and basic cardiac exams in order to identify emergent conditions such as: hemothorax, pneumothorax, pericardial effusion, hemoperitoneum, impaired global ventricular function, cardiac tamponade, and collapse or dilated inferior vena cava. This elective is distinctive in that it will be focused on using point of care ultrasound on infants, children, and adolescents. These interactions with children and their families are unique and require a different approach to successfully obtain and interpret images. This 10 day (M-F) 2-week elective will provide the learner with online video learning as well as simulated and hands-on instruction in emergent ultrasound. Skills taught will include basic lung and cardiac ultrasound, E-FAST, and peripheral/central IV access with the goals of understanding how to identify hemothorax, pneumothorax, basic cardiac function, cardiac tamponade, IVC fluid status, and intraperitoneal fluid.

title: Pediatric Endocrinology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Clinical experience in pediatric endocrinology and diabetes clinic. Participation in special clinical research problems (e.g., study of thyroid disorders, diabetes, growth problems, adrenal and gonadal disorders in children, etc.). Introduction to endocrinology laboratory assessment and interpretation of clinical laboratory data.

title: Pediatric Environmental Health
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Focuses on perinatal and pediatric exposures to environmental hazards and the creation of healthy environments for children.

title: Pediatric Gastroenterology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Diagnosis and management of children (ambulatory and in-hospital) with intestinal, liver, and nutritional disorders. The student will have the opportunity to participate in the evaluation of patients from infancy through adolescence. The student will assume responsibilities for inpatient subspeciality consultation similar to a pediatric resident. There is no night or weekend call. Elective includes experience with a variety of gastrointestinal procedures and biopsies, and participation in weekly clinical and pathology conferences.

title: Pediatric Health Equity & Social Determinants of Health Navigation
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This undergraduate course explores the intersection of pediatric health, equity, and social determinants of health (SDOH), focusing on health disparities among children. While centered on pediatric health, the course also examines the impact of poverty, racial disparities, and structural factors that contribute to intergenerational economic challenges. Students will gain insight into how social, economic, and environmental factors influence children's health outcomes and well-being into adulthood. The course aims to equip students with the skills to critically analyze these determinants and advocate for health equity among children and adolescents. The course consists of two components: a weekly class lecture and 3 hours/week screening patients and families for social needs and connecting them to community resources at Primary Children’s Hospital.

title: Pediatric Hem/Onc Sub-Internship
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: A sub-internship on the Hematology/Oncology ward (Lahey) at PCMC. Student is assigned patients as a ward intern and is fully responsible for their care and evaluation, under the direct supervision of the resident, fellow and attending physician. The student will participate in all teaching and service responsibilities including night call every 4th night as well as opportunities for certain procedures such as lumbar puncture, bone marrow aspiration and biopsy. Opportunities for exposure to outpatient Hematology/Oncology might be available.

title: Pediatric Hematology-Oncology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: (1) Basic principles of pediatric hematology/oncology for the generalist; (2) clinical microscopy of blood and bone marrow; (3) skills in procedures such as lumbar punctures, bone marrow aspirations and starting I.V.s; and (4) comprehensive team management. This elective includes a large volume of inpatient and outpatient material, hands-on practical experience, and one-to-one teaching. A lecture series in pediatric hematology/oncology is included. Research opportunities within the Division of Pediatric Hematology/Oncology are also available.

title: Pediatric Infectious Disease
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Major emphasis is on seeing infectious disease problems and consultations on pediatric patients. Extensive reprint files and library textbooks available. Experience in the clinical bacteriology and virology laboratory and travel medicine.  Opportunity to participate in research projects. Structure is rounding and consulting on hospitalized pediatric patients and some outpatient clinics.

title: Pediatric Intensive Care
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Acceptable to fill sub-internship requirement.  Designed for senior students who are interested in the care of critically ill children outside of the neonatal age range.  While it is largely intended for students who are pursuing a future career in pediatrics, other students may be interested in the course materials. The student will function as a sub-intern, admitting and caring for children admitted to the pediatric ICU at Primary Children's Medical Center, performing history and physical examinations, writing daily notes, and presenting patients on attending rounds. On-call responsibilities will be every fourth night, in-house call is mandatory. The student will be permitted to do technical procedures within the limits of their abilities and the exigencies of patient care. The educational emphasis is on the pathophysiology of critical illness in children, especially the recognition and therapy of acute respiratory failure and cardiovascular collapse. There also will be considerable exposure to pediatric trauma.

title: Pediatric IV/Wound Care Team
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: A one-week course working with the IV/Wound Care teams at Primary Children's Medical Center. Students will spend time working with both teams to gain experience in wound care, ostomy care, and intravenous access on the pediatric population in hospital setting.

title: Pediatric Level I Practicum
description: The Pediatric Level I Practicum experience is designed to build on the OT process I coursework and adds observation and participation with an occupational therapist in practice. Documentation will be a continued topic in this practicum. Clinical reasoning skills will be developed through fieldwork assignments and guided experiences in a clinical setting. This practicum also builds on professional skills, attitudes, and behaviors.

title: Pediatric Medicine Clerkship
description: Clinical clerkship with emphasis on diseases seen, and use and limitations of therapeutic agents employed in pediatric medical practice.

title: Pediatric Nephrology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Diagnosis and management of children and adolescents with renal, fluid, electrolyte, and hypertensive disorders. The student will see inpatients and perform consultations at University Hospital as well as Primary Children's Medical Center. Students will also evaluate patients in the Pediatric Renal Clinic. The student will be introduced to dialysis and transplantation.

title: Pediatric Neurology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Diagnosis and management of children with neurologic disorders, including X-ray procedures, electrical and chemical studies.

title: Pediatric Neurology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Diagnosis and management of children with neurologic disorders, including X-ray procedures, electrical and chemical studies.

title: Pediatric Neurology Elective
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This four-week clinical rotation provides the opportunity for the student to become familiar with the techniques required for evaluation of the pediatric patient with neurological disease. Students are assigned to the child neurology unit at Primary Childrens Medical Center. Activities include direct patient care, daily ward rounds, procedures, and participation in clinical conferences, brain-cutting sessions, and the child neurology outpatient clinics under the supervision of the child neurology staff. Fulfills Neurology requirement.

title: Pediatric Neurology Sub-Internship
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: The sub-internship in pediatric neurology is a 4 week rotation that prepares 4th year medical students to be successful first year residents on an inpatient pediatric neurology service. Clinical responsibilities will build on those acquired during the third year neurology clerkship, focusing on increasing levels of independence and responsibility. The student will develop his/her communication skills through daily interactions with patients, families, and health care team members. The sub-internship will foster lifelong learning skills through self-directed study and feedback.

title: Pediatric Nurse Practitioner Practicum I
description: Students work with a preceptor in a primary health care setting to develop skills required to assess and manage common episodic health problems. Clinical conferences include discussions of the nurse practitioner role within the context of state and national health issues, as well as case analyses.

title: Pediatric Nurse Practitioner Practicum I
description: Required for pediatric nurse practitioner emphasis students to develop clinical skills in assessment, diagnostic reasoning, medical decision making, creating management plans, and evaluating treatment responses of pediatric in various settings. This course is the first of a three-course series and requires  completion of 120 direct clinical patient care hours supervised by an experienced preceptor.

title: Pediatric Nurse Practitioner Practicum II
description: Students work with a preceptor to develop skills required to assess and manage common acute and chronic health problems. Clinical conferences include discussions of the nurse practitioner role within the context of state and national health care issues, as well as case analyses.

title: Pediatric Nurse Practitioner Practicum II
description: Required for pediatric nurse practitioner emphasis students to continue development of clinical skills in assessment, diagnostic reasoning, medical decision making, creating management plans, and evaluating treatment responses of pediatric patients in various settings. This course is the second of a three-course series and requires completion of 240 direct clinical patient care hours supervised by an experienced preceptor.

title: Pediatric Nurse Practitioner Practicum Immersion
description: Required for pediatric nurse practitioner emphasis students to demonstrate proficient clinical skills in assessment, diagnostic reasoning, medical decision making, creating management plans, and evaluating treatment responses of pediatric patients in various care settings. This course is the last of a three-course series and requires completion of 420 direct clinical patient care hours supervised by an experienced preceptor.

title: Pediatric Nurse Practitioner Residency
description: Clinical experience providing health care to clients and families in a variety of settings. Residency experience provides an opportunity to assume responsibility for health care services of individuals and their families under supervision of an established nurse practitioner and/or physician preceptor. Students are expected to practice as a nurse practitioner assuming increasing responsibility for planning and implementing therapeutic processes and for documenting and evaluating outcomes of care.

title: Pediatric Nursing
description: This course focuses on nursing care of children and their families with an emphasis on physiological, psychological, developmental, social, and cultural adaptations.  Nursing management strategies address health concerns/problems or needs of children and their families from a culturally diverse perspective.

title: Pediatric Nursing Clinical
description: This family-centered clinical course focuses on nursing interventions associated with physiological, psychological, developmental, social, and cultural adaptations of individuals and families.  Students apply nursing theory in adapting assessment skills and the nursing process to the car of children and their families in acute care settings.

title: Pediatric Nursing: Clinical
description: Students apply nursing theory in adapting assessment skills and the nursing process to the care of children and their families in acute and chronic care settings. Transition course taught fall semester 1998 only.

title: Pediatric Nursing: Theory
description: Nursing care of children and adolescents; responses to illness and effects of holistic nursing care. Physiological, psychological, developmental, social, and cultural adaptations of children and families during acute and chronic illness. Transition course taught fall semester 1998 only.

title: Pediatric Pathology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: The pediatric Pathology Course provides an opportunity to understand the diagnostic and consultative role of pediatric pathologists, learn basic principles of pediatric pathology, participate in conferences, and participate in a research project by special arrangement.

title: Pediatric Perfusion
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course covers cardiac congenital defects, the surgical procedures used to correct each defect, and an overview of pediatric perfusion. Components of the pediatric perfusion circuit, device selection, CPB management, cannulation techniques, temperature management, deep hypothermic circulatory arrest, and cerebral protection techniques will also be covered.

title: Pediatric Pharmacotherapy
description: An elective course designed to build baseline knowledge of the safe and effective use of medication therapy in pediatric patients. This course will highlight the pathophysiology and pharmacotherapeutics pertaining to common pediatric disease states.

title: Pediatric Radiology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Students with interests in all areas of medicine are encouraged to request the customizable elective. This is a self-driven course that will include exposure to pediatric plain film, fluroscopy, ultrasound, neuroradiology, body CT, and nuclear medicine. The student is expected to personalize this elective rotation to maximize learning related to their personal specialty interests. The rotation will take place at the Primary Children's Hospital (PCH).

title: Pediatric Rehabilitation
description: Concepts and principles in the evaluation and treatment of children with a variety of impairments. Includes normal and abnormal development, and various treatment and management approaches. Students register for one lab section only.

title: Pediatric Research
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: An elective which will permit interested students to concentrate a period of time on a pediatric research project. The project may consist of laboratory investigation, clinical research, review of literature or review of clinical case material. The students will, with help of their adviser: (1) review and evaluate literature which is relevant to the problem; (2) design a specific research protocol to investigate the problem; (3) learn techniques necessary to perform the experimental procedures; (4) carry out the experimental protocol; (5) critically analyze results, and draw the appropriate conclusions; and (6) present the results of the completed research project both orally and in written form.

title: Pediatric Scenarios
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course is designed for second-year students. Through a combination of case-based lectures and virtual interactive simulations, students will enhance their ability and build confidence to assist the surgeon in the pediatric operating room.

title: Pediatric Speech-Language Pathology
description: Surveys a broad range of pediatric speech and language delays/disorders in terms of associated characteristics, assessment techniques and treatment considerations.

title: Pediatrics
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course focuses on the pediatric population with an emphasis on stages of development, anticipatory guidance, and medical conditions specific to this population.

title: Pediatrics
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Introduction to the physiology of and diseases seen in newborns, infants, children, and adolescents.

title: Pediatrics Ambulatory Care Curriculum for EPAC Cohort Students
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: The pediatrics online ambulatory care course is an online curriculum for primary care that allows students to study primary care topics in an easily accessible, interactive and learner-centered format. The curriculum covers essential topics in outpatient pediatric primary care. For each topic, it includes pre-test, post-test and case-based didactic sections in an interactive format. Pre- and post-test responses are tracked to provide evidence of successful learning. Case-based didactic sections include cases and questions with thorough discussions of critical topics. The curriculum is designed to allow individual learners to track and document their own progress.

title: Pediatrics Clerkship
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: The Pediatrics Clerkship is a 4-6 week immersive clinical course in which students gain important team-based experience and knowledge in caring for patients with medical problems core to the pediatrics specialty. Clinical experiences are complemented by a discussion-based didactic (and simulation curriculum).

title: Pediatrics Clerkship
description: This elective clerkship will further enhance the knowledge and skills of students in the management of pharmacotherapy in the pediatric population, promote the clinical pharmacist's role on the health care team and provide direct patient care to the pediatric patient population.  This clerkship will take place within a pediatric acute care unit.  Students will participate on daily medical rounds with other members of the medical team to provide evidence based pharmaceutical care to the patients on the unit(s).  Students may also be required to give presentations to staff and patients, complete a project, or present cases.

title: Pediatrics Clinical Pharmacology Research in Progress
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course focuses on clinical research studies in pediatrics and clinical pharmacology. Students will be introduced to research projects. Sessions will include presentations on study design and progress from faculty members and fellows in various specialties. Students will be required to present progress in their research projects and critique the peer-reviewed articles during the semester.

title: Pediatrics Infectious Diseases Clerkship
description: Advanced-specialty clinical clerkship. Drugs in the care of infectious-disease patients.

title: Pediatrics Leadership Experience
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course is for student leaders who will assist with classroom & clinical instruction and management under the supervision of a course instructor. Responsibilities will depend on the leadership role, but may include holding review sessions, training students in the clinical environment, facilitating discussions in online courses, leading team meetings, public relations and recruitment, and piloting new clinical research studies in the Emergency Department at Primary Children's Hospital (PCH).

title: Pediatrics LIC - Family Medicine
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: A Longitudinal Integrated Clerkship is a model of clinical education in which students participate in the comprehensive care of patients over time, engage in continuity of relationships with preceptors, patients, health system & the surrounding community, while meeting core clinical competencies across multiple disciplines simultaneously. The specialties included in this introductory clinical experience include Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Neurology, Obstetrics and Gynecology, Pediatrics, Psychiatry, and Surgery. Settings for clinical experiences will be predominately outpatient with intermittent inpatient immersions. The Pediatrics Longitudinal Integrated Clerkship will provide experiences with patients of all ages; however, the focus when possible will be on the pediatric-aged patient.

title: Pediatrics LIC - Internal Medicine
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
