title: Poverty Law
college: LW - S.J. Quinney College of Law
description: This course provides an overview of the legal issues surrounding poverty. Topics typically covered include access to justice, housing and homelessness, education, employment issues of low-wage workers, income support, and welfare reform.

title: Poverty, Policy, and Economics
description: This course will present facts and theories for assessing and understanding the impact of poverty upon the formulation and implementation of policies at the state and federal levels. Implications of economic trends, especially upon the poor and other disenfranchised groups will be discussed. Special emphasis will be placed upon issues of racism, sexism, and discrimination.

title: Powder Metallurgy
description: Powder preparation, rapid-solidification processing principles, powder characterization, theory of compaction, sintering, full-density processing, powder metallurgy component design, compact characterization, application of powder metallurgy processing to structural, electrical, magnetic, and biomedical components.

title: Powder Metallurgy
description: Powder preparation, rapid-solidification processing principles, powder characterization, theory of compaction, sintering, full-density processing, powder metallurgy component design, compact characterization, application of powder metallurgy processing to structural, electrical, magnetic, and biomedical components. The laboratory sessions are a integral part of the course. Participation by students is mandatory. The credit hour for the laboratory portion is 1.0. Laboratory schedule and location will be determined during the semester.

title: Power & Politics: Political Sociology
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: The modern state touches nearly every aspect of our lives, but we usually spend little time thinking about it. The existence of states seems natural, as does their authority to collect taxes, raise armies, wage wars, regulate economies, build infrastructures, and provide services. This course analyzes how states acquired these powers over time. Topics include the emergence, development, and possible decline of modern states; war; democracy and its spread around the world; nationalism; globalization; citizenship; and human rights. The overarching goal of this course is for students to develop a better understanding of the state, society, and power in the modern world, with a focus on how history shapes current events.

title: Power and Politics Within Organizations
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: Organizations are fundamentally political entities and in them, power and influence are key mechanisms by which things get done. Moreover, effective leadership involves developing and wielding influence among others. In this course, such processes will be diagnosed and analyzed focusing on the sources, dynamics, and effects of power and political struggles in organizations. Course objectives include: developing the ability to create and use sources of power beyond formal authority, identifying common strategies and tactics of influence, and exercising skills that make each student more effective in complex, changing organizations. Course materials and activities focus on topics such as: the management of strategic dependencies and social/political capital; ethics; culture and unobtrusive control; commitment; and persuasion processes; and network building.

title: Power Basics
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: Power Basics is an extensive review of the capacity we call power. It examines power in many interdisciplinary areas including business, politics, philosophy, psychology, sociology, and theology. Throughout the course, emphasis is placed on the use and abuse of power in organizational and personal areas of everyday life. Students will become acquainted with some of the most critical thoughts, stratagems, and techniques employed in a selection of power contexts. Ample consideration will be given to the intersection of power and ethics.

title: Power Electronics Fundamentals
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: This course will introduce the power electronics basis and its applications. Students will learn about dc-dc converters dc-ac inverters, solid state power devices, and applications of power electronics in renewable energy area. In present days, power electronics is an extremely demanding field especially for the development of plug-in hybrid vehicles and renewable energy harvesting. Therefore, this course should be considered as a gateway to many other courses in power engineering.

title: Power in U.S. Government: Unchecked and Unbalanced?
description: A woman asked Ben Franklin as he left the Constitutional Convention what form of government the U.S. would have.  He replied, "A republic, if you can keep it."  This course will examine the transformations of the U.S. constitutional republic and what can be done to "keep" it.  Included will be an examination of core ethical issues and examples of past remedies that may serve as models for the present. Utilizing a wide variety of court cases, articles, books, video clips, and films, issues core to U.S. governance and relations with other nations will be explored, including the power to make war; the engagement in wars of aggression; the role of the judiciary in restraining executive branch conduct; military commissions; the history of Congress's responses to executive branch abuses; impeachment; surveillance of U.S. residents; deprivations of the writ of habeas corpus; torture; treaty obligations; assassination of U.S. citizens; drone killings; presidential emergency powers; continuity-of-government plans; the PATRIOT Act; domestic policing by military troops; and indefinite imprisonment of people, including U.S. citizens, without charges, trial, legal assistance, or a hearing before an independent tribunal.

title: Power System Economics
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: This course introduces the market structure of electric power systems, and the market agents including system operator, generating companies, and customers. The course describes the basic market concepts from micro-economics and then continues with introducing the tools and models for electricity market operation, including economic dispatch, optimal power flow, and unit commitment.

title: Power System Economics
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: This course introduces the market structure of electric power systems, and the market agents including of system system operator, generating companies, and customers. The course describes the basic market concepts from micro-economics and then continues with introducing the tools and models for electricity market operation, including economic dispatch, optimal power flow, and unit commitment.

title: Power System Protection
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: This course takes in the study of the largest machine ever built: the integrated power grid. You will be introduced to the broad range of theory and methods related to power system protection. In the process, you will: (1) Understand the nature of symmetrical and asymmetrical faults on power systems and the computational tools to evaluate them. (2) Identify and describe the equipment involved in electric power system protection. (3) Identify the techniques and technologies utilized for the detection, location, and isolation of electrical faults. (4) Explain the types of analytical studies that are performed in the context of system protection.

title: Power System Security Analysis
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.

This course starts with introducing the concepts and definitions of reliability and security in power systems. The course then introduces deterministic and stochastic models that the system operators utilize to ensure the security of power system operation against random failure and uncertainties.

college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: This course will introduce the basics of Electric Power System and its components. Students will learn about power generation, transmissions, and distribution, transmission line modeling, load-flow analysis and balanced and unbalanced fault analysis in power systems. This course should be considered as a starting point to understand the concept of Smart Grid and other branches of modern power systems.

title: Power Yoga
description: This course will incorporate various intense Yoga exercises in rapid successive sequencing to provide the student with a cardiovascular and strength enhancing workout.

title: PR Agency: Absolute Communication
description: This course is the student-run advertising and public relations agency that provides public relations, social media, advertising, and strategic planning services for real-world clients. title: Practical Applications of Clinical Genetics
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course will focus on the practical application of critical information that is presented in the Clinical Genetics Across the Lifespan course. Students will participate in class discussions, case review, presentations, and other activities to support critical thinking and application of clinical genetics concepts. Genetic counseling skills will also be emphasized throughout the course. Pre-recorded lectures may be included in this course, as well invited speakers or families, to give more depth of knowledge regarding the lived experiences of individuals with genetic conditions.

title: Practical Aspects of Intravenous Drug Delivery
description: Course will teach professional pharmacy students technical and physiologic issues that are important to understand and consider when administering drugs by intravenous infusion.

title: Practical Data Science
description: This class provides an introduction to data science and how it fits into an organization, and answers some key questions. What is a data scientist? How do you become one? What does a day as a data scientist look like? How does data analytics in industry compare to academia? It is expected that students are already familiar with common statistical procedures such as t-tests and linear regression and have a basic experience with R. This course will focus on the skills needed for practical data science.

description: The course includes an introduction to the fundamentals of image processing with topics such as basic 2D image processing, 3D image processing, quantitative analysis of images, and practical applications. title: Practical Experience I
description: This course provides health and wellness coaching students with hands-on experience in diverse health settings. Over the semester, students will engage in shadowing and practicing health coaching in clinical, corporate, and community environments. This practical experience is designed to enhance students' coaching skills, professional development, and understanding of various health and wellness contexts.

title: Practical Experience II

Over the semester, students will engage in shadowing and practicing health coaching in clinical, corporate, and community environments. This practical experience is designed to enhance students' coaching skills, professional development, and understanding of various health and wellness contexts.

title: Practical Experience III
description: KINES 6913 is the third course in a series, designed to facilitate the progress of students in the Health Education Specialist and Wellness Coaching MS non-thesis degree program within the Health and Kinesiology Program. The series, including 6911, 6912, 6913, and 6914, is taken during the 5 semesters of the program to prepare students to qualify to sit for the Certified Health Education Specialist (CHES®) and National Board Certified Health and Wellness Coach (NBC-HWC) certifications. All courses in the series will contain three similar areas of emphasis: 1) practical experience in clinical and community settings, 2) skill acquisition based on the core competencies outlined by the CHES and NBC-HWC certifications, and 3) health & wellness content in preparation to work with a variety of populations.

title: Practical Experience IV
description: KINES 6914 is the final course in a series, designed to facilitate the progress of students in the Health Education Specialist and Wellness Coaching MS non-thesis degree program within the Health and Kinesiology Program. title: Practical Industrial Process Engineering (PIPE)
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Technical elective targeted towards chemical engineering juniors and seniors. Covers topics valued in industry and relevant for process or design engineers, such as computer aided design, piping systems, industrial power, process instrumentation, distributed control systems, plus software and tools commonly used in industry. Classes include lectures, hands-on training and presentations by invited speakers.

title: Practical Management Science
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: Meets with OIS 6610. Managerial decisions - regardless of their functional orientation - increasingly leverage quantitative models from the discipline of management science. This course takes a managerial approach to management science by using Microsoft Excel to setup, solve and analyze problems in a wide array of fields such as finance, marketing, operations, information systems, etc. The tools covered may include linear and integer models, critical- path method/project management, risk, insurance, decision trees and simulation.

title: Practical Management Strategies in Healthcare
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: This course is a cohort course for students in the MHA program. It is intended to add to students' understanding of healthcare administration by engaging students in critical thinking about issues facing healthcare administrators. The course begins with an overview of the historical development of medicine and the hospital industry. It then focuses on practical management strategies for working with healthcare professionals, including span of control, hospital governance, leadership and emotional intelligence, dealing with licensure and disciplinary issues, and implementing and sustaining team care. Emphasis is on delivering high quality healthcare efficiently. The course is team taught and practicing healthcare administrators are included as visiting faculty.

title: Practical Skills for Health Care Leaders
description: This course is offered in workshop format with rotating topics. Potential topics include facilitating meetings, negotiation skills, marketing, advocacy, team building, and conducting root cause and failure mode analyses relevant to medication safety initiatives.

title: Practical Statistics
description: Statistical methods and concepts will be introduced with a special focus on basic topics applied in clinical research. A pragmatic approach will be used to familiarize the student with the uses (and misuses) of statistics discussed in scientific journal articles, prepare the student for material covered in more depth in future courses, such as Evidence-Based Practice and Epidemiology and Population Science, but also ensure that the statistics encountered in daily life are understood.

title: Practical Statistics for HPE Scholarship
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course focuses on how to interpret and apply common statistical analyses in education scholarship. The emphasis is on both understanding how statistical analyses relate to study design and how they are used to draw conclusions from the data collected. Students may find this course useful in drafting an analysis plan for their capstone scholarly project.

title: Practice and Critic of Design Build
description: Practice and critic of the design build process both in theory and in practice as experienced during the course of the Design Build Studio at Bluff.

title: Practice I:  Role of Social Workers in Health Settings
description: This 3-credit practice course builds on generalist year HBSE content and explores the person in environment from a bio-psycho-social perspective across the life span as one encounters challenges to one's physical health. Knowledge of specific major health/illness issues such as diabetes, cancer, disability, and pain management are presented from acute, chronic, and terminal condition perspectives. The accompanying psycho-social impact of these conditions on individual and family systems is discussed within a framework of cultural and ethnic diversity. The realities of SW practice in interdisciplinary health care settings (hospital, rehab, long-term care, home health/hospice and community-based care) are explored, as well as the impact of public health policy (Medicare, Medicaid, managed care) on social work practice and the role of prevention in health care. Social work values and ethics (e.g., confidentiality, self-determination, locus of responsibility) and their application to practice in health settings are addressed.

title: Practice I: Assessment, Engagement, Intervention, and Evaluation
description: Students will acquire basic skills, knowledge, and values in social work practice assessment, engagement, intervention, and evaluation.

title: Practice I: Lecture
description: Students who take this required MSW lecture class will study basic skills, knowledge, and values in social work practice assessment, engagement, intervention, and evaluation. All MSW students will receive this content in a large lecture format. Weekly topics taught in their lecture class will be taught simultaneously in their concurrent Practice I: Application class.

title: Practice II
description: In the first half of this required class, students will learn major theoretical approaches that inform today's social work practice. In the last weeks, students will learn the major approaches to social work practice with groups and families. Opportunities for discussion, viewing of real-client sessions through on-way mirrors, instruction through instructor modeling, and application role plays will be offered.

title: Practice II
description: Students continue to develop basic skills, knowledge, and values in social work assessment, engagement, intervention, and evaluation.

title: Practice II
description: Students will learn to apply theories of the planned changed process (assessment, intervention, evaluation) to groups, couples and families across the life span, as a result of course emphasis on praxis. Students are introduced to the process of building and nurturing relationships with groups, couples and families. Central to the course is an emphasis on self-awareness and consciousness. The exploration of the intersections of personal and professional ethics and values is stressed in this course. Issues of diversity are introduced both as a practice competency and a practice value and tenets.

title: Practice III: Lecture
description: In the first half of this required lecture-format class, students will learn major theoretical approaches that inform today's social work practice. In the last weeks, students will learn the major approaches to social work practice with groups and families. All students will attend this class in one large-room section.

title: Practice Leadership Capstone
description: In this course we will cover different dental ownership structures, including single practice, multi-practice, and start-up practice ownerships. We will conduct interviews with leaders in each of the structures.

title: Practice Leadership I
description: In this course, we will cover self-discovery, strengths, and weaknesses and creating a self-investment plan. We will learn about the various leadership styles, the advantages and disadvantages of each, and which style you gravitate towards.

title: Practice Leadership II
description: In this course, we will cover emotional intelligence and its value in leadership. We will also learn various communication styles and strategies appertaining to managing teams.

title: Practice Leadership III
description: In this course, we will study and develop business plans, including, executive statements, patient acquisition plans, patient retention plans, cash flow plans, systemization plans, and exit strategies.

title: Practice Leadership IV
description: In this course we will cover financial statements and valuation methods. We will select an office and conduct a practice valuation for the office.

title: Practice Leadership V
description: In this course we will cover team motivation and accountability. We will perform several morning huddles, executive alignment, and team training meetings.

title: Practice Lecture/Application II
description: In the first half of this required lecture-format class, students will learn major theoretical approaches that inform today's social work practice. In the last weeks, students will learn the major approaches to social work practice with groups and families. Each weeks, students will learn how to apply the theories and approaches. Opportunities for discussion, viewing of real-client sessions through one-way mirrors, instruction through instructor modeling, and application role plays will be offered.

title: Practice Management I
description: This course is designed to build a foundation for successful personal practice management.

title: Practice Management II
description: Financial planning in continued management of student loans and personal finance. Designed to build a foundation for successful personal practice management.

title: Practice Management II
description: In this course, selected guest speakers will provide instruction on choice of business entity, practice valuations, dental demographics, contracts, evaluating insurance plans, and evaluating various practice models.

title: Practice Management III
description: This course will cover information related to practice management including understanding contracts, practice metrics, financial statement analysis, demographic selection, overhead calculations, QBS, insurances, business entity types, risk management and case model review of failed practice.

title: Practice Management III
description: In this course, selected guest speakers will provide instruction on choice of business entity, practice valuations, dental demographics, contracts, evaluating insurance plans, and evaluating various practice models.

title: Practice Management IV
description: This course will cover information related to practice management including understanding contracts, practice metrics, financial statement analysis, demographic selection, overhead calculations, QBS, insurances, business entity types, risk management and case model review of failed practice.

title: Practice of Public Management
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Emphasizes the contexts in which public managers manage; how managers of the public good get things done in practice. Contexts include both intra- and inter-organizational systems and settings. Getting things done through influence (without formal authority) and inter-organizational networks are addressed as well as, for example, management skills and/or management survival skills within public bureaucracies. The course addresses aspects of management policy, but not issues of public policy analysis or formation.

title: Practice Research I
description: This grounds students in the critique of practice theory underlying social work assessments and interventions at the direct practice level. Students will undertake critical literature reviews involving theoretical and empirical foundations with respect to all elements of client-system diversity. In addition, students will define critical practice research issues that emerged from the literature review.

title: Practice Research I: Micro Practice
description: This grounds students in the critique of practice theory underlying social work assessments and interventions at the direct practice level.  Students will undertake critical literature reviews involving theoretical and empirical foundations with respect to all elements of client/system diversity.  In addition, students will define critical practice research issues that emerged from the literature review.

title: Practice Research II
description: This course promotes a critique of the theoretical and empirical literature regarding mezzo and macro level interventions. Students apply advanced evaluative research designs to the critique and development of promising new research-based intervention strategies.

title: Practice Research II: Mezzo and Macro Practice
description: This course promotes a critique of the theoretical and empirical literature regarding mezzo and macro level interventions.  Students apply advanced evaluative research designs to the critique and development of promising new research based intervention strategies.

title: Practice Scholarship in 21st Century Social Work
description: This course examines the emerging knowledge, skills, and values of new century social work practice.  The course will explore traditional and emerging theories and trends in the interrelated areas of social work practice, supervision, and scholarship.  Students will consider new century social work in the context of globalization and global survival threats; changes in patterns of human immigration, diversity, and urbanization; demands for accountability and evidence-based practice in the helping professions; and emerging scholarship in such fields as evolutionary biology and neuropsychiatry.  This course is a social work elective.

title: Practice Theory I
description: Understanding theories for assessment and intervention.

title: Practice-based Research Networks
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course is designed as a 1 credit hour weekly seminar. This course will address the design and infrastructure of different types of practice-based research networks, successful application for participation, protocol design and development, IRB submissions, recruitment strategies, data collection, cost containment, and other aspects that impact the success for failure of these networks.

title: Practice: Family and Child
description: Direct and indirect practice course designed to support the family and child integrative emphasis.

title: Practice: Social Work in Organizations and Communities
description: History and theories of community and organizational development.  Planned developmental change efforts (assessments, intervention, evaluation) with diverse populations as the macro levels of neighborhoods, communities, and organizations within a social justice framework.  Ethics, knowledge, values, and skills.

title: Practices in Community Engaged Learning
description: This course will use discussions, readings, lectures, and community engagement to study how place and race are leveraged in environmental justice efforts. Complementing our methodological considerations of community engagement perspectives, processes, and outcomes, students will conduct semester-length research projects to critically interrogate local intersections of place- and race-based efforts for environmental justice.

title: Practicum
description: LING 5813 focuses on the development of English as a second, foreign, and additional language teaching skills, particularly skills for lesson planning and delivery for different levels of language proficiency and different contexts. To this end, the course is designed to give pre-service teachers opportunities to do the following: (1) identify indicators of effective second language (L2) instruction, (2) develop skills in observing L2 classes, (3) select and develop or adapt instructional activities appropriate for different levels of language proficiency and contexts, (4) develop skills in planning lessons for L2 learners, (5) practice teaching skills using a variety of instructional strategies, (6) incorporate constructive criticism into lesson planning and micro-teaching demonstrations.

title: Practicum
description: LING 6813 focuses on the development of second and foreign language teaching skills, particularly skills for lesson planning and delivery for different levels of language proficiency and different contexts. To this end, the course is designed to give preservice teachers opportunities to do the following: (1) identify indicators of effective language instruction, (2) develop skills in observing second language (L2) classes, (3) select and/or develop instructional activities appropriate for different levels of language proficiency and contexts, (4) develop skills in planning lessons for L2 learners, (5) practice teaching skills using a variety of instructional strategies, (6) incorporate constructive criticism into lesson planning and micro-teaching demonstrations. The course has either a 30-hour field experience requirement for LING 5813 or a 45-hour field experience requirement for LING 6813. LING 6813 also requires that students develop a professional e-portfolio.

title: Practicum for Secondary Mathematics Teachers
description: This is a practicum course that will parallel MATH 4090.  One purpose of this course is to help students develop an awareness of meaningful ways to teach geometry and algebra to students in the 7th through 12th grades.  Another purpose of this course is to help students become reflective teachers who can look critically at textbooks, teaching materials, assessments and their own teaching for the purpose of better meeting the needs of students.  This course will have a strong student teaching component.

title: Practicum I (PNP, ANP, GNP, FNP)
description: Students work with a preceptor in a primary health care setting to develop skills required to assess and manage common episodic health problems. Clinical conferences include discussions of the nurse practitioner role within the context of state and national health issues, as well as case analyses.

title: Practicum I: Supervised Field Work with Learners who are Deafblind
description: The intent of the practicum experience is to provide students with in-depth field experience with children and youth who are deafblind. Students will apply knowledge and skills learned in the required deafblind specialization courses as they conduct functional vision and hearing assessments, a child-guided assessment to determine child strengths and needs, and work with parents to plan for their child's future.

title: Practicum II (PNP, ANP, GNP, FNP)
description: Students work with a preceptor to develop skills required to assess and manage common acute and chronic health problems. Clinical conferences include discussions of the nurse practitioner role within the context of state and national health care issues, as well as case analyses.

title: Practicum III
description: This is the third of six clinical courses in which students work with a preceptor in an acute health care setting. Students will continue to practice their skills in assessment, diagnoses, including differential diagnoses and medical decision making, laboratory and other diagnostic studies interpretations, development of a comprehensive plan of care, implementation and evaluation of prescribed treatments. The focus of this semester will continue to be surgical, cardiac, pulmonary and other medical disciplines in the acute and critical care environment. The Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner (AGACNP) role within the context of local, state and national levels will also be reviewed.

title: Practicum III A
description: Application of advanced roles, models and theories of social work to agency practice; using the generalist perspective.

title: Practicum III B
description: Application of advanced roles, models and theories of social work to agency practice; using the generalist perspective.

title: Practicum in Applied Educational Psychology
description: Student participates in a supervised educational psychology experience in applied setting. On-site supervisor mentors student in real-world skills that round student's academic experience and may increase employability.

title: Practicum in Clinical Psychology: P
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Practicum experience in important areas of specialization in clinical psychology. Topics vary by year and instructor. Examples include health psychology, behavioral medicine, neuropsychological assessment, personality, personality disorders, object relations psychology, cognitive therapy, group therapy, sex therapy, family therapy, autism treatment.

title: Practicum in College/University Teaching
description: Supervised experience in teaching college and university courses.

title: Practicum in Counseling
description: Individual counseling practice under supervision in school, university, or other agency setting.

title: Practicum in Counseling Psychology
description: Individual counseling and psychotherapy practice at the University Counseling Center, including weekly individual and group supervision, professional development activities, and career counseling experiences.

title: Practicum in Counseling Supervision
description: Supervised experience in counseling/clinical supervision of beginning counselors.

title: Practicum in Dance Education
description: This course is designed for the advanced dance education student to facilitate individualized projects and/or investigation of special topics in dance education.  Course content is directed by the student's interest in relation to dance education theories.

title: Practicum in Effective Teaching -- Doctoral
description: This course will provide graduate students in PETE with the opportunity to model quality physical education teaching, supervise practicum students, and maintain sites of good practice for the PETE program.

title: Practicum in Effective Teaching -- Masters
description: This course will provide graduate level students with the opportunity to model quality physical education teaching, supervise practicum students, and maintain sites of good practice for the PETE program.

title: Practicum in Environmental Systems Sustainability
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Using actual clients and a systems thinking approach, multi-disciplinary student teams resolve real world problems in environmental sustainability. Student teams define system structures, feedback loops, counter-intuitive relationships and the unintended consequences of policy decisions. Students having completed "System Dynamics and Environmental Policy" get to apply their experience in systems modeling in support of team efforts in full-scale, practical problem solving. Possible topics include: urban growth, drinking water, energy resources, air/water quality and environmental justice.

title: Practicum in Environmental Systems Sustainability
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Meets with CVEEN 6661, GEO 6341, GEOG 6371, and POL S 6324. Using actual clients and a systems thinking approach, multi-disciplinary student teams resolve real world problems in environmental sustainability. Student teams define system structures, feedback loops, counter-intuitive relationships and the unintended consequences of policy decisions. Students having completed "System Dynamics and Environmental Policy" get to apply their experience in systems modeling in support of team efforts in full-scale, practical problem solving. Possible topics include: urban growth, drinking water, energy resources, air/water quality and environmental justice.  Meets with GEO 6341, CVEEN 6661, GEOGR 6371, POL S 6324.

title: Practicum in L2 Program Administration
description: Issues related to L2 program administration.  Observation of and practice in L2 administration.

title: Practicum in L2 Teacher Education
description: Issues related to supervision of L2 Teachers.  Observation of and teaching L2 teachers.

title: Practicum in Measurement, Analysis, or Design
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Supervised experience in measurement, analysis, or design. Typically computer intensive.

title: Practicum in Physiology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Taught alternate years. Required of majors; open to medical and graduate students.  A laboratory-oriented practicum emphasizing the practice of physiological technique as it pertains to specific research problems.  Course covers membrane models, ion selectivity, intracellular pH and calcium regulation. Recording surface potentials, ionic currents, nerve discharge and documentation of nervous activity with antibody markers are taught.  The second half of the practicum emphasizes assays involving antibodies including receptor binding, and radio immunoassays.  Microfluorometric analysis, confocal microscopy, in-vivo drug assay, and genetic markers in disease are given practical consideration.

title: Practicum in Research
description: Provides students with an opportunity to study a research question related to physical therapy. Focuses on a master's project consisting of a written paper and a verbal presentation and defense. The primary goal is to enable students to continue their professional education throughout their careers.

title: Practicum in Research
description: Supervised research under direction of a faculty member or an approved outside supervisor.

title: Practicum in School Counseling
description: Introduction to professional practice under supervision of a licensed school counselor in a public school setting.

title: Practicum IV
description: Applies advanced roles, models, and theories of social work to agency practice, utilizing the generalist perspective. Students gain skills in developing and integrating individualized, multimodal social work practice under the supervision of an approved clinical instructor. Students practice in a focused area of study and integrate this agency-based learning with research and advanced elective courses.

title: Practicum IV A
description: Application of advanced roles, models, and theories of social work to agency practice; using the generalist perspective.

title: Practicum-Project Development
description: Individual research and development of the non-thesis project, supervised by graduate faculty.

title: Practicum-Project Implementation
description: Individual field-based experience in completion of non-thesis project, supervised by graduate faculty.

title: Practicum: Study Abroad
description: Opportunity for University of Utah nursing students to learn about another country, its health care delivery system, health status of the people, and nursing.  Students will have classroom education and clinical experience as observers.  Experience will occur in a variety of settings depending on program objectives.

title: Pragmatics
description: This course examines how language senders and receivers use context to jointly construct meaning out of an utterance. Key aspects include determining which aspects of meaning are explicit (i.e., semantic) and which are implicit (i.e., pragmatic), investigating how context both constructs and is constructed by discourse, and exploring the role of intentions in conveying meaning. The main topics are the semantics/pragmatics boundary, implicature, reference, presupposition, speech acts, dynamic semantics, and information structure.

title: Pragmatics
description: This course examines how language senders and receivers use context to jointly construct meaning out of an utterance. Key aspects include determining which aspects of meaning are explicit (i.e., semantic) and which are implicit (i.e., pragmatic), investigating how context both constructs and is constructed by discourse, and exploring the role of intentions in conveying meaning. The main topics are the semantics/pragmatics boundary, implicature, reference, presupposition, speech acts, dynamic semantics, and information structure.

title: Pragmatism and Philosophy of John Dewey
description: Meets with ECS 6621.  Looks at John Dewey's philosophy in the context of American pragmatism.  Focuses on educational, political, cultural, and scientific issues.  Students enrolled in 7621 will be expected to meet a higher standard of performance and may be assigned additional work.

title: Pragmatism and the Philosophy of John Dewey
description: Meets with ECS 7621.  Looks at John Dewey's philosophy in the context of American pragmatism. Focuses on educational, political, cultural, and scientific issues.

description: Professional practice sequence for Design majors.

title: Praxis Design One - Spring
description: Professional practice sequence for Design majors.

title: Pre-Columbian Architecture
description: Survey of the arts, emphasizing architecture, of major North and South American Pre-Columbian civilizations.

title: Pre-Law Service Learning
description: Pre-Law Service Learning: a multi-year, pre-professional LEAP for third-year Pre-Law students.

title: Pre-modern China
description: Covers the political, social, economic, and cultural history of China from earliest times to the 15th century.

title: Pre-modern Japan
description: A survey of Japanese state and society from its early origins to the mid-19th century.

title: Pre-Nursing LEAP: Innovations in Patient Care
description: This course will be an innovation-cased, problem solving approach to explore current issues in the delivery of patient care, and investigate and ultimately propose solutions that create a better patient experience. The primary goal is to engage in the process of developing innovative ideas to initiate change in healthcare. Specific topics in the course will vary, however issues will be related to nursing practice and nurse-sensitive patient outcomes. Students will participate in project-based activities involving interdisciplinary thinking. this course is restricted to Pre-Nursing LEAP students.

title: Pre-Nursing NEAP: Explore Nursing
description: This course introduces concepts for professional nursing practice and the patient experience within the healthcare system. Emphasis is placed on exploring the nurse's role as an integral member of the healthcare team across multiple contexts and settings, developing professional identity, identifying nurse-sensitive patient outcomes, and understanding patients as individuals, and within the context of family, and community. This course is restrict to Pre-Nursing NEAP Students.

title: Pre-senior Thesis
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Contact undergraduate director for information. Students complete original research projects under supervision of a faculty member and prepare a written thesis.

title: Pre-Trial Practice
college: LW - S.J. Quinney College of Law
description: Prepares students to represent a client during the pretrial phase of a lawsuit. In this course you may prepare a pleading (complaint or answer); conduct "paper discovery" (i.e., prepare and respond to interrogatories, requests for admission, and requests for production of documents); conduct a witness interview and prepare a written interview summary; conduct a deposition and prepare a written deposition summary; prepare non-dispositive motions and memoranda (for or against jurisdiction, joinder, and interpleader); prepare and argue a dispositive motion (for or against summary judgment); and negotiate and document the settlement of a lawsuit. The course includes one large section class per week and one small section class per week . Counts toward the experiential education requirement.

title: Precalculus
description: Provides in-depth and accelerated review of college algebra and trigonometry to prepare for science-track calculus courses. Most topics from MATH 1050 and MATH 1060 are covered in this course.

title: Preceptorship
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Clinical experience in application and practice of surgery in the community hospital by participation with a clinical faculty member in private practice. Rotations available at most major hospitals in Salt Lake City, Provo, Ogden, and many outlying areas.

title: Preceptorship
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: The students will be assigned to practicing ob/gyn specialists to work with them in both inpatient and outpatient aspects of their practice.  Approval of a specific preceptorship arrangement is required prior to registration.

title: Preceptorship
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Meant to give students with basic clinical skills an opportunity to see patients in a clinical practice. The experience will be full time, and preceptors will be selected in consultation with the student. The student should contact the course coordinator several months before the anticipated preceptorship in order to set this up.

title: Preceptorship 1
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Following completion of their didactic educations, PA students complete three semester of intensive clinical training. This training utilizes a hybrid clinical model, placing a strong emphasis on extended primary care as well as shorter clerkships. Students are exposed to a variety of clinical settings and patient populations during their clinical year. The program is accountable for establishing student rotations; placements are arranged by clinical faculty will be assigned in a neutral and non-discriminatory fashion, without regard to a students' gender, age, race, sexual orientations, religious preference, or ethnicity. A reliable method of transportation is required during the clinical year, and students may be asked to commute to several sites throughout the year.

college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Experience in specialty clinics; majority of time may be arranged in one of the subspecialties. Involvement in all clinical conferences.

title: Preceptorship in Ophthalmology: Research
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: In-depth experience in newer facets of ophthalmic research. Student must discuss proposed project with one of the ophthalmology faculty, rotate through specialty clinics of that faculty member, and participate in all clinical conferences.

title: Preceptorship in Orthopaedics & Sports Medicine
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: A two-week elective, non-surgical rotation with an attending in the Department of Orthopedics.

title: Preceptorship in Urology
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Two weeks or more preceptorship with a practicing urologist. The student spends the entire two-week period with one of the clinical urologic faculty. This includes office practice, surgery, and attendance at urologic meetings.

title: Pregnancy Risk Line Clerkship
description: Clinical clerkship with emphasis on use and limitations of therapeutic agents used in maternal and infant care, and in obsetrics and gynecology.

title: Prehistoric Archaeology
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: Introduction to the two-million-year-old archaeological record of human prehistory.

title: Premodern Southeast Asia
description: This course is a survey of Southeast Asian History through the mid-1800s, covering the region's major political, social, and religious changes. Topics covered include: the enduring mythology of the Spice Islands, the interplay between Hinduism, Buddhism, Islam, and Christianity, and the rise of colonial powers across Southeast Asia.

title: Preparation for General Chemistry
description: This course is for students with little or no background in chemistry and is designed to prepare students for General Chemistry. Covers basic topics through lecture and online problems. Students need either to have taken MATH 1050, or be taking it, when taking this course.

title: Preparation for Global Health Service & Learning
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course is for graduate students. Course Goals: as a result of completing (1) Students will be able to plan and prepare for a safe and ethically-guided global service and learning experiences. (2) Students will be able to describe ethical conundrums and best practices for students and trainees. (3) Students will be able to discuss personal health, safety and security during global health electives and rotations. (4) Students will be able to demonstrate understanding of qualitative research in low-resource settings. (5) Students will be able to locate and identify contextually-appropriate resources (e.g., manuals, guidelines and other resources) for global health electives and rotations in low-resource settings. (6) Students will be able to summarize the importance of post-trip assessment, evaluation and reflection in completing a well-rounded global health elective or rotation.

(6) Students will be able to summarize the importance of post-trip assessment, evaluation and reflection in completing a well-rounded global health elective or rotation.

description: This half semester course provides a basic understanding of organic chemistry. Course stresses nomenclature of organic chemistry and the basic principles guiding the reactivity of organic molecules. Application of the principles of organic chemistry to biological systems is also provided. The course is designed for people who want a foundation in the discipline for either general information or as preparation for the two semester organic chemistry sequence (2310 and 2320). Students should complete an introductory chemistry class before taking this class.

college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci

title: Preparing Effective Research Proposals
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course will guide students through the process of formulating a research idea, developing Specific Aims and identifying appropriate methods. The course will also cover other important components of proposals for federal agencies and foundations such as descriptions of innovation and broader impacts. Budgeting research projects, approval processes, and the application process for NIH grants will also be covered. The final product will be a full proposal and associated materials needed for submission to NIH.

title: Preparing for Life After Graduation
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: A final year course to prepare students for post-graduation life and employment. Students learn how to integrate their academic identity into a professional identity through portfolio building, career pathways opportunities, and creation of a personal contribution statement. The course provides the structure and support for students to engage in the steps required to apply to graduate school or seek a job post-graduation.

title: Preparing for Your Ed.D. Capstone in Higher Education
description: This course is designed to provide guidance to students as they identify a problem of practice in higher education that will launch their Ed.D. Capstone process. It is designed as the final course in the curriculum before students enroll in ELP 7989 – Ed.D. Capstone Project. It will draw upon program curriculum, scholarly literature, and lived experiences of the student as key components for identifying the issue, opportunity, or challenge that centers the Capstone Project. The class setting offers space for understanding, discussion, and exploration as a design collaborative. Course topics include: understanding the problem of practice as a scholar-practitioner; capstone proposal development and presentations; collaboration, communication, and conflict with committee and key partners; identifying significant literature for the problem and developing the literature review; developing strategies that address solutions to the problem; moving from reading, synthesis, and analysis to writing; communicating your solutions; deliverables and defending the capstone; reflecting on the process; and general topics that impact progress in completing the Capstone. Through these topics, students will offer a deeper understanding of the Capstone process.

title: Preparing, Examining and Cross-Examining Witnesses
college: LW - S.J. Quinney College of Law
description: Opening statements and closing arguments are seen as the trial lawyer's stock in trade, but trials are won and lost on the witness stand.  This course will focus on the preparation, handling and presentation of the witness at trial.  The class will emphasize the importance of pre-trial preparation before both direct and cross-examination, and the execution of those skills.  We will also deal with witnesses who need specific preparation, handling, and presentation, such as experts, child victims of violent or sex-related crimes, witnesses who are mentally or emotionally disabled, and witnesses who must testify through the use of an interpreter.  The format of the class will be a lecture on the use and presentation of a particular classification of witness, a demonstration of a direct and/or cross-examination of that class of witness, and hands-on participation in the examinations of the witness by students.

title: Preperformance Vocal
description: Solo performance opportunities in a master class and jury format ready the freshman voice performance and choral music education major for private voice study. The academic portion of the class covers basic vocal anatomy, International Phonetic Alphabet and clarifies breath, phonation and resonance function.

title: Preservation Administration and Law
description: Preservation law, planning, and economics.

title: Preservation Research Methodology
description: Research methodology for historic preservation.

title: Preservation Theory and Practice
description: History of the theory and practice of the preservation movement in the United States. Course provides a survey of a range of preservation activities: history of preservation, stewardship of the built environment, design issues, period styles, preservation law, economics, preservation technology, community revitalization, and curatorial management.

title: Prestressed Concrete Design
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: The focus of this course is to learn the basic concepts, materials and design methods for prestressed concrete construction including pre-tensioned and post-tensioned elements. Determine prestress losses and carry out flexural, shear and torsional design of prestressed elements. Analyze and design indeterminate prestressed concrete structures. Design of a two-way prestresses slab and plate systems and post-tensioned flat-plate floor systems. There is no other course in the existing curriculum that offers an opportunity to our students to focus on pre-stressed and post-tensioning concepts.

title: Prethesis
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Only for students with major status and advanced juniors who will take ECE 4900 the following fall semester. Students do necessary library research, develop writing skills, discuss issues of professionalism, prepare and submit a senior-thesis proposal, and receive approval from faculty.

title: Preventing Chronic Pain
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Preventing Chronic Pain: A Human Systems Approach.

title: Prevention Approaches for Disordered Eating and Obesity
description: Online course to provide professional skills that will help upper division and graduate students to select, implement, and evaluate the effectiveness of current prevention approaches and intervention strategies for disordered eating and obesity.

title: Prevention in Schools: A Course for Educators
description: This course is a graduate level survey course in school-based prevention research.  The course covers epidemiology, etiology, design, intervention, and effectiveness of school-based prevention interventions, with special attention paid to dissemination issues.  The final section will introduce students to exemplary school-based programs.

title: Prevention Research
description: Designed to provide professional skills that will help students to select, implement, and evaluate the effectiveness of evidence-based health promotion and prevention interventions.

title: Preventive Cardiology at the Fitness Institute: LDS Hospital
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This elective offers students experience in the practice of preventive cardiology including cardiovascular risk assessment, resting and exercise ECG testing, cardiac rehabilitation, and the design of programs to modify cardiovascular risk and promote a state of optimal wellness. Students will be expected to follow patients in outpatient cardiac rehabilitation, participate in exercise ECG testing, and initiate a personal lifestyle improvement project during the month-long rotation. A tutorial in ECG interpretation will be also be offered.

title: Preventive Medicine: Policy and Implementation
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Historical and methodological aspects of clinical preventive services and screening guidelines.  Practical approaches for putting prevention into practice and some aspects of alternative preventive services will be discussed.

title: Pricing and Revenue Management
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: This course focuses on business pricing strategies and tactics from both theoretical and applied managerial perspectives. Substantial content of the course concentrates on how firms attempt to capture value, as well as profits, in the revenues that they earn. Additional focus will be placed on pricing dynamics and the reaction to and by competitors at the firm and product level. The materials used in the course are intended to provide a comprehensive exposure to making managerial pricing decisions. Students will be expected to understand theoretical pricing concepts and, more importantly, apply them to a variety of applied marketing scenarios. The course will cover pricing examples from a number of different industries.

title: Primary Care Community Engagement
description: This course is designed for Primary Care DNP students to foster citizenship through community engagement. In collaboration with the faculty member, students will develop and implement individualized goals, objectives and outcomes for a service experience within a community. This experience will provide the Doctor of Nursing Practice student the opportunity to engage in learning and service while immersing in a unique experience impacting the health of individuals or communities.

title: Primary Care Health Information Systems
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Content and organization of clinical records for primary care. Principles of database design for primary care including data definitions and data modeling. Man-machine interfaces including patient health summary, encounter forms, and GUI-based workstations.

title: Primary Care Providers in Post-Acute/Long-Term Care
description: This course will integrate advanced clinical practice skills with the care of the adult in a post-acute/long-term setting. Problems and issues of adults in these settings will be included in the didactic portion of the class. Students will be placed in post-acute/long-term settings so that they will be able to apply the didactic portion of the class in their placement setting. 3 Credits total (2 Didactic, 1 Clinical).

title: Primary Data Collection Methods
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course will cover primary data collection techniques relevant to epidemiological and public health research, including survey methodology, instrument design and testing, direct observation, key informant interviews and focus groups, qualitative methodology, and SEIR (susceptible-infectious-exposed-removed) models. Students will learn, through hands-on projects, how to develop primary data collection tools, as well as analysis and interpretation of associated data. The course builds on concepts and techniques presented in Epidemiology II (PBHLT 7300) and Biostatistics II (PBHLT 7100 or PHS 7000).

title: Primate Evolution
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: This course explores the origin and evolution of the Order Primate from its origin in the Paleocene up to the diversification of modern species. Topics addressed include evolutionary theory, phylogeny and systematics, functional morphology, the reconstruction of primate behavior, and the relationship between fossil and living primates.

title: Primate Evolution

title: Primates
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: A survey of the diversity of non-human primates within the framework of evolutionary ecology. This course also explores the ways that the study of other primates contributes to our understanding of human behavior and evolution.

title: Primates: Studying our Closest Relatives
college: SB - Coll of Soc & Behavioral Sci
description: There are over 500 species of living primates. this course provides an introduction to the biology and behavior of our closest living relatives. Students will learn about evolutionary theory and primate evolution classification, morphology, evolution, biogeography and distribution, socioecology, communication, and conservation.

title: Principle Based Leadership in Healthcare
college: BU - David Eccles Sch of Business
description: The concept for this course is to give students the opportunity to delve into some of the most vexing aspects of leadership. The objective of the course is to help students understand the importance of critical thinking, communication skills, and decision-making skills required of successful leaders in healthcare. Real-life management situations and leadership development skills shared by resident faculty will facilitate learning around prominent healthcare management topics. The course begins with problem solving and ends with healthcare reform and future trends. A set of sessions on transformational leadership: principles and practice, gives students a glimpse at some leadership challenges they may face in their careers. Positioned in the last year of the MHA program the course gives students an opportunity to start to transition from student to professional. This semester uses cases based on actual problems and issues and gives students the chance to explore possible solutions while still in the “safety” of the classroom. The goals of this course is to both add to students’ fund of knowledge about healthcare administration and to engage students in critical thinking about issues facing healthcare administrators. Students should be in the spring semester of their last year of the MHA program.

title: Principles and Applications in Molecular Diagnostics
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: Develop advanced understanding of scientific principles of molecular biology as applied to molecular diagnostic laboratory testing.  Understand the application of molecular diagnostics as a means to assess health and disease including test selection and correlation of laboratory data to pathologic states in areas of genetics, oncology and infectious disease.  Learn to assess the quality of performance of molecular testing, abnormal laboratory data, discrepant results and validity of test results.

title: Principles and Practice of Nanoscience and Technology
description: The course will cover the principles of material behavior and synthesis at the nanoscale, and its application to a wide range of industrial and biotechnology applications. A historical development and an overview of the nanotechnology is first provided followed by treatment of the basic physics of behavior at the nanoscale. This is followed by (i) synthesis of particle and structure at the nanoscale using vapor phase, physical vapor deposition, commination and electrochemical approaches for use in metallurgical, pharmaceutical, cosmetic, medical, electronic, ceramic, agricultural, and other applications, (ii) processing and mechanical behavior of nano-scale structures, (iii) electrochemical synthesis and characterization in nanostructures including micro-/nano-machining, (iv) magnetism at the nanoscale and principles and fabrication of nanoscale magnetic devices, (v) biochemical processing, and (vi) Nanoscale characterization using AFM, STM, MFM, TEM and other techniques.

title: Principles and Practice of Pharmacometrics
college: MD - S. F. E. School of Medicine
description: This course provides an extensive overview of topics in population pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamic models, Monte Carlo simulation, and best practices. Instruction combines didactic lectures with hands-on exercises using R, Monolix, SimCyp, and NONMEM.

title: Principles and Practice of Transmission Electron Microscopy
college: EN - J & M Price College of Eng.
description: Meets with MSE 6240, MET E 5240/6240.  The course will cover the basic principles of electron diffraction in materials and the operation of transmission electron microscope.  Hands on experience with preparation of samples of various materials and structures in a TEM will be provided in laboratory sessions to illustrate the principles and practice of various TEM techniques.  The course will consist of 2 lecture sessions and 1 laboratory session per week.

description: The course will provide a comprehensive understanding of the basics of x-ray diffraction, crystallography and the ability to use X-ray diffraction for structural analysis of powder, polycrystalline and single crystal metals, minerals and engineered materials.

title: Principles and Practices of Art Education: An Introduction to Art Education
description: The course introduces students to the practices and principles of art education. Students examine: the historical and philosophical foundations of art education; current issues in art education; theories of art education; the major pedagogical approaches to art education; and human development and the arts. The course provides students with an understanding of art education as an important stand-alone discipline as well as a discipline that can be integrated across the curriculum.

title: Principles and Practices of Integrative Health
description: The purpose of this course is to review the specific interventions, approaches and methods of evidenced based integrative health practice. Much of the course will explore the mission and evidences of the National Center of Complementary and Alternative Medicine whose mission is to define, through rigorous scientific investigation, the usefulness and safety of complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) interventions and their roles in improving health and health care. This class will explore the research that supports these integrative health practices also referred to as complementary healing interventions.

description: The course will cover the principles of material behavior and synthesis at the nanoscale, and its application to a wide range of industrial and biotechnology applications.
